questions.explanation_en: Each pilot who deviates from an ATC clearance in response to a TCAS II resolution advisory shall notify ATC of that deviation as soon as practicable and expeditiously return to the current ATC clearance when the traffic conflict is resolved. Answer (A) is incorrect. Since ATC is not responsible for IFR aircraft separation during a deviation, the pilot should notify ATC of the deviation and expeditiously return to the clearance in effect after the conflict is resolved. Answer (B) is incorrect. Since deviations from clearances should be kept to the minimum necessary to satisfy a TCAS advisory, the pilot should notify ATC of the deviation and expeditiously return to the clearance in effect after the conflict is resolved.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim

subunit.title: Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS)

questions.question: Each pilot who deviates from an ATC clearance in response to a TCAS II, resolution advisory (RA) is expected to

choices.text: maintain the course and altitude resulting from the deviation, as ATC has radar contact.
request ATC clearance for the deviation.
notify ATC of the deviation as soon as practicable.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. TCAS II RA에 따른 ATC clearance 이탈은 가능한 한 빨리 ATC에 통보하고, traffic conflict가 해소되면 신속히 현재 clearance로 복귀한다.
tags: Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS)
questions.explanation_en: Each pilot who deviates from an ATC clearance in response to a TCAS II resolution advisory (RA) shall notify ATC of that deviation as soon as practicable and expeditiously return to the current ATC clearance when the traffic conflict is resolved. Answer (A) is incorrect. Since ATC is not responsible for IFR aircraft separation during a deviation, the pilot should notify ATC of the deviation and expeditiously return to the clearance in effect after the conflict is resolved. Answer (B) is incorrect. ATC clearance for a deviation in response to a TCAS advisory is not required, although the pilot is expected to notify ATC of the deviation as soon as practicable.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim

subunit.title: Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS)

questions.question: With no traffic identified by TCAS when in 10 miles of visibility, you

choices.text: can rest assured that no other aircraft is near.
must continually scan for other traffic.
must scan only for hot air balloons and gliders.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. TCAS는 안전비행에 대한 조종사의 기본 권한과 책임을 대신하지 않는다. Transponder가 없거나 고장 난 항공기는 TCAS가 탐지하지 못할 수 있으므로 항상 외부 교통을 계속 감시해야 한다.
tags: Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS)
questions.explanation_en: TCAS does not alter or diminish the pilot’s basic authority and responsibility to ensure safe flight. Since TCAS does not respond to aircraft which are not transponder equipped or aircraft with a transponder failure, TCAS alone does not ensure safe separation in every case. Thus, due diligence is required, and pilots should always be scanning for traffic. Answer (A) is incorrect. TCAS alone does not ensure safe separation in every case. Answer (C) is incorrect. TCAS does not respond to aircraft which are not transponder equipped or those aircraft with a transponder failure. Pilots must continually scan for all kinds of other traffic including, but not limited to, hot air balloons and gliders.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: When should ADS-B equipment be operated on the ground while taxiing?

choices.text: Only when ATC specifically requests your ADS-B equipment be activated.
Any time when the airport is operating under IFR conditions.
All the time when on the airport surface.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. ADS-B는 고정밀 GPS 신호를 이용하므로 레이더가 취약한 산악지형에서도 작동할 수 있고, 저고도와 지상에서도 기능해 유도로·활주로 교통 감시에 활용할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: ADS-B uses highly accurate GPS signals. Because of this, ADS-B will work where radar often will not work, even in mountainous terrain. It can also function at low altitudes and on the ground, meaning it can be used to monitor traffic on the taxiways and runways. Answer (A) is incorrect. ADS-B is highly accurate. It can be used in mountainous terrain and at low altitudes, even on the ground. Having the system on will enable the controllers to monitor traffic on taxiways and runways. Answer (B) is incorrect. The ADS-B system should be left on while on the ground in all weather conditions. This will enable ATC to monitor traffic on taxiways and runways.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which reports are always required when on an IFR approach not in radar contact?

choices.text: Leaving FAF inbound or outer marker inbound and missed approach.
Leaving FAF inbound, leaving outer marker inbound or outbound, and missed approach.
Leaving FAF inbound, leaving outer marker inbound or outbound, procedure turn outbound and inbound, and visual contact with the runway.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Radar contact이 아닐 때 비정밀접근에서는 FAF를 inbound로 통과할 때, 정밀접근에서는 outer marker를 inbound로 통과할 때 보고해야 한다. Missed approach는 radar 여부와 관계없이 항상 보고한다.
questions.explanation_en: When not in radar contact, a pilot is required to report when leaving final approach fix (FAF) inbound on final approach (nonprecision approach) or when leaving the outer marker inbound on final approach (precision approach). At all times, a pilot will report a missed approach. Answer (B) is incorrect. A pilot is required to report leaving the outer marker inbound, not outbound, on final approach. Answer (C) is incorrect. A pilot is not required to report leaving the outer marker outbound, the execution of a procedure turn, and/or visual contact with the runway.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What action(s) should a pilot take if vectored across the final approach course during an IFR approach?

choices.text: Continue on the last heading issued until otherwise instructed.
Contact approach control, and advise that the flight is crossing the final approach course.
Turn onto final, and broadcast in the blind that the flight has proceeded on final.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Final approach course로 vector 중에는 항공기 간격·분리를 위해 ATC heading을 그대로 따라야 한다. ATC가 course를 가로질러 vector할 것이라고 말하지 않았는데 final course가 임박하면 approach control에 crossing을 알리고 확인해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: If a pilot is being vectored to the final approach course, these vectors are used for spacing and separating aircraft. Pilots must not deviate from the headings issued by approach control. Pilots will normally be informed when it is necessary to vector across the final approach course for spacing or other reasons. If approach course is imminent and the pilot has not been informed of crossing the final approach course, the pilot should contact approach control and advise that the flight is crossing the final approach course. Answer (A) is incorrect. The pilot should maintain last heading issued but should also advise approach control that the flight is crossing the final approach course. Answer (C) is incorrect. A pilot should broadcast in the blind that the flight has turned onto final when operating VFR at an uncontrolled airport.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: When cleared for an IFR approach to an uncontrolled airport with no FSS, what precaution should the pilot take after being advised to change to advisory frequency?

choices.text: Monitor ATC for traffic advisories as well as UNICOM.
Broadcast position and intentions on the Common Traffic Advisory Frequency and monitor the frequency.
Wait until visual contact is made with the airport and then broadcast position and intentions to land on UNICOM.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. FSS가 없는 비관제공항에 IFR 접근 중 ATC가 'Change to advisory frequency approved'라고 하면 CTAF에서 접근 종류와 FAF 또는 outer marker inbound 통과시각을 포함해 자신의 의도를 방송하고 다른 항공기의 위치보고를 계속 청취해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: When making an IFR approach to an uncontrolled airport with no FSS, after ATC advises, “Change to advisory frequency approved,” the pilot should broadcast his or her intentions, including the type of approach and the time at which (s)he arrives over the FAF or outer marker inbound. The pilot should monitor the CTAF for reports from other pilots and for continual updates to position reports. Answer (A) is incorrect. After ATC advises the pilot to change to advisory frequency, ATC will no longer be able to provide traffic advisories. Answer (C) is incorrect. A pilot should always broadcast intentions and continually update position reports on the CTAF, not wait until visual contact is made with the airport. Waiting is unsafe and can contribute to an accident.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: When is radar service terminated while vectored for an IFR approach at an uncontrolled airport?

choices.text: Only upon landing or advised to change to advisory frequency.
When aligned on the final approach course.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 비관제공항 IFR 접근을 위해 vector 중인 항공기의 radar service는 착륙 완료 또는 'change to advisory frequency' 통보 중 먼저 발생하는 시점에 종료된다.
questions.explanation_en: Radar service is terminated while the airplane is being vectored for an IFR approach at an uncontrolled airport when the landing is completed or when the pilot is advised to change to advisory frequency, whichever occurs first. Answer (B) is incorrect. When an airplane is established on the final approach course, radar separation will be maintained and the pilot will be expected to complete the approach utilizing the approach aid designated in the clearance (ILS, VOR, etc.). Answer (C) is incorrect. When an airplane is cleared for the approach, approach control will continue to maintain radar separation, and the pilot is expected to complete the approach utilizing the approach aid designated in the clearance (ILS, VOR, etc.).

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: While being vectored to the final approach course of an IFR approach, when may the pilot descend to published altitudes?

choices.text: Anytime the flight is on a published leg of an approach chart.
When the flight is within the 10-mile ring of a published approach.
Only when approach control clears the flight for the approach.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Final approach course로 vector 중 approach clearance를 받았다면 항공기가 공표된 route 또는 IAP segment에 established된 후부터 공표고도로 강하할 수 있다. 이후 각 segment에는 공표고도가 적용되며 ATC가 다른 고도를 주면 그 지시를 따른다.
questions.explanation_en: While being vectored to the final approach course and being cleared for the approach, a pilot may descend to published altitudes anytime the flight is established on a segment of a published route or IAP. After the airplane is so established, published altitudes apply to descent within each succeeding route or approach segment unless a different altitude is assigned by ATC. Answer (A) is incorrect. One must be cleared for the approach to be able to descend to published altitudes. Answer (B) is incorrect. When the flight is within the 10-mile ring of a published approach, a pilot will maintain the minimum altitude for IFR and maintain altitude issued by approach control until established on a published segment of the approach.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: If visual reference is lost while circling to land from an instrument approach, what action(s) should the pilot take?

choices.text: Make a climbing turn toward the landing runway until established on the missed approach course.
Turn toward the landing runway maintaining MDA, and if visual reference is not regained, perform missed approach.
Make a climbing turn toward the VOR, and request further instructions.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Circling 중 시각참조를 잃으면 해당 절차의 missed approach를 수행해야 한다. 공표 missed approach course에 진입하기 위해 먼저 활주로 쪽으로 상승선회한 뒤 해당 course에 established될 때까지 계속 선회한다.
questions.explanation_en: If visual reference is lost while circling to land from an instrument approach, the missed approach specified for that particular procedure must be followed. To become established on the prescribed missed approach course, the pilot should make an initial climbing turn toward the runway and continue the turn until established on the missed approach course. Answer (B) is incorrect. Once visual reference is lost while circling, a missed approach must be executed. While turning toward the runway, a climbing turn should be established (MDA should not be maintained). Answer (C) is incorrect. A pilot should make a climbing turn toward the runway, not VOR, to ensure obstacle clearance while becoming established on the missed approach course.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is the difference between a visual and a contact approach?

choices.text: A visual approach is an IFR authorization while a contact approach is a VFR authorization.
Both are the same but classified according to the party initiating the approach.
A visual approach may be initiated by ATC while a contact approach can only be initiated by the pilot.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Visual approach는 교통흐름 단축을 위해 ATC가 시작하지만 contact approach는 조종사가 요청해야 한다. 구름을 피하고 비행시정 1 SM 이상이며 그 상태로 목적공항까지 계속 갈 수 있다고 합리적으로 예상할 때 contact approach를 요청할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Visual approaches are initiated by ATC to reduce pilot/controller workload and expedite traffic by shortening flight paths to the airport. A contact approach must be initiated by the pilot. A pilot operating clear of clouds who has at least 1 SM flight visibility and can reasonably expect to continue to the destination airport in those conditions may request ATC authorization for a contact approach. Answer (A) is incorrect. Both a visual and a contact approach are initiated from an IFR flight plan. Answer (B) is incorrect. A visual approach is one in which the pilot has a preceding aircraft or the airport in sight and can maintain basic VFR weather minimums. A contact approach is used by a pilot in lieu of conducting a standard or special instrument approach to an airport.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: When may a pilot execute a missed approach during an ASR approach?

choices.text: Only when advised by the controller.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. ASR approach는 관제사가 azimuth(방위) 유도만 제공하는 radar approach이다. 활주로 연장선에 정렬하도록 heading을 제공하며, 조종사는 언제든 자신의 판단으로 missed approach를 수행할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: An ASR approach is one in which a controller provides azimuth guidance only. The pilot is furnished headings to fly to align the airplane with the extended line of the runway. A pilot may execute a missed approach during an ASR anytime at the pilot’s discretion. Answer (B) is incorrect. The controller will instruct the pilot to execute a missed approach at the MAP or anytime during the approach that the controller considers that safe guidance cannot be provided. Answer (C) is incorrect. A pilot can execute a missed approach anytime at the pilot’s discretion, not only when advised by the controller.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Except during an emergency, when can a pilot expect landing priority?

choices.text: When cleared for an IFR approach.
When piloting a large, heavy aircraft.
In turn, on a first-come, first-serve basis.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 특정 종류의 IFR approach clearance를 받았다고 해서 다른 교통보다 착륙 우선권이 생기는 것은 아니다. 관제탑은 비행계획 종류와 관계없이 원칙적으로 first-come, first-served로 착륙 순서를 정한다.
questions.explanation_en: A clearance for a specific type of approach to an airplane operating on an IFR flight plan does not mean that landing priority will be given over other traffic. Air traffic control towers handle all airplanes, regardless of the type of flight plan, on a first-come, first-served basis. A landing sequence will be issued to each airplane as soon as possible to enable the pilot to adjust his or her flight path properly. Answer (A) is incorrect. A clearance for an IFR approach does not mean landing priority will be given over other traffic. Answer (B) is incorrect. A large, heavy aircraft will be sequenced for landing on a first-come, first-served basis, with no special priority over other traffic.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: How should a pilot describe braking action?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Braking action 보고에는 nil, poor, medium, good 또는 이들의 조합처럼 쉽게 이해되는 표준 용어를 사용해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: Pilots should describe the quality of braking action by using the terms “nil,” “poor,” “medium,” and “good” or a combination of these terms. In describing braking action for a portion of a runway, pilots should use descriptive terms that are easily understood. Answer (A) is incorrect. To describe braking action, a pilot should use nil (not 00%), poor (not 50%), medium (not 75%), or good (not 100%). Answer (B) is incorrect. To describe braking action, a pilot should use the terms nil (not zero-zero), poor (not fifty-fifty), medium, or good (not normal).

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What action is expected of an aircraft upon landing at a controlled airport?

choices.text: Continue taxiing in the landing direction until advised by the tower to switch to ground control frequency.
Exit the runway at the nearest suitable taxiway and remain on tower frequency until instructed otherwise.
Exit the runway at the nearest suitable taxiway and switch to ground control upon crossing the taxiway holding lines.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 착륙 후 별도 지시가 없으면 착륙 방향으로 계속 taxi하여 가장 가까운 적절한 유도로로 지체 없이 이탈한다. Tower가 지시하기 전에는 tower 주파수에서 ground control 주파수로 임의 변경하지 않는다.
questions.explanation_en: After landing, unless otherwise instructed by the control tower, continue to taxi in the landing direction, proceed to the nearest suitable taxiway, and exit the runway without delay. A pilot who has just landed should not change from the tower frequency to the ground control frequency until directed to do so by the controller. Answer (A) is incorrect. Upon landing, the pilot should exit the runway at the nearest suitable taxiway to clear the runway for other traffic and then switch to ground control when directed. Answer (C) is incorrect. While the crossing of the taxiway hold lines indicates clearing of the active runway, a pilot should not switch to ground control until directed to do so by the controller. Switching without permission may be confusing to ATC.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Upon landing, you should exit the runway

choices.text: Without delay, but not onto another runway unless authorized by ATC.
At the first high-speed exit and hold short of the taxiway.
Without undue delay, but not directly onto the ramp.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 활주로는 가능한 첫 유도로 또는 ATC가 지정한 유도로로 지체 없이 이탈해야 한다. ATC 허가 없이 착륙활주로에서 다른 활주로로 나가거나, 관제공항에서 활주로 위에 정지·역주행해서는 안 된다.
questions.explanation_en: You should exit the runway without delay at the first available taxiway or on a taxiway as instructed by ATC. Pilots shall not exit the landing runway onto another runway unless authorized by ATC. At airports with an operating control tower, pilots should not stop or reverse course on the runway without first obtaining ATC approval. Answer (B) is incorrect. When exiting a runway, the aircraft must be completely past the runway hold short line. If holding short of the taxiway, the aircraft would not be clear of the runway environment. Answer (C) is incorrect. While pilots should exit the runway without any undue delay, ramp space is not near runways.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: When the approach procedure involves a procedure turn the maximum speed that should be observed from first overheading the course reversal IAF through the procedure turn is
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Procedure turn이 포함된 접근에서는 장애물 회피구역 안에 머물도록 course reversal IAF를 처음 통과한 때부터 procedure turn을 완료할 때까지 IAS 200 kt 이하를 유지해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: When the approach procedure involves a procedure turn, the pilot should observe a maximum speed of not greater than 200 kt. IAS, from first overheading the course reversal IAF through completing the procedure turn maneuver, to ensure containment within the obstruction clearance area. Answer (A) is incorrect. The maximum speed for the procedure turn maneuver is 200 kt. IAS, not 180 kt. IAS. Answers (B) are incorrect. Airspeed limitations are based on indicated airspeed (IAS), not true airspeed (TAS).

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: A minimum instrument altitude for en route operations off of published airways which provides obstruction clearance of 1,000 feet in nonmountainous terrain areas and 2,000 feet in designated mountainous areas within the United States is called
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. OROCA는 항로 밖 장애물 회피고도로, 미국 내 비산악지역에서는 장애물 위 1,000 ft, 지정 산악지역에서는 2,000 ft의 여유를 제공한다. 다만 지상 NAVAID 신호, ATC radar 또는 통신 커버리지는 보장하지 않는다.
questions.explanation_en: OROCA is an off-route altitude that provides obstruction clearance with a 1,000-ft. buffer in nonmountainous terrain areas and a 2,000-ft. buffer in designated mountainous areas within the U.S. This altitude may not provide signal coverage from ground-based navigation systems, ATC radar, or communications coverage. Answer (A) is incorrect. MOCAs represent the lowest published altitude in effect between radio fixes on VOR airways, off-airway routes, or route segments that meets obstacle clearance requirements for the entire route segment and ensures acceptable navigational signal coverage only within 25 statute (22 nautical) miles of a VOR. Answer (B) is incorrect. MSAs provide obstruction clearance of 1,000 ft., not 2,000 ft., in designated mountainous terrain.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: An off-route altitude which provides obstruction clearance of 1,000 feet in nonmountainous terrain areas and 2,000 feet in designated mountainous areas within the United States is called
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. OROCA는 off-route obstruction clearance altitude로, 비산악지역 1,000 ft와 지정 산악지역 2,000 ft의 장애물 여유를 제공하지만 항행시설·레이더·통신 커버리지는 보장하지 않는다.
questions.explanation_en: Off-route obstruction clearance altitude (OROCA) is an off-route altitude that provides obstruction clearance with a 1,000-ft. buffer in nonmountainous terrain areas and a 2,000-ft. buffer in designated mountainous areas within the U.S. This altitude may not provide signal coverage from ground-based navigation systems, ATC radar, or communications coverage. Answer (A) is incorrect. MVAs in designated mountainous areas may provide only a 1,000-ft., not a 2,000-ft., obstacle clearance when required for flying terminal routes or for vectoring for an instrument approach. Answer (C) is incorrect. MSAs provide obstruction clearance of 1,000 ft., not 2,000 ft., in designated mountainous terrain.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: Pilots should notify controllers on initial contact that they have received the ATIS broadcast by

choices.text: repeating the alphabetical code word appended to the broadcast.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. ATIS를 수신했다면 최초 ATC 교신 때 방송 끝에 붙는 알파벳 code word를 말해 수신 사실을 알려야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: Pilots should notify controllers on initial contact that they have received the ATIS broadcast by repeating the alphabetical code word appended to the broadcast. Answer (A) is incorrect. The use of the phrase “Have Numbers” means that the pilot received only the wind, runway, and altimeter information. It does not indicate receipt of the ATIS broadcast and should never be used for this purpose. Answer (B) is incorrect. “Have Weather” does not indicate receipt of the ATIS broadcast and should never be used for this purpose.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: An airport may not be qualified for alternate use if

choices.text: the airport has AWOS-3 weather reporting.
the airport is located next to a restricted or prohibited area.
the NAVAIDs used for the final approach are unmonitored.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 모든 공항을 alternate로 사용할 수 있는 것은 아니다. 최종접근에 사용하는 NAVAID가 감시되지 않는 경우 해당 공항은 alternate로 부적합할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Not all airports can be used as an alternate. An airport may not be qualified for alternate use if the NAVAIDs used for the final approach are unmonitored. Answer (A) is incorrect. An airport can qualify for alternate use if the airport has AWOS-3 weather reporting. An airport may not qualify for alternate use if the NAVAIDs used for the final approach are unmonitored. Answer (B) is incorrect. An airport can qualify for alternate use if the airport is located next to a restricted or prohibited area. An airport may not qualify for alternate use if the NAVAIDs used for final approach are unmonitored.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: Precipitation static problems caused by defective dischargers may include

choices.text: Complete loss of VHF communications, 30 degree compass errors, high-pitched audio squeals, and erratic instrument readings.
Complete loss of UHF communications, 50 degree compass errors, low-pitched audio squeals, and limited instrument readouts.
Little interference in VHF communications, 20 degree compass errors, medium-pitched audio squeals, and negligible instrument indication changes.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Precipitation static은 VHF 통신 완전 상실, 최대 약 30°의 자기나침반 오차 같은 심각한 문제부터 고음 잡음, 불규칙 계기지시, St. Elmo's fire까지 일으킬 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Precipitation static has the potential to create problems from the serious, such as the complete loss of very-high frequency (VHF) communications and erroneous magnetic compass readings of up to 30°, to the annoyance of high-pitched audio squealing, erratic instrument readings, and St. Elmo’s fire. Answer (B) is incorrect. Precipitation static can cause 30° compass errors, high-pitched audio squeals, and erratic instrument readings. Answer (C) is incorrect. Precipitation static can cause 30° compass errors, high-pitched audio squeals, and erratic instrument readings.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: Under the stabilized approach concept, what is the maximum acceptable descent rate during the final stages of an approach?

choices.text: 1,000' per minute for precision and 1,200' per minute for non-precision.
1,200' per minute above 1,000' AGL and 500' per minute below 1,000' AGL for all approaches.
1,000' per minute for either precision or non-precision.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 계기접근 최종단계에서 1,000 fpm을 초과해 강하하면 안전여유가 크게 감소한다. Stabilized approach 개념상 이 중요한 구간에서는 1,000 fpm 초과 강하를 피해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: Research has shown that the margin of safety is seriously reduced when descending at greater than 1,000' per minute during the final stages of any instrument approach procedure. Thus, the stabilized approach concept states that descents above this rate should not be attempted during this critical stage of flight. Answer (A) is incorrect. A descent rate of 1,200' per minute would compromise the safety margin of the flight. Descent rates above 1,000' per minute should not be utilized in the final stages of any instrument approach procedure. Answer (B) is incorrect. A descent rate of 1,200' per minute would compromise the safety margin of the flight. Descent rates above 1,000' per minute should not be utilized in the final stages of any instrument approach procedure.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: When flying an aircraft with advanced avionics

choices.text: The pilot should fly by engaging the autopilot as first choice.
The pilot should know what autopilot modes are engaged.
Engaging the autopilot is the safe flight control activation.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Autopilot을 engage한 뒤 annunciator panel을 확인해 선택한 mode가 실제로 engage되었는지 반드시 검증해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: The pilot should engage the autopilot, then verify that the selected modes are engaged by monitoring the annunciator panel. Answer (A) is incorrect. The autopilot is a tool, not a crutch. The autopilot should not be assumed to be free of error or misprogramming until the pilot verifies it is tracking the course/ clearance as anticipated. Answer (C) is incorrect. The pilot should always be prepared to fly the airplane manually if the autopilot fails or is not tracking the course/clearance as expected.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: You notice ATC is unusually quiet and one of your VHF transmit lights is illuminated. You suspect

choices.text: your VHF transmitter is keyed and you probably have a stuck microphone.
the radio is performing a self-test function.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 무전이 갑자기 조용한데 VHF transmit light가 켜져 있다면 microphone이 stuck되어 계속 송신 중일 수 있다. 이 경우 같은 주파수의 다른 송신도 방해한다.
questions.explanation_en: If your radio has been quiet and the VHF transmit light is illuminated, you may have a stuck microphone. You are transmitting on the frequency and simultaneously preventing others from transmitting on that same frequency. Answer (A) is incorrect. The VHF transmit light being illuminated suggests the radio is transmitting, not inoperative. The receiver may work fine, but the radio is in the transmit mode, not the receive mode. Answer (C) is incorrect. VHF radios are not designed to perform self-tests at arbitrary times. It is more likely you have a stuck microphone that is monopolizing the frequency by transmitting on it.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: If you notice that one of your VHF transmitter lights is illuminated, you know

choices.text: The radio is performing a self test.
It should be illuminated when you are talking to ATC.
It means the radio is on.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Transmit light는 현재 송신 중임을 알려주는 표시이며 예상치 않게 켜져 있으면 의도치 않은 송신을 알려줄 수 있다. 고장등이나 시험진행 표시가 아니다.
questions.explanation_en: The transmit light is there to acknowledge that you are transmitting and may inform the pilot that the radio is transmitting when not expected. The transmit light is not a malfunction light or a test-in-progress light. Answer (A) is incorrect. The radio performs a self test when the unit is initially turned on, but this is not indicated by the transmit light. Answer (C) is incorrect. All the other radio lights and frequency displays on the radio indicate that the radio is on.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: What is the purpose of an off-route clearance altitude (OROCA) depicted on an IFR enroute navigation chart?

choices.text: The OROCA is intended for emergencies and situational awareness.
The OROCA provides signal coverage for ground-based NAVAIDs, air traffic control radar and communications coverage.
The OROCA provides minimum altitude for RNAV off-route planning.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. OROCA는 비산악지역 1,000 ft, 지정 산악지역 2,000 ft의 장애물 여유를 제공하는 off-route altitude이며 주로 비상상황과 상황인식(SA)을 위한 조종사 참고값이다.
questions.explanation_en: The OROCA is an off-route altitude that provides obstruction clearance with a 1,000-foot buffer in non-mountainous terrain areas and a 2,000-foot buffer in designated mountainous areas within the U.S. OROCAs are intended primarily as a pilot tool for emergencies and SA. Answer (B) is incorrect. The OROCA is an off-route altitude that may not provide signal coverage from ground-based navigational aids, air traffic control radar, or communications coverage. Answer (C) is incorrect. OROCAs depicted on en route charts do not provide the pilot with an acceptable altitude for terrain and obstruction clearance for the purposes of off-route, random RNAV direct flights in either controlled or uncontrolled airspace.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: You are in IMC and descending below 1,000 feet above the TDZE on a straight-in instrument approach in a turbojet. The approach is considered stabilized when the airplane is

choices.text: fully configured and on the correct speed with a descent rate of less than 1,000 FPM.
fully configured with the engines spooled up and a descent rate of no more than 500 FPM.
at least partially configured and on the correct speed with a descent rate of no more than 1,200 FPM.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. IFR straight-in instrument approach는 항공기가 완전히 착륙구성에 있고 올바른 속도·비행경로를 유지하며 강하율이 1,000 fpm 미만일 때 stabilized된 것으로 본다.
questions.explanation_en: Straight-in instrument approaches in IFR conditions are considered stabilized once fully configured and at the correct speed and flight path with a descent rate less than 1,000 fpm. Answer (B) is incorrect. The engines should not only be spooled up, but the aircraft should be at the correct speed and flight path with a descent rate less than 1,000 fpm, not 500 fpm. Answer (C) is incorrect. A descent rate in excess of 1,000 fpm is unacceptable below 1,000 ft. AGL due to human perceptual limitations.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: What would authorize an air carrier to conduct a Special Instrument Approach Procedure?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. FAA Operations Specifications 또는 Letter of Authorization으로 특별히 승인받지 않은 승무원은 Special Instrument Approach Procedure를 수행해서는 안 된다.
questions.explanation_en: Unless specifically authorized by FAA operations specifications or a letter of authorization, flightcrews must not conduct flight operations with Special Instrument Approach Procedures. Answer (B) is incorrect. Any special conditions, equipment, or training would be specified in the operations specifications. Answer (C) is incorrect. Any special conditions, equipment, or training would be specified in the operations specifications.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: Where does the DME indicator have the greatest error between the ground distance and displayed distance to the VORTAC?

choices.text: High altitudes close to the VORTAC.
Low altitudes close to the VORTAC.
Low altitudes far from the VORTAC.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. DME 거리는 항공기와 VORTAC 사이의 직선거리인 slant range이다. 지표면상의 수평거리와의 차이가 slant-range error이며, 시설 가까이에서 고도가 높을수록 가장 커진다.
questions.explanation_en: The mileage readout on the DME is the direct distance from the airplane to the VORTAC and is commonly referred to as slant-range distance. The difference between a measured distance on the surface and the DME slant-range is known as slant-range error and is greatest at high altitudes close to the VORTAC. Answer (B) is incorrect. At low altitudes close to the VORTAC, the slant-range error is less than at high altitudes close to the VORTAC. Answer (C) is incorrect. The slant-range error is at its smallest at low altitudes far from the VORTAC.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: How does DME change with altitude?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. GPS는 waypoint와 항공기 사이의 수평거리를 표시하지만 DME는 slant range를 표시한다. 따라서 시설에 가까우면서 고도가 높을수록 DME 오차가 커지고, 저고도 또는 장거리에서는 작아진다.
questions.explanation_en: GPS systems provide distance as the horizontal measurement from the waypoint (WP) to the aircraft. At 3,000 feet and 0.5 miles, the DME (slant range) distance would read 0.6 NM while the GPS distance would show the actual horizontal distance of 0.5 DME. This error is smallest at low altitudes and/or long ranges. It is greatest when the aircraft is closer to the facility, at which time the DME receiver will display altitude in NM above the facility. DME increases with altitude. Answer (A) is incorrect. DME does not remain the same when altitude changes due to the errors with a DME system caused by slant range distance. Slant range distance refers to the distance from the aircraft’s antenna to the ground station. Answer (C) is incorrect. As the aircraft climbs, the DME distance increases as you are moving away from your WP.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: What DME indications should a pilot observe when directly over a VORTAC site at 12,000 feet?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. VORTAC 바로 상공에서는 DME가 시설 위의 고도를 NM로 나타내는 셈이다. 1 NM은 약 6,000 ft이므로 12,000 ft 상공이면 약 2 DME가 표시된다.
questions.explanation_en: When directly over a VORTAC site, the DME will display altitude in nautical miles (NM) above the site. One NM equals approximately 6,000 ft. At 12,000 ft. directly above the VORTAC, the DME will indicate 2 DME. Answer (A) is incorrect. The DME would indicate 0 DME if it were sitting on top of the VORTAC site. Answer (C) is incorrect. The DME would indicate 2.3 if the airplane were at 13,800 ft. (6,000 × 2.3) above the VORTAC site.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: What would be the identification when a VORTAC is undergoing routine maintenance and is considered unreliable?

choices.text: A test signal, “TESTING,” is sent every 30 seconds.
Identifier is preceded by “M” and an intermittent “OFF” flag would appear.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. VOR를 확실히 식별하는 방법은 Morse code 식별부호 또는 자동 음성식별을 확인하는 것이다. 정비 중에는 TEST code를 송신하거나 식별부호를 제거할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: The only positive method of identifying a VOR is by its Morse code identification or by the recorded automatic voice identification, which is always indicated by the use of the word “V-O-R” following the range’s name. During periods of maintenance, the facility may radiate a T-E-S-T code, or the identification code would be removed. Answer (A) is incorrect. A facility may send a T-E-S-T code, not the test signal “TESTING,” during periods of maintenance. Answer (B) is incorrect. An identifier preceded by “M” designates an identification group for the Microwave Landing System (MLS).

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: Which indication may be received when a VOR is undergoing maintenance and is considered unreliable?

choices.text: Identifier is preceded by “M” and an intermittent “OFF” flag might appear.
An automatic voice recording stating the VOR is out-of-service for maintenance.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. VOR의 확실한 식별은 Morse code 또는 자동 음성식별로 한다. 정비 중에는 TEST 식별을 송신하거나 정상 식별부호가 제거될 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: The only positive method of identifying a VOR is by its Morse code identification or by the recorded automatic voice identification, which is always indicated by the use of the word “V-O-R” following the range’s name. During periods of maintenance, the facility may radiate a T-E-S-T code, or the identification code would be removed. Answer (B) is incorrect. An identifier preceded by “M” designates an identification group for the Microwave Landing System (MLS). Answer (C) is incorrect. When a VOR is undergoing maintenance and is considered unreliable, the automatic voice recording used to identify the station is removed, not replaced with a message that the VOR is out-of-service.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: What angular deviation from a VOR course centerline is represented by a full scale deflection of the CDI?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. CDI는 선택 radial 또는 reciprocal 위에서 중앙에 온다. 표준 VOR CDI는 한 dot당 약 2°이고, 완전편위는 약 10° 이상을 의미한다.
questions.explanation_en: The CDI is the course deviation indicator. This indicator is composed of an instrument face with a needle hinged to move across the instrument face. The needle centers when the aircraft is on the selected radial or its reciprocal. Each dot on the face of the instrument represents 2° off course. The outer edge of the center circle is 2° off course. Full needle deflection to either side of the center position indicates the aircraft is 10° or more off course (assuming that there is normal needle sensitivity). Answer (A) is incorrect. Full scale deflection is to the last dot on the outside of the scale, the fifth dot. Off the scale would be beyond the fifth dot. The aircraft would then be 12° or more off course. Answer (C) is incorrect. If the needle were on the second dot to the left or right of the center of the scale, the aircraft would be 4° off course.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: With full CDI deflection, you will be
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. CDI full-scale deflection은 약 10°이다. 60:1 법칙에 따라 station에서 60 NM 거리에서는 radial 1° 간격이 약 1 NM이므로, 10° 벗어나면 약 10 NM의 횡방향 오차가 된다.
questions.explanation_en: Full scale deflection of a CDI is 10°. The 60:1 rule states that for each 60 miles you are from a station, there is 1 nautical mile (NM) between each radial. Thus, if you are 60 miles from the station, there must be 1 NM between each radial. At full CDI deflection (10°) from the desired course and 1 NM between radials, you are 10 NM off course (10 × 1 = 10). Answer (A) is incorrect. A CDI deflection of 2 dots (4°) would be 4 miles off course. Answer (C) is incorrect. Off course by 12 miles would be beyond full deflection of the CDI needle.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 139 on page 381.) What is the lateral displacement of the aircraft in nautical miles from the radial selected on the No. 1 NAV?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. VOR CDI는 대략 NM당 dot당 200 ft의 횡방향 오차로 볼 수 있다. 60 NM에서 한 dot은 약 2 NM이므로 2.5 dot 편위는 약 5 NM이다.
questions.explanation_en: On VORs, the displacement from course is approximately 200 ft. per dot per NM. At 30 NM from the station, one dot deflection indicates approximately 1 NM displacement of the airplane from the course centerline. At 60 NM, it would be 2 NM for every dot of displacement. Since displacement here is 2 1/2 dots, the airplane would be 5 NM from the centerline. Answer (B) is incorrect. The distance of 7.5 NM would be indicated by a displacement of almost 4 dots. Answer (C) is incorrect. The distance of 10.0 NM would be indicated by a full deflection.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 139 on page 381.) On which radial is the aircraft as indicated by the No. 1 NAV?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Fig. 139에서 OBS 350°와 FROM이면 중앙일 때 R-350이다. CDI가 왼쪽으로 약 5° 편위되어 있으므로 항공기는 R-345 부근에 있다.
questions.explanation_en: The course selector in Fig. 139 is set on 350° with a FROM reading, indicating that, if the course deflection bar were centered, the airplane would be on R-350. Since a total deflection is approximately 10° to 12°, one-half deflection is 5° to 6°. Here, deflection is less than one-half, so it is about 5°. The course deflection bar indicates that this airplane is to the left of R-350, which would be R-345. Answer (A) is incorrect. R-175 would require a TO indicator. Answer (B) is incorrect. R-165 would require a TO indicator and a left deflection.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 139 on page 381.) What is the lateral displacement in degrees from the desired radial on the No. 2 NAV?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 표준 5-dot VOR에서 완전편위 5 dot이 약 10°이므로 2 dot 편위는 약 4°이다.
questions.explanation_en: Since on a standard 5-dot VOR indicator, a full deflection of 5 dots is about 10°, 2 dots means a 4° deflection. Answer (A) is incorrect. A 1° lateral displacement is indicated by a 1/2-dot displacement of the CDI. Answer (B) is incorrect. A 2° lateral displacement is indicated by a 1-dot displacement of the CDI.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 139 on page 381.) Which OBS selection on the No. 1 NAV would center the CDI and change the ambiguity indication to a TO?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Fig. 139에서 OBS 350° FROM이고 CDI가 왼쪽으로 약 5°이면 항공기는 R-345이다. CDI를 중앙에 하고 TO 표시를 얻으려면 reciprocal인 약 165°로 OBS를 설정한다.
questions.explanation_en: The course selector in Fig. 139 is set to 350° with a FROM indication, which means the airplane would be on R-350, if the course deviation bar were centered. However, the deviation bar indicates that the airplane is 5° (2° per dot) to the left of R-350, or R-345. Thus, to center the CDI and change the ambiguity indicator to TO, the OBS should be set to the reciprocal of 345°, which is 165° (345° – 180°). Answer (A) is incorrect. An OBS setting of 175° would change the ambiguity indication to TO, but it would not center the CDI. Answer (C) is incorrect. An OBS setting of 345° would center the CDI, but the ambiguity indication would be FROM, not TO.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 139 above.) Which OBS selection on the No. 2 NAV would center the CDI?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Fig. 139에서 OBS 170°와 FROM이면 중앙일 때 R-170이다. CDI가 왼쪽으로 편위되어 있으므로 항공기는 radial 오른쪽인 약 R-174에 있다.
questions.explanation_en: The course selector in Fig. 139 is set to 170° (it is not an HSI; it is a VOR) and the TO-FROM indicator indicates FROM, which means the airplane would be on R-170 if the course deviation bar were centered. Since the bar indicates a left deflection (2° per dot), the airplane is to the right of the radial, or on R-174. Answer (B) is incorrect. A right, not left, deflection would indicate R-166. Answer (C) is incorrect. The TO-FROM indicator is on FROM, not TO.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 139 above.) Which OBS selection on the No. 2 NAV would center the CDI and change the ambiguity indication to a TO?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Fig. 139에서 실제 위치가 약 R-174이므로 TO 표시를 얻으려면 OBS를 reciprocal인 약 354°로 설정해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: The course selector in Fig. 139 is set to 170° (it is not an HSI; it is a VOR) and the TO-FROM indicator indicates FROM, which means the airplane would be on R-170 if the course deviation bar were centered. Since the bar indicates a left deflection (2° per dot), the airplane is to the right of the radial, or on the 174° radial. To obtain a TO indication, one would have to change the OBS selection by 180° from 174° to 354°. Answer (A) is incorrect. A right deflection would currently mean the airplane is on R-166. To change the ambiguity indicator to a TO, 180° must be added to the current radial. Answer (B) is incorrect. A right, not left, deflection would mean the airplane is currently on R-166.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 142 on page 383 and Figure 143 on page 383.) To which aircraft position does HSI presentation “A” correspond?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Fig. 142/143의 HSI A는 course 090°, TO, right deflection, heading 205°이다. 이 조합은 항공기 1의 위치와 일치한다.
questions.explanation_en: On Figs. 142 and 143, HSI “A” has a VOR course selection of 090°, with a TO indication, meaning the airplane is to the left of the 360/180 radials. It has a right deflection, which means it is north of the 270/090 radials. The airplane heading is 205°, which means airplane 1 is described. Answer (B) is incorrect. Airplane 8 is to the right of the 360/180 radials, which would require a FROM indication. Answer (C) is incorrect. Airplane 11 is to the right of the 360/180 radials and is south of the 270/090 radials, which would require a FROM indication and a left deviation indication.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 142 on page 383 and Figure 143 on page 383.) To which aircraft position does HSI presentation “B” correspond?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Fig. 142/143의 HSI B는 course 270°, FROM, right deflection, heading 135°이며 이 조건은 항공기 19에 해당한다.
questions.explanation_en: On Figs. 142 and 143, HSI “B” has a VOR course selection of 270° with a FROM indication, meaning that the airplane is to the left of the 360/180 radials. Since it has a right deflection, the airplane is south of R-270. Given a heading of 135°, airplane 19 is described. Answer (A) is incorrect. Airplane 9 would require a left, not right, course deflection bar indication and a TO indication. Answer (B) is incorrect. Airplane 13 is to the right of the 360/180 radials and would require a TO indication.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 142 on page 383 and Figure 143 on page 383.) To which aircraft position does HSI presentation “C” correspond?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Fig. 142/143의 HSI C는 course 360°, TO, CDI left, heading 310°이므로 항공기는 R-180의 동쪽에 있으며 항공기 12와 일치한다.
questions.explanation_en: On Figs. 142 and 143, HSI “C” has a VOR course selection of 360° with a TO indication, meaning the airplane is south of the 270/090 radials. Since the course deflection bar is to the left, the airplane is to the east of the 180° radial. Given a 310° heading, airplane 12 is described. Answer (A) is incorrect. Airplane 6 has a heading of 360° and is north of the 270/090 radials, which would require a FROM indication. Answer (B) is incorrect. Airplane 7 is north of the 270/090 radials, which would require a FROM indication.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 142 on page 383 and Figure 143 on page 383.) To which aircraft position does HSI presentation “D” correspond?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Fig. 142/143의 HSI D는 OBS 180°, FROM, CDI left, heading 180°이므로 항공기 17의 위치와 일치한다.
questions.explanation_en: On Figs. 142 and 143, HSI “D” has a VOR course selection (OBS) of 180°. Its FROM indication means the airplane is south of R-270/090. Since the course deflection bar is to the left, the airplane is west of R-180. Given the heading of 180°, the position describes airplane 17. Answer (A) is incorrect. Airplane 4 is to the north of the 270/090 radials, which would require a TO indication. Answer (B) is incorrect. The course deflection bar on airplane 15 would have a centered deflection bar and a heading of 360°.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 142 on page 383 and Figure 143 on page 383.) To which aircraft position does HSI presentation “E” correspond?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Fig. 142/143의 HSI E는 course 360°, FROM, CDI left, heading 360°이므로 항공기 6에 해당한다.
questions.explanation_en: On Figs. 142 and 143, HSI “E” has a VOR course selection of 360°. Its FROM indication means the airplane is north of R-270/090. Given the course deflection bar to the left, the airplane is to the east of the 360° radial. Given the 360° heading, the position describes airplane 6. Answer (A) is incorrect. Airplane 5 would have a centered deflection bar and has a heading of 180°. Answer (C) is incorrect. Airplane 15 is to the south of the 270/090 radials, which would require a TO indication, and the deflection bar would be centered.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 142 on page 383 and Figure 143 on page 383.) To which aircraft position does HSI presentation “F” correspond?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Fig. 142/143의 HSI F는 course 180°, FROM, CDI centered, heading 045°이므로 항공기는 R-180 위에 있고 항공기 16과 일치한다.
questions.explanation_en: On Figs. 142 and 143, HSI “F” has a VOR course selection of 180° with a FROM indication, meaning that the airplane is south of the 270/090 radials. Since the course deflection bar is centered, the airplane is on R-180. Given a heading of 045° (at the top of the HSI), airplane 16 is described. Answer (A) is incorrect. Airplane 10 is north of the 270/090 radials and east of the 360/180 radials, which would require a TO indication and a right course deflection. Answer (B) is incorrect. Airplane 14 is to the east of R-180, which would require a right course deflection.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 141 below, and Figure 140 on page 385.) To which aircraft position(s) does HSI presentation “A” correspond?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Fig. 140/141에서 HSI A는 heading 360°이고 localizer 편위가 없으므로 localizer 위에 있다. 이 조건에는 항공기 6과 9가 해당한다.
questions.explanation_en: On Figs. 140 and 141, HSI “A” has a heading of 360° with no localizer deviation, which means the airplane is on the localizer. Airplanes 6 and 9 are on the localizer with a 360° heading. Answer (B) is incorrect. The indication will be the same on both the front course and the back course. Answer (C) is incorrect. The indication will be the same on both the front and the back course.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 141 below, and Figure 140 on page 385.) To which aircraft position(s) does HSI presentation “B” correspond?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Fig. 140/141에서 HSI B는 heading 090°, localizer setting 090°, right deflection이다. Back course setting으로 인해 reverse sensing이 적용되며 항공기는 localizer 남쪽에 있어 항공기 5 또는 13과 일치한다.
questions.explanation_en: On Figs. 140 and 141, HSI “B” has a heading of 090°. It has a localizer setting at 090° with a right deflection, meaning the airplane is south of the localizer. Both airplanes 5 and 13 are described. Note the back course setting. If the front course 270° (instead of 90°) had been set, normal (rather than reverse) sensing would be indicated. Answer (A) is incorrect. Airplane 11 has a 270° heading. Answer (C) is incorrect. Airplanes 7 and 11 have 270° headings.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 141 below, and Figure 140 on page 385.) To which aircraft position does HSI presentation “C” correspond?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Fig. 140/141에서 HSI C는 heading 090°이고 CDI가 중앙이므로 localizer 위에 있으며 항공기 12에 해당한다. 중앙편위에서는 back course setting의 영향이 없다.
questions.explanation_en: On Figs. 140 and 141, HSI “C” has a heading of 090° with a centered course deflection bar, which means the airplane is on the localizer with a 090° heading, which is airplane 12. The back course setting (090) has no effect because the deflection bar is centered. Answer (A) is incorrect. Airplane 9 has a 360° heading. Answer (B) is incorrect. Airplane 4 has a 270° heading.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 141 below, and Figure 140 on page 385.) To which aircraft position does HSI presentation “D” correspond?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Fig. 140/141에서 HSI D는 heading 310°, back course setting 090°로 reverse sensing이 생긴다. Right deflection은 항공기가 localizer 남쪽임을 뜻해 항공기 2와 일치한다.
questions.explanation_en: On Figs. 140 and 141, HSI “D” has a heading of 310° in a back course setting (090), resulting in reverse sensing. It has a right deflection, meaning the airplane is south of the localizer. Thus, airplane 2 is described. Answer (A) is incorrect. Airplane 1 is on a 225° heading, not a 310° heading, and is north of the localizer. Answer (B) is incorrect. Airplane 10 has a 135° heading and is north of the localizer. ion and Direction of Flight.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 140 above, and Figure 141 on page 386.) To which aircraft position(s) does HSI presentation “E” correspond?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Fig. 140/141에서 HSI E는 heading 045°, back course setting 090°와 right deflection이므로 reverse sensing상 localizer 남쪽에 있고 항공기 3 또는 8에 해당한다.
questions.explanation_en: On Figs. 140 and 141, HSI “E” has a heading of 045°. It has a right deflection with a back course HSI setting of 090. This results in reverse sensing, meaning the airplane is south of the localizer. Thus, airplanes 3 and 8 are described. Answer (A) is incorrect. Both airplanes 8 and 3 have a 045° heading and are south of the localizer. Answer (C) is incorrect. Both airplanes 8 and 3 have a 045° heading and are south of the localizer.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 141 below, and Figure 140 on page 387.) To which aircraft position does HSI presentation “F” correspond?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Fig. 140/141에서 HSI F는 localizer 270°, CDI centered, heading 270°이므로 항공기 4이다.
questions.explanation_en: On Figs. 140 and 141, HSI “F” has a localizer setting at 270° with a centered bar and a 270° heading, which is airplane 4. Answer (B) is incorrect. Airplane 11 has a left course deviation bar. Answer (C) is incorrect. Airplane 5 has a 090° heading, not 270°. It also should have a right deflection because it is south of the localizer.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 141 below, and Figure 140 on page 387.) To which aircraft position(s) does HSI presentation “G” correspond?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Fig. 140/141에서 HSI G도 localizer 270°, CDI centered, heading 270°이므로 항공기 4와 일치한다.
questions.explanation_en: On Figs. 140 and 141, HSI “G” has a localizer setting at 270° with a centered bar and a 270° heading, which is airplane 4. Answer (B) is incorrect. Airplane 11 has a left course deviation bar. Answer (C) is incorrect. Airplane 12 has a 090° heading, not 270°.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 141 below, and Figure 140 on page 387.) To which aircraft position does HSI presentation “H” correspond?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. HSI H는 heading 215°와 centered CDI를 나타내지만 Fig. 141에는 그 위치에 해당하는 항공기가 없다.
questions.explanation_en: HSI “H” depicts an airplane with a heading of 215° and a centered CDI. No aircraft are shown in this position in Fig. 141. Answer (B) is incorrect. On Figs. 140 and 141, HSI “H” has a localizer setting at 270° with a centered CDI, meaning the airplane is on the localizer. Airplane 1 is on the correct heading of 215° but is not lined up on the localizer. Answer (C) is incorrect. Airplane 2 has a heading of 315° and is located south of the localizer.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 141 below, and Figure 140 on page 387.) To which aircraft position does HSI presentation “I” correspond?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 항공기 4는 localizer 위에서 CDI가 중앙이고 heading 270°이며, 이는 HSI I의 표시와 일치한다.
questions.explanation_en: Airplane 4 is on the localizer with a centered CDI and on a heading of 270°. This matches what is shown on HSI “I.” Answer (B) is incorrect. Airplane 12 has a heading of 090°, not 270°. Answer (C) is incorrect. HSI “I” has a centered CDI with a heading of 270°. Thus, the airplane is on the localizer. Airplane 11 has a 270° heading but is north of the localizer. ion and Direction of Flight.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 140 above, and Figure 141 on page 386.) If on a back course to the Runway 9 approach, to which HSI presentation does aircraft 8 correspond?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 항공기 8은 heading 045°이고 localizer course 오른쪽에 있다. Back course localizer 접근이므로 reverse sensing이 나타나며 HSI E와 일치한다.
questions.explanation_en: Aircraft 8 is on a heading of 045°, which is only represented by HSI “E.” Aircraft 8 is also to the right of the localizer course, and because a backcourse localizer approach is being flown, the HSI will display reverse sensing, as seen in HSI “E.” Answer (A) is incorrect. HSI “H” represents an aircraft on a heading of 215° and on the localizer; however, aircraft 8 is on a heading of 045° and is right of the localizer. Answer (B) is incorrect. HSI “I” represents an aircraft on a heading of 270° and on the localizer; however, aircraft 8 is on a heading of 045° and is right of the localizer.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 123 below.) You receive this ATC clearance: “...HOLD EAST OF THE ABC VORTAC ON THE ZERO NINER ZERO RADIAL, LEFT TURNS...” What is the recommended procedure to enter the holding pattern?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. ABC VORTAC 동쪽 R-090에서 좌선회 holding이면 holding side는 R-090 남쪽이다. 남서쪽에서 heading 55°로 진입하는 조건에서는 sector 판정상 parallel entry가 적절하다.
questions.explanation_en: You are cleared to hold east of the ABC VORTAC with left turns on R-090. The holding side will be south of R-090, and you are entering from the southwest on a 55° heading (Fig. 123). Draw the 70° line through the VOR and on R-340, R-160. A parallel entry is appropriate for R-160 to R-270. R-270 to R-340 Teardrop R-340 to R-160 Direct R-160 to R-270 Parallel Answer (B) is incorrect. A direct entry would be appropriate if you were coming in on R-340 to R-160. Answer (C) is incorrect. A teardrop entry would be appropriate if you were coming in from R-270 to R-340.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 123 below.) You receive this ATC clearance: “...CLEARED TO THE ABC VORTAC. HOLD SOUTH ON THE ONE EIGHT ZERO RADIAL...” What is the recommended procedure to enter the holding pattern?

choices.text: Parallel only. Figure 123. Aircraft Course and DME Indicator.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. R-180 남쪽에서 우선회 holding이면 holding side는 R-180 동쪽이다. 남서쪽 R-240에서 접근하므로 direct entry가 적절하다.
questions.explanation_en: You are cleared to hold south on the 180° radial with right turns, which means you will be to the east of R-180. Since you are coming in from the southwest (R-240), you can make a direct entry. R-290 to R-360 Teardrop R-360 to R-110 Parallel R-110 to R-290 Direct Answer (A) is incorrect. A teardrop entry would be appropriate only from R-290 to R-360. Answer (C) is incorrect. A parallel entry would be appropriate only from R-360 to R-110.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 123 above.) You receive this ATC clearance: “...CLEARED TO THE XYZ VORTAC. HOLD NORTH ON THE THREE SIX ZERO RADIAL, LEFT TURNS...” What is the recommended procedure to enter the holding pattern?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. XYZ VORTAC 북쪽 R-360에서 좌선회 holding이면 radial 동쪽이 holding side이다. 남서쪽 R-240에서 접근하므로 teardrop entry가 적절하다.
questions.explanation_en: Holding north of the XYZ VORTAC with left turns on R-360 means you are on the east side of the radial. Since you are coming in from the southwest (R-240), you will be making a teardrop entry. R-180 to R-250 Teardrop R-250 to R-070 Direct R-070 to R-180 Parallel Answer (A) is incorrect. A parallel approach would be appropriate only if coming in between R-070 and R-180. Answer (B) is incorrect. A direct entry is appropriate only between R-250 and R-070.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 123 on page 388.) You receive this ATC clearance: “...CLEARED TO THE ABC VORTAC. HOLD WEST ON THE TWO SEVEN ZERO RADIAL...” What is the recommended procedure to enter the holding pattern?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. R-270 서쪽에서 우선회 holding이면 holding side는 R-270 남쪽이다. R-240에서 접근하므로 direct entry가 적절하다.
questions.explanation_en: You are cleared to hold west on R-270 with right turns, so you will be south of R-270. Since you are coming in on R-240, you need to make a direct entry. R-020 to R-090 Teardrop R-090 to R-200 Parallel R-200 to R-020 Direct Answer (A) is incorrect. A parallel entry is appropriate only on R-090 to R-200. Answer (C) is incorrect. A teardrop entry is appropriate only when coming in on R-020 to R-090.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: The maximum speed a propeller-driven airplane may hold at is
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 14,000 ft MSL 초과 고도에서 모든 항공기의 최대 holding speed는 265 kt이다.
questions.explanation_en: The maximum holding airspeed for all aircraft (including a propeller-driven airplane) is 265 kt. when holding at an altitude above 14,000 ft. MSL. Answer (B) is incorrect. While 230 kt. is the maximum holding airspeed from 6,001 ft. to 14,000 ft., a higher airspeed of 265 kt. is permitted when holding at an altitude above 14,000 ft. Answer (C) is incorrect. This is not a maximum holding speed for any altitude.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: Maximum holding speed for a turbojet airplane above 14,000 feet is
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 14,000 ft 초과 holding의 최대속도는 모든 항공기에서 265 kt이다. 난기류·착빙 등 안전상 필요하면 ATC와 협의해 더 높은 속도를 사용할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: The maximum airspeed above 14,000 ft. for holding patterns is 265 kt. for all aircraft, including a turbojet airplane. This speed limit can be increased if necessary for safety reasons through discussion with ATC. Answer (A) is incorrect. This is not a maximum holding speed at any altitude. Answer (B) is incorrect. This is the maximum holding speed for all aircraft from 6,001 ft. to 14,000 ft., not above 14,000 ft.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: Maximum holding speed for a civil turbojet aircraft at a joint use airport (civil/Navy) between 7,000 and 14,000 feet is
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 6,001~14,000 ft에서 모든 항공기의 최대 holding speed는 230 kt이다.
questions.explanation_en: The maximum holding speed for all aircraft, including a civil turbojet, from 6,001 ft. to 14,000 ft. is 230 kt. Holding speeds are based on altitudes at joint-use airports. Answer (A) is incorrect. This is the maximum holding speed of all aircraft from the MHA (minimum holding altitude) through 6,000 ft., not from 6,001 ft. to 14,000 ft. Answer (B) is incorrect. This is the maximum holding speed for all aircraft from 14,001 ft. and above.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: What is the maximum holding speed for a civil turbojet holding at a civil airport at 15,000 ft. MSL, unless a higher speed is required due to turbulence or icing and ATC is notified?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 14,000 ft MSL 초과에서 최대 holding speed는 265 kt이며, 난기류나 착빙 때문에 더 높은 속도가 필요하면 ATC에 알리고 사용할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: The maximum holding speed for all aircraft, including a civil turbojet, above 14,000 ft. MSL is 265 kt. A higher airspeed may be used if necessary due to turbulence or icing and provided ATC is notified. Answer (B) is incorrect. This is the maximum holding speed for any aircraft holding at an altitude between 6,001 ft. and 14,000 ft., not above 14,000 ft. Answer (C) is incorrect. This is not a maximum holding airspeed at any altitude.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: An aircraft holding at an altitude of 14,000 feet should expect to operate at which holding pattern airspeed?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 6,001~14,000 ft에서 모든 항공기의 최대 holding speed는 230 kt이다.
questions.explanation_en: The maximum holding speed for all aircraft from 6,001 ft. to 14,000 ft. is 230 kt. Answer (A) is incorrect. This is not a maximum holding airspeed at any altitude. Answer (B) is incorrect. This is not a maximum holding speed at any altitude.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 124 below.) A pilot receives this ATC clearance: “...CLEARED TO THE ABC VORTAC. HOLD WEST ON THE TWO SEVEN ZERO RADIAL...” What is the recommended procedure to enter the holding pattern?

choices.text: Direct only. Figure 124. Aircraft Course and DME Indicator.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. R-270 서쪽에서 우선회 holding이면 pattern은 radial 남쪽에 형성된다. 북서쪽 R-330에서 heading 155°로 fix에 접근하므로 direct entry가 적절하다.
questions.explanation_en: When holding west on the 270° radial, use right turns because left turns were not stated in the clearance. The holding pattern will be to the south of the 270° radial, so the VORTAC (the fix) is at the end of the inbound leg. To determine entry procedures, draw a 70° line through the holding fix such that the 70° line crosses through the outbound leg one-third of the leg length from abeam the fix. R-020 to R-090 Teardrop R-090 to R-200 Parallel R-200 to R-020 Direct Since you are approaching the holding fix from the northwest (R-330) on a 155° heading, you will make a direct entry. Answer (A) is incorrect. The parallel or teardrop entries are alternatives only when approaching on R-090. Answer (B) is incorrect. The parallel entry is appropriate only when approaching on R-090 to R-200.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 124 above.) A pilot receives this ATC clearance: “...CLEARED TO THE XYZ VORTAC. HOLD NORTH ON THE THREE SIX ZERO RADIAL, LEFT TURNS...” What is the recommended procedure to enter the holding pattern?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. R-360 북쪽에서 좌선회 holding이면 pattern은 radial 동쪽에 형성된다. 북서쪽에서 heading 155°로 접근하므로 direct entry가 적절하다.
questions.explanation_en: Visualize a 360° radial with left turns. The pattern will be to the east of the radial with the holding fix being the VORTAC. Since you are approaching from the northwest with a heading of 155° (Fig. 124), you will be able to make a direct entry. R-180 to R-250 Teardrop R-250 to R-070 Direct R-070 to R-180 Parallel Answer (A) is incorrect. If you were approaching on R-180 to R-250, you would make a teardrop entry. Answer (B) is incorrect. If you were approaching on R-070 to R-180, you would fly through the VOR, parallel the holding course, turn right to the holding course, and make a parallel entry.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 124 above.) A pilot receives this ATC clearance: “...CLEARED TO THE ABC VORTAC. HOLD SOUTH ON THE ONE EIGHT ZERO RADIAL...” What is the recommended procedure to enter the holding pattern?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. R-180 남쪽에서 우선회 holding이면 pattern은 radial 동쪽에 형성된다. R-330 방향에서 inbound하므로 teardrop entry가 적절하다.
questions.explanation_en: If you are holding south on the 180° radial, you will have right turns because left turns are not specified and you will be on the east side of the radial (to cross the VORTAC at the end of your inbound leg). Draw the 70° line through the VORTAC on R-110, R-290. Since you are inbound on R-330 (Fig. 124), you would make a teardrop entry. R-290 to R-360 Teardrop R-360 to R-110 Parallel R-110 to R-290 Direct Answer (B) is incorrect. A parallel entry is appropriate from R-360 to R-110. Answer (C) is incorrect. A direct entry is appropriate from R-110 to R-290.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: When using a flight director system, what rate of turn or bank angle should a pilot observe during turns in a holding pattern?

choices.text: 3° per second or 25° bank, whichever is less.
3° per second or 30° bank, whichever is less.
1-1/2° per second or 25° bank, whichever is less.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Flight director를 사용할 때 최대 선회율 또는 bank는 초당 3° 또는 bank 25° 중 작은 값을 사용한다.
questions.explanation_en: The maximum rate of turn or bank to be used when using a flight director system should be 3° per second or 25° bank, whichever is less. Answer (B) is incorrect. Maximum bank while holding using a flight director is 25° bank, not 30° bank. Answer (C) is incorrect. Maximum bank while holding using a flight director is 25° bank or 3° per second, not 1-1/2° per second, whichever is less.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: When entering a holding pattern above 14,000 feet, the initial outbound leg should not exceed

choices.text: 1-1/2 minutes or 10 NM, whichever is less.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 14,000 ft MSL 초과 holding에서는 최초 outbound leg가 1분 30초를 넘지 않아야 하며, 이후에는 inbound leg가 1분 30초가 되도록 outbound 시간을 조정한다.
questions.explanation_en: When at an altitude greater than 14,000 ft. MSL, the initial outbound leg should not exceed 1-1/2 min. Timing for subsequent outbound legs should be adjusted as necessary to achieve proper inbound leg time (1-1/2 min. inbound). Answer (A) is incorrect. An initial outbound leg of 1 min. should be used only when below 14,000 ft. Answer (C) is incorrect. A DME distance is issued only by the specified controller for aircraft equipped with DME capability. A DME distance is not required unless specified by the controller.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: All 14 CFR Part 139 airports must report

choices.text: noise complaint statistics for each departure procedure or runway.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Declared distance는 이륙·착륙 성능요건에 사용할 수 있는 최대 적합거리이다. 포장 활주로 길이에 clearway·stopway를 더하고 필요한 안전구역·object free area·runway protection zone 확보를 위해 일부 길이를 뺀 값으로 산정한다.
questions.explanation_en: Declared distances for a runway represent the maximum distances available and suitable for meeting takeoff and landing distance performance requirements. These distances are determined in accordance with FAA runway design standards by adding to the physical length of paved runway any clearway or stopway and subtracting from that sum any lengths necessary to obtain the standard runway safety areas, runway object free areas, or runway protection zones. All 14 CFR Part 139 airports report declared distances for each runway. Answer (A) is incorrect. The operator of an aircraft that is involved in an accident or incident, not a 14 CFR Part 139 airport, must file a report within 10 days of the accident or incident, not annually. Answer (B) is incorrect. Individual airports, not all 14 CFR Part 139 airports, are responsible for determining noise abatement requirements, establishing their own operating procedures, tracking complaints, and conducting their own enforcement.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: What is the latest point at which a missed approach climb must be executed for obstacle clearance protection?

choices.text: For an ILS, on glidepath at the decision altitude.
For a straight-in localizer, no later than the departure end of the runway (DER).
For a straight-in localizer, or ILS, at the Middle Marker.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 장애물 회피를 보장받으려면 missed approach는 MAP에서 시작해야 한다. DA/DH 또는 MDA 이후 늦게 missed approach를 시작하면 공표 missed approach course와 altitude에 established될 때까지 추가 위험이 생긴다.
questions.explanation_en: For obstacle clearance to be assured, the pilot must execute the missed approach at the Missed Approach Point (MAP). Any missed approach after the Decision Altitude (DA), Decision Height (DH), or Minimum Decision Altitude (MDA) involves additional risk until established on the published missed approach procedure course and altitude. Answer (B) is incorrect. The MAP must be well prior to the departure end of the runway. Answer (C) is incorrect. The Middle Marker would be too far and too high away from the runway to be able to possibly see the runway environment for landing. If the missed approach procedures involved a turn-and-do-this at the Middle Marker, obstacle clearance is not guaranteed.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 114 on page 453 and Figure 114A on page 454.) The changeover point on V394 between DAG VORTAC and POM VORTAC is
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Fig. 114A에서 POM VORTAC에서 V394(V210-394)를 따라 changeover point까지 보면 DAG VORTAC까지 거리는 64 DME이다.
questions.explanation_en: Refer to Fig. 114A. On the lower portion of the chart, locate POM VORTAC and move right to follow V394 (V210-394) to the changeover point indicated by “.” The number at the top is the distance to DAG VORTAC, or 64 DME. Answer (A) is incorrect. When the changeover point is NOT located at the midway point, aeronautical charts will depict the location and give mileage to each VORTAC. Answer (B) is incorrect. The 38 DME from DAG VORTAC is APLES INT, not the changeover point.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 114 on page 453.) The minimum crossing altitude at APLES INT southwest bound on V394 is
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Fig. 114에서 DAG VORTAC에서 V394를 따라 APLES INT를 찾으면 해당 지점의 southwest 방향 MCA는 9,100 ft이다.
questions.explanation_en: Fig. 114 provides an en route low-altitude chart. In the upper portion, locate DAG VORTAC (in the right center) and move left along V394 to APLES INT (38 DME from DAG VORTAC). The flag with an X indicates a minimum crossing altitude (MCA). Below APLES INT, it reads “V210-394 9100 SW,” which means the minimum crossing altitude is 9,100 ft. when flying southwest on V394. Answer (A) is incorrect. The minimum en route altitude (MEA) from DAG VORTAC to APLES INT on V394, not the MCA at APLES INT, is 7,500 ft. Answer (C) is incorrect. The MEA after APLES INT, not the MCA at APLES INT, is 11,500 ft.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 114A on page 454 and Figure 163A on page 393.) (Refer to the lower panel.) What is the minimum en route altitude on V210, when crossing the POM VORTAC southwest bound and continuing on the same airway?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Fig. 114A에서 POM VORTAC southwest 방향 V210에는 별도 MCA가 없으므로 MEA가 MCA 역할을 하며 그 값은 5,300 ft이다.
