questions.question: To conduct an RNAV (GPS) approach to LPV minimums, the aircraft must be furnished with

choices.text: a GPS/WAAS receiver approved for an LPV approach by the AFM supplement.
a GPS (TSO-C129) receiver certified for IFR operations.
an IFR approach-certified system with required navigation performance (RNP) of 0.5.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. WAAS avionics는 TSO-C145 또는 TSO-C146 기준으로 인증되어야 하며 FAA 승인 AFM과 supplement에 따라 운용한다. Flight manual supplement에는 receiver가 지원하는 접근 수준이 명시된다.
questions.explanation_en: WAAS avionics must be certified in accordance with Technical Standard Order (TSO) TSO-C145 or TSO-C146. GPS/WAAS operation must be conducted in accordance with the FAA-approved aircraft flight manual (AFM) and flight manual supplements. The flight manual supplements will state the level of approach procedure that the receiver supports. Answer (B) is incorrect. Stand-alone GPS equipment used in IFR operations for approach to LPV minimums must meet the standards set forth in TSO-C145 or TSO-C146, not TSO-C129. Answer (C) is incorrect. An approach certified system must provide RNP of 0.3, not 0.5.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: In order to use a substitute means of guidance on departure procedures, pilots of aircraft with RNAV systems using DME/DME/IRU without GPS input must

choices.text: ensure their aircraft navigation system position is confirmed within 2,000 feet of the initialization point.
ensure their aircraft navigation system position is confirmed within 1,000 feet of pushback.
ensure their aircraft navigation system position is confirmed within 1,000 feet at the start point of takeoff roll.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. GPS/GNSS 없이 DME/DME/IRU를 사용하는 경우 takeoff roll 시작점에서 항공기 항법시스템 위치가 1,000 ft 이내 정확도로 확인되어야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: Pilots using DME/DME/IRU without GPS/ GNSS must ensure the aircraft navigation system position is confirmed within 1,000 feet at the start point of the takeoff roll. Answer (A) is incorrect. The tolerance is 1,000 feet, not 2,000 feet, and the reference point is the start of the takeoff roll, not the initialization point. Answer (B) is incorrect. The reference point for the aircraft navigation system position is the start of the takeoff roll, not the pushback position.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: During flight planning, you selected an alternate airport serviced by only an RNAV (GPS/WAAS) approach. There are no prohibitions on the instrument approach procedure chart against using the airport as an alternate, and your aircraft is WAAS equipped. Therefore, the airport may

choices.text: be selected as an alternate using the LNAV minima line.
not be selected as an alternate since it only has an RNAV (GPS) approach.
be selected as an alternate using the LPV minima line.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. WAAS avionics를 설치했다고 해서 예정 항로에 적합한 다른 장비가 반드시 필요한 것은 아니다. 일정 제한은 있지만 required alternate에서도 WAAS avionics가 승인된 계기접근을 계획할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Installation of WAAS avionics does not require the aircraft to have other equipment appropriate to the route to be flown. There are certain restrictions on WAAS operations. Pilots may plan to use any instrument approach authorized for use with WAAS avionics at a required alternate. Answer (B) is incorrect. Unlike TSO-C129 avionics, which were certified as a supplement to other means of navigation, WAAS avionics are evaluated without reliance on other navigation systems. Installation of WAAS avionics does not require the aircraft to have other equipment appropriate to the route to be flown. Answer (C) is incorrect. When using WAAS at an alternate airport, flight planning must be based on flying the RNAV (GPS) LNAV minima line or minima on a GPS approach procedure or conventional approach procedure with “or GPS” in the title.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 293 on page 433.) What is the distance from ASALT intersection to the MAP?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Approach plate profile view에 따르면 ASALT에서 MAP까지 거리는 6 NM + 2.6 NM = 8.6 NM이다.
questions.explanation_en: The distance from ASALT to the MAP is 8.6 NM (6 NM + 2.6 NM) as per the approach plate profile view. Answer (B) is incorrect. The DME distance from CRI to CRI 2.6 is 2.6 NM. Answer (C) is incorrect. The distance from ASALT to CANARSIE is 6 NM.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 293 on page 433.) The distance from the FAF to the MAP for the VOR or GPS RWY 13L/13R approach is
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. FAF에서 MAP까지 거리는 접근차트의 profile view와 오른쪽 아래 speed/time table 위 두 곳에서 확인할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: The distance from the FAF to the MAP can be found in two places on the approach chart. The first is in the profile view and the second is in the lower right corner above the speed/time table. Answer (A) is incorrect. The distance of 6.2 NM is the sum of the distance from CRI to the MAP plus the distance to the 13L runway. Answer (B) is incorrect. The distance of 3.2 NM is the distance from the FAF (CRI VOR/DME) to the lead-in lights.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: “Unreliable”, as indicated in the following GPS NOTAMS: SFO 12/051 SFOWAAS LNAV/VNAV AND LPV MNM UNRELBL WEF0512182025-0512182049 means

choices.text: within the time parameters of the NOTAM, the predicted level of service will not support LPV approaches.
satellite signals are currently unavailable to support LPV and LNAV/VNAV approaches.
within the time parameters of the NOTAM, the predicted level of service will not support RNAV approaches.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. WAAS NOTAM의 'UNRELBL'은 예상되는 WAAS service 수준을 이용하지 못할 수 있다는 advisory이다. 따라서 LNAV/VNAV와 LPV가 이용 가능할 수도, 불가능할 수도 있다.
questions.explanation_en: The term “unreliable” (UNRELBL) is an advisory to pilots indicating that the expected level of WAAS service may not be available. This NOTAM indicates that both LNAV/VNAV and LPV approaches may or may not be available. Answer (B) is incorrect. When satellite signals are not available, the name of the satellite and the words “SATELLITE UNAVBL” will be included in the NOTAM (i.e., “PACIFIC SATELLITE UNAVBL”). Answer (C) is incorrect. This NOTAM does not support RNAV approaches.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 250 on page 435.) During the preflight brief, you receive a WAAS [MAY NOT BE AVBL] NOTAM for the RNAV (GPS) RWY 2 approach at KCHA. For planning purposes only, you know that you can descend to the

choices.text: LPV DA minima of 882 ft. and 2,400 RVR in your CAT B aircraft.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. WAAS [MAY NOT BE AVBL] NOTAM은 비행계획용 예측정보이다. 도착 후 avionics가 LNAV/VNAV 또는 LPV service available을 표시하면 표시된 service 수준으로 vertical guidance를 사용할 수 있고, 접근 중 outage가 발생하면 LNAV minimum으로 되돌아가야 할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: WAAS [MAY NOT BE AVBL] NOTAMs are predictive in nature and published for flight planning purposes only. Upon arrival at a location that has been NOTAMed WAAS [MAY NOT BE AVBL], if the WAAS avionics indicated LNAV/ VNAV or LPV service is available, then vertical guidance may be used to complete the approach using the displayed level of service. Should an outage occur during the approach, reversion to LNAV minimums may be required. Answer (A) is incorrect. Vertical navigation (VNAV) utilizes an internally generated glideslope based on WAAS. Answer (C) is incorrect. LPV approaches take advantage of the refined accuracy of WAAS for lateral and vertical guidance.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: You arrive at the initial fix for the LPV approach into XYZ. The preflight briefer issued you an unreliable advisory on the approach before you took off. Your avionics indicates good signals and full GPS service is available. You

choices.text: know you can fly the approach down to LPV minimums.
cannot use that approach because of the advisory from FSS.
must revert to another approach system such as VOR.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. WAAS UNRELIABLE NOTAM도 비행계획용 예측정보이다. 현장에서 avionics가 LNAV/VNAV 또는 LPV available을 표시하면 vertical guidance를 사용할 수 있으며, 운항 중 service가 상실되면 LNAV minimum 적용이 필요할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: WAAS UNRELIABLE NOTAMs are predictive in nature and published for flight planning purposes only. Upon arrival at a location that has been NOTAMed WAAS UNRELIABLE, if the WAAS avionics indicate LNAV/VNAV or LPV service is available, then vertical guidance may be used to complete the approach using the displayed level of service. Should an outage occur during the approach, reversion to LNAV minimums may be required. Answer (B) is incorrect. WAAS UNRELIABLE NOTAMs are predictive in nature and published for flight planning purposes only. Upon arrival at a location that has been NOTAMed WAAS UNRELIABLE, if the WAAS avionics indicate LNAV/VNAV or LPV service is available, then vertical guidance may be used to complete the approach using the displayed level of service. Answer (C) is incorrect. WAAS UNRELIABLE NOTAMs are predictive in nature and published for flight planning purposes only. Upon arrival at a location that has been NOTAMed WAAS UNRELIABLE, if the WAAS avionics indicate LNAV/VNAV or LPV service is available, then vertical guidance may be used to complete the approach using the displayed level of service.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 249 on page 437.) You arrive at PILOC on the RNAV (GPS) RWY 19R approach to BET. The briefer gave you an UNRELIABLE advisory for the approach before takeoff. Your avionics indicate good signals, and GPS service is available.

choices.text: You can only fly the approach to LNAV DA minimums of 459 because of the advisory.
You can only fly the approach down to the LNAV MDA of 560.
You can use the LPV DA minimums of 368 and 2400 RVR in your category B airplane.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 'Unreliable'은 GPS/WAAS NOTAM에서 예상 WAAS service(LNAV/VNAV/LPV)가 이용 불가할 수 있음을 알리는 예측 advisory이다. 접근 시 실제 avionics가 service available을 표시하면 그 수준을 사용할 수 있으나 상실 시 LNAV minima로 복귀해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: The term “unreliable” is used in conjunction with GPS and WAAS NOTAMs. It is an advisory to pilots indicating the expected level of WAAS service (LNAV/VNAV/ LPV) may not be available. WAAS unreliable NOTAMs are predictive in nature and published for flight planning purposes. Once commencing an approach at locations NOTAMed WAAS UNRELIABLE, if the WAAS avionics indicate LNAV/VNAV or LPV service is available, then vertical guidance may be used to complete the approach using the displayed level of service. Should an outage occur during the approach, reversion to LNAV minima may be required. As the WAAS NOTAM is for planning purposes, you will know you can descend to the LNAV DA of 459 ft. as shown on the chart in Fig. 249. This applies to all category of aircraft. Answer (A) is incorrect. Once commencing an approach at locations NOTAMed WAAS UNRELIABLE, if the WAAS avionics indicate LNAV/VNAV or LPV service is available, then vertical guidance may be used to complete the approach using the displayed level of service. Answer (B) is incorrect. Should an outage occur during the approach, reversion to LNAV minima may be required. As the WAAS NOTAM is for planning purposes, you will know you can descend to the LNAV DA of 459 ft. as shown on the chart in Fig. 249.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: To utilize the localizer performance with vertical guidance (LPV) decision altitude (DA) minima on a RNAV (GPS) instrument approach procedure, the aircraft must be equipped with an appropriately certified

choices.text: GPS receiver with mode S transponder.
GPS receiver with mode Z transponder.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. LPV는 WAAS 기반 APV minimum으로 localizer 수준의 lateral accuracy와 전자식 lateral/vertical guidance를 제공한다. AFM에 탑재장비가 LPV를 지원한다고 명시되어 있어야 하며 GPS/WAAS receiver는 관련 TSO 인증을 받아야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: LPV identifies WAAS approach with vertical guidance (APV) approach minimums with electronic lateral and vertical guidance capability. The lateral guidance is equivalent to localizer accuracy, and the protected area is considerably smaller than the protected area for the present LNAV and LNAV/ VNAV lateral protection. Aircraft can fly this minima line with a statement in the AFM that the installed equipment supports LPV approaches. TSO-145A/146A certifies the GPS/WAAS receiver. Answer (A) is incorrect. Mode S transponders are covered under TSO-C112e and are not certified under TSO-145A/146A. Answer (C) is incorrect. It is the GPS that must be TSO certified and must have a minimum mode C transponder.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches
questions.question: What does “UNREL” indicate in the following GPS and WAAS NOTAM: BOS BOS WAAS LPV AND LNAV/VNAV MNM UNREL WEF 0305231700 - 0305231815?

choices.text: Satellite signals are currently unavailable to support LPV and LNAV/VNAV approaches to the Boston airport.
The predicted level of service, within the time parameters of the NOTAM, may not support LPV approaches.
The predicted level of service, within the time parameters of the NOTAM, will not support LNAV/VNAV approaches.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. WAAS UNRELIABLE NOTAM은 비행계획용 예측정보이며 NOTAM 끝의 date/time group이 시스템이 unreliable할 수 있는 특정 시간창을 나타낸다.
questions.explanation_en: The FAA’s WAAS UNRELIABLE NOTAMs are predictive in nature and are published for flight planning purposes. The date/time group of numbers at the end of this NOTAM indicate a specific window when the system may be unreliable. Answer (A) is incorrect. The FAA’s WAAS UNRELIABLE NOTAMs are predictive in nature and are published for flight planning purposes. The date/time group of numbers at the end of this NOTAM indicate a specific window when the system may be unreliable. The outage is not current, but predicted for a future time frame that will last for 1 hour and 15 minutes. Answer (C) is incorrect. GPS and WAAS NOTAMs are designed to provide information regarding the viability of LNAV, LNAV/VNAV, and LPV approaches.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches

subunit.title: Ground Based Augmentation System (GBAS) Landing System (GLS)

questions.question: (Refer to Figure 293 on page 439.) What must be operational for N711JB to execute the VOR or GPS RWY 13L/13R approach to JFK?

choices.text: Lead-in Light System, Radar and DME.
Lead-in Light System, VOR/DME or GPS.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 접근판의 'DME or RADAR REQUIRED'는 절차 수행에 DME 또는 radar 중 최소 하나가 필요하다는 뜻이다. 또 'For inoperative LDIN, procedure not authorized'는 Lead-in Light System이 불능이면 절차를 수행할 수 없음을 의미한다.
tags: Ground Based Augmentation System (GBAS) Landing System (GLS)
questions.explanation_en: In the middle and to the right on the Instrument Approach Plate is the indication “DME or RADAR REQUIRED.” The approach requires at least one of these supported avionics to fly the procedure. There is a note at the top of the approach plate that reads “For inoperative LDIN, procedure not authorized.” LDIN is the acronym for “Lead-in Light System.” Answer (A) is incorrect. WAAS is not needed for this approach. Answer (B) is incorrect. Radar and DME should be Radar OR DME. Also needed is a VOR or GPS along with the LDIN.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches

subunit.title: Ground Based Augmentation System (GBAS) Landing System (GLS)

questions.question: GBAS provides

choices.text: glidepath database alignment for non-linear approaches.
ground-based assessment of runway and taxiing airport traffic.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. GLS는 활주로에 정확히 정렬·강하하도록 precision navigation guidance를 제공하며 GNSS에 differential augmentation을 적용한다. GBAS는 ICAO에서 LAAS를 부르는 명칭이다.
tags: Ground Based Augmentation System (GBAS) Landing System (GLS)
questions.explanation_en: The GLS provides precision navigation guidance for exact alignment and descent of aircraft on approach to a runway. It provides differential augmentation to the Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS). GBAS is the ICAO term for Local Area Augmentation System (LAAS). Answer (A) is incorrect. The LAAS was developed as an “ILS look-alike” system from the pilot perspective and provides precision guidance for exact alignment and descent of aircraft on approach to a runway. Answer (B) is incorrect. The equipment consists of a GBAS Ground Facility (GGF), four reference stations, a VHF Data Broadcast (VDB) uplink antenna, and an aircraft GBAS receiver. The system has it for approach purposes only. It does not assess ground-based runway and taxiing airport traffic.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches

subunit.title: Ground Based Augmentation System (GBAS) Landing System (GLS)

questions.question: GBAS approaches are

choices.text: automatically tuned and displayed after selection of the 3-letter procedure identifier.
flown the same as an LDA with glideslope selection and identification.
flown using the same techniques as an ILS once selected and identified.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. GLS 접근은 FMS에서 해당 5자리 GBAS channel을 선택한 뒤 chart의 RPI/approach ID와 flight deck 표시 또는 Morse audio identification을 대조해 올바른 절차가 load되었는지 확인한다. 선택·식별 후 비행기법은 ILS와 유사하다.
tags: Ground Based Augmentation System (GBAS) Landing System (GLS)
questions.explanation_en: Pilots will select the five-digit GBAS channel number of the associated approach within the Flight Management System (FMS) menu or manually select the five digits (system dependent). Following the procedure selection, confirmation that the correct LAAS procedure is loaded can be done by cross checking the charted Reference Path Indicator (RPI) or approach ID with the flight deck displayed RPI or audio identification of the RPI with Morse Code (for some systems). The pilot will fly the GLS approach using the same techniques as an ILS once selected and identified. Answer (A) is incorrect. Pilots will select the five-digit GBAS channel number, not a 3-letter procedure identifier. Answer (B) is incorrect. The pilot will fly the GLS approach using the same techniques as an ILS once selected and identified.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: IFR Navigation Equipment, Holding, and Approaches

subunit.title: Ground Based Augmentation System (GBAS) Landing System (GLS)

questions.question: (Refer to Figure 322 on page 441.) The highest terrain shown in the planview section of the LDA/DME RWY 25 approach to Eagle County Regional is
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 이 instrument approach plate에서 실제 장애물 중 가장 높은 값은 11,573 ft이며, 차트 북동쪽 IAF VOAXA 바로 위에 표시되어 있다.
tags: Ground Based Augmentation System (GBAS) Landing System (GLS)
questions.explanation_en: The highest of the values that correspond to an actual obstacle on this instrument approach plate is 11,573. It is located on the NE side of the approach plate, just above the (IAF) VOAXA. Answer (B) is incorrect. The figure 11,320 feet is lower than the obstacle found in the NE portion of the approach plate. Answer (C) is incorrect. The figure 12,200 feet is the minimum en route altitude. It can also be seen on the profile of the approach plate. The aircraft must be at or above 12,200 feet when crossing WEHAL at 15.3 DME.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 95 on page 480 and Figure 171 on page 460.) You depart the Chicago Midway airport on the Midway Nine SID. Your level-off point is on the 270° radial at 19 NM from the Gipper VORTAC. With the winds aloft forecast to be 230° at 51 knots and a magnetic variation of 1°W, what TAS should be maintained to arrive over CRL VORTAC 42 minutes after level-off?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Level-off 후 42분 뒤 CRL VORTAC에 도착하려면 먼저 필요한 groundspeed를 구한다. 거리는 19+129=148 NM이고 42분은 0.7시간이므로 GS는 약 211 kt이다. 평균 바람과 course를 E6B에 적용하면 필요한 TAS는 약 171 kt이다.
questions.explanation_en: To determine the required TAS to arrive over CRL VORTAC 42 min. after level-off, determine the required groundspeed. The distance is 19 NM (L/O to GIJ) + 129 NM (GIJ to CRL) = 148 NM. The required groundspeed is 211 kt. [148 ÷ (42/60)]. Next, compute the TAS on the wind side of your computer: 1. Set the average magnetic wind direction of 232° (231° to GIJ and 233° to CRL) under the true index, and place a pencil mark at 51 kt. (windspeed) up from the grommet. 2. Place the average MC of 086° (090° to GIJ, 082° to GIJ/CRL COP, and 087° to CRL) under the true index. 3. Slide the grid so the groundspeed of 211 kt. is under the grommet. 4. Read the TAS of 171 kt. under the pencil mark. Answer (A) is incorrect. This would be required if the wind speed were 59 kt., not 51 kt. Answer (B) is incorrect. This would be required if the wind speed were 55 kt., not 51 kt.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 95 on page 480 and Figure 171 on page 460.) In a DME equipped aircraft while on the Midway Nine departure, what action should be taken by the pilot, if communications are lost, while IMC, after takeoff on RWY 13L at Chicago Midway Airport?

choices.text: Return and land immediately at Chicago Midway Airport.
Complete initially assigned turn south of DPA R-096, maintain 3,000 feet or lower if assigned. Then 10 minutes after departure, climb to FL 190, direct to GIJ, then flight plan route.
Complete initially assigned turn within 4 DME of Midway and maintain 3,000 feet or lower, if assigned. Then 10 minutes after departure, climb to FL 190, direct to GIJ, and then flight plan route.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. IMC에서 Chicago Midway RWY 13L 이륙 후 양방향 통신이 두절되면 14 CFR 91.185에 따라 Midway Nine Departure의 통신두절 절차를 따른다. 최초 배정 선회는 4 DME 이내에 완료하고 3,000 ft 또는 더 낮게 배정된 고도를 유지한 뒤, 출발 10분 후 FL190으로 상승해 GIJ VORTAC 직행 후 filed route를 따른다.
questions.explanation_en: In the event of a two-way communication failure, ATC service will be provided on the basis that the pilot is operating in accordance with 14 CFR 91.185. If the failure occurs after takeoff on RWY 13L at Chicago Midway, while in IMC, the pilot should follow the departure route description for the Midway Nine Departure. The airplane is DME equipped. The pilot should complete the initially assigned turn within 4 DME of Midway and maintain 3,000 ft. or an assigned lower altitude. Then 10 min. after departure, (s)he should climb to FL 190, direct to GIJ VORTAC, and follow the flight plan route. Answer (A) is incorrect. To return and land immediately at Chicago Midway would mean that the pilot has also declared an emergency along with the loss of communications. A loss of communications is not an emergency in itself. Answer (B) is incorrect. A pilot would complete the initially assigned turn south of DPA R-096 if the airplane was not DME equipped. N60JB is DME equipped.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 258 on page 481.) How can the FAF on the RNAV RWY 32 approach at BUF be identified?

choices.text: The RNAV receiver will indicate 175.1° and 2.5 DME miles from BUF VORTAC.
The RNAV receiver will indicate a change from TO to FROM and 0 deflection of the course needle.
Two flashes/second on the OM beacon light.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. RNAV FAF인 DEPEW는 database, degree-distance fix 또는 위·경도 좌표로 입력할 수 있다. Waypoint 통과 시 VORTAC 통과와 비슷하게 RNAV 표시가 TO에서 FROM으로 바뀌고 course needle 편위가 없어야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: The pilot will input the FAF waypoint DEPEW from a database or by the use of degree-distance fix based on navigational aids or by latitude/longitude coordinates. The waypoint crossing is noted similar to that of crossing a VORTAC station. The RNAV receiver will indicate a change from TO to FROM, and there should be no deflection of the course needle. Answer (A) is incorrect. The waypoint is defined to the RNAV computer as 175.1° and 2.5 DME from BUF VORTAC. Answer (C) is incorrect. The OM is part of a precision approach and is a radio transmitter. An RNAV approach is a nonprecision approach, and the FAF on the RNAV RWY 32 approach to Buffalo is a waypoint.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 258 on page 481.) How can the GPS LNAV/MDA MAP for the RNAV (GPS) RWY 32 approach at Buffalo Niagara Intl (BUF) be identified?

choices.text: GPS annunciator will switch to FROM.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Waypoint를 통과하면 GPS receiver annunciator는 FROM으로 전환된다.
questions.explanation_en: The GPS receiver annunciator will switch to FROM. Answer (B) is incorrect. GPS receivers will not automatically sequence to a MAP during an approach. Answer (C) is incorrect. The point at 1.4 NM is a visual descent point (VDP) from the end of the runway.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 258 on page 481.) What is the recommended descent angle for the RNAV (GPS) RWY 32 approach?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. RNAV(GPS) RWY 32 접근절차 profile view에 공표된 descent angle은 3.00°이다.
questions.explanation_en: The profile view of the RNAV (GPS) RWY 32 instrument approach procedure indicates a descent angle of 3.00°. Answer (A) is incorrect. The profile view of the RNAV (GPS) RWY 32 instrument approach procedure indicates a descent angle of 3.00°, not 2.12°. Answer (B) is incorrect. The profile view of the RNAV (GPS) RWY 32 instrument approach procedure indicates a descent angle of 3.00°, not 2.52°.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 258 on page 481.) What is the procedure for the missed approach on the RNAV (GPS) RWY 32 approach at BUF?

choices.text: Climbing straight ahead to 3,000 feet to TOMDE while selecting the MAP mode, left turn to 239° track to SUSKE and hold.
Climb to 3,500 feet and hold at SUSKE on the 239° track from TOMDE.
Select MAP mode, climb to 3,000 feet and hold using left turns at SUSKE on the 239° track from TOMDE.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. GPS는 missed approach를 자동 sequence하지 않으므로 수동으로 활성화해야 한다. 3,000 ft까지 직진상승해 TOMDE로 가는 동안 MAP mode를 선택하고, TOMDE 도착 후 R-239를 따라 SUSKE로 진행하는 holding 절차를 수행한다.
questions.explanation_en: The GPS will not automatically cycle to the missed approach procedure. Instead, it has to be manually sequenced. While climbing straight ahead to 3,000 ft. to TOMDE, manually select the MAP mode and hold once arrived at TOMDE track R-239 to SUSKE. Answer (B) is incorrect. The proper altitude is 3,000 ft., not 3,500 ft., as indicated in the missed approach instructions. Answer (C) is incorrect. The holding pattern at SUSKE is right turns, not left turns, as indicated by the arrows on the MAP hold position.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 360 on page 482.) Greater Buffalo Intl was closed upon N60JB’s arrival and was not expected to be open for 4 hours, for snow removal. N60JB received clearance to ROC. Upon arrival at ROC, the flight was cleared for the ILS RWY 28. To fly the ILS RWY 28 at ROC, the aircraft must have the following navigation equipment:

choices.text: Radar and VOR, localizer, glideslope, and DME.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Fig. 360의 ROC ILS or LOC RWY 28 접근에서 ILS RWY 28을 비행하려면 VOR/ILS 장비가 필요하다.
questions.explanation_en: Fig. 360 is the ILS or LOC RWY 28 IAP at ROC. To fly the ILS RWY 28 approach, you must have a VOR/ILS. Answer (A) is incorrect. Radar and DME are not required to fly the ILS RWY 28 approach. Answer (C) is incorrect. A VOR with a glide slope indicator, not a radar or DME, are required to fly the ILS RWY 28 approach.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 360 on page 482 and Figure 388 on page 483.) N60JB desired to list ROC as an alternate for BUF. The active RWY at ROC was expected to be RWY 28. What weather forecast was required at Greater Rochester Intl, for N60JB to list it as an alternate?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Fig. 388에서 ROC ILS RWY 28의 Cat A/B/C alternate minimum은 800-2이다. LOC RWY 28에는 별도 비표준 minimum이 없으므로 standard nonprecision alternate minimum인 800-2가 적용되어, precision과 nonprecision 모두 alternate 계획 기준은 800-2이다.
questions.explanation_en: Fig. 388 lists the alternate minimums for Rochester, NY (ROC). For the ILS RWY 28 (precision approach), the alternate minimums for Cat. A, B, and C aircraft are 800-2. Standard alternate minimums of 800-2 for nonprecision approach can be used since there is no listing for the LOC RWY 28 at ROC for A, B, or C aircraft. Thus, to list ROC as an alternate, the weather forecast must be 800-2 for both precision and nonprecision approaches. Answer (B) is incorrect. While 600-2 are the standard alternate minimums for a precision approach, ROC has nonstandard alternate minimums for the ILS RWY 28, which is 800-2 for Cat. A, B, and C aircraft. Answer (C) is incorrect. While 600-2 are the standard alternate minimums for a precision approach, ROC has nonstandard alternate minimums for the ILS RWY 28, which is 800-2 for Cat. A, B, and C aircraft. Since LOC RWY 28 is not listed for A, B, or C aircraft, the standard alternate minimums of 800-2, not 800-2 1/4, can be used.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 360 on page 482 and Figure 388 on page 483.) An air carrier needs to list ROC as an alternate for a flight to BUF in a category C aircraft. The active RWY at ROC was expected to be RWY 28. What weather forecast is required at Greater Rochester Intl for the air carrier to list it as an alternate? This air carrier’s policy is not to use localizer approaches for alternate planning purposes.
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 접근판의 비표준 alternate 표시를 따라 Fig. 388을 확인하면 ILS RWY 28 Cat C는 800-2이다. 문제에서 localizer 접근을 alternate 계획에 사용하지 말라고 했으므로 RNAV(GPS) RWY 28을 봐야 하며 Cat C minimum은 800-2 1/4이다.
questions.explanation_en: The instrument approach plate has the nonstandard alternate minimums triangle “A” on it. Look at the IFR Alternate Minimums page in Fig. 388 to determine the alternate minimums. Note 2 under Rochester, NY, applies to the ILS RWY 28. The ILS for CAT C aircraft requires 800-2 to be used as an alternate. The question states not to use localizer approaches for alternate planning purposes, so we have to look at RNAV (GPS) Rwy 28 alternate minimums in Fig. 388. Refer to note 4, that indicates CAT C minimums are 800-2 1/4. Answer (A) is incorrect. There are no minimums listed on any of the referenced charts. Answer (B) is incorrect. There are standard alternate minimums. The A in the black triangle at top left of the approach plate indicates that the minimums are nonstandard.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 101 on page 485 and Figure 101A on page 486.) Which frequency should be selected to check airport conditions and weather prior to departure at DFW Intl?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Fig. 101A Dallas-Ft. Worth Chart Supplement의 Communications에 따르면 출발 항공기용 ATIS 주파수는 135.925 MHz이다.
questions.explanation_en: The Automatic Terminal Information Service (ATIS) provides airport noncontrol and weather information. The Chart Supplement on Fig. 101A for Dallas-Ft. Worth lists the ATIS frequencies under Communications. The ATIS frequency for departing airplanes is 135.925 MHz. Answer (A) is incorrect. This is the Maverick VOR/DME. Answer (B) is incorrect. This is the listed ATIS frequency for arriving, not departing, airplanes.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 99 on page 450, Figure 100 on page 451, Figure 101 on page 485, Figure 102 on page 487, and Figure 102A on page 488.) The frequency change from ARTCC in the Navasota VORTAC area to the IAH Approach control after departing DFW Intl for IAH is expected to be
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Fig. 102A에서 서쪽에서 도착하는 항공기의 regional approach control 주파수는 124.35 MHz이다. Fig. 100의 Houston College Station ARTCC remote site 주파수는 128.075 MHz이다.
questions.explanation_en: The approach control frequency is listed in the Chart Supplement on Fig. 102A under Communications. The regional approach control frequency for a flight arriving from the west is 124.35. The ARTCC frequency is found on Fig. 100 above the symbol “4.” It is in a jagged-edged box that identifies that it is an ARTCC remote site with the discrete VHF and UHF frequencies. This is Houston College Station on 128.075 MHz. Answer (A) is incorrect. The ARTCC frequency southwest of Navasota is 132.15. Answer (B) is incorrect. The approach control frequency for west arriving traffic is 124.35 MHz.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 100 on page 451.) (Refer to area 8.) Where is the VOR changeover point on V571 between Navasota (TNV) and Humble (IAH)?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. V571에서 TNV와 IAH 사이 changeover point는 TNV에서 18 NM, IAH에서 24 NM 지점이다.
questions.explanation_en: When the COP is not located at the midway point, the chart will depict the COP location on the airway and give the mileage to the radio aids. Looking at V571 between TNV and IAH, the changeover point is 18 miles from TNV and 24 miles from IAH. Answer (B) is incorrect. The VOR changeover point is 24 miles from IAH and 18 miles from TNV. Answer (C) is incorrect. A VOR changeover point will be halfway between two navigation aids only when a specific point is not depicted on the airway.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 100 on page 451 and Figure 262 on page 489.) How should the pilot identify the position to leave V369 for the RIICE THREE Arrival?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. BILEE transition에서는 BILEE INT에서 TNV R-334를 따라 HOMRN으로, 이어 IAH R-313을 intercept한 후 inbound로 RIICE intersection까지 진행하여 Rice Three Arrival에 진입한다.
questions.explanation_en: The BILEE transition indicates that from BILEE INT the pilot should maintain the R-334 of TNV VORTAC to HOMRN and the R-313 of IAH, then intercept and track inbound on the R-313 of IAH VORTAC to RIICE intersection for the Rice Three Arrival. Answer (B) is incorrect. There is no DME fix for 21 NM from TNV VORTAC on either the STAR or the IFR En Route Chart. Answer (C) is incorrect. A pilot should have changed over to TNV VORTAC, and there is no 141 DME fix from DFW on V369.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 101 below, Figure 101A on page 486, Figure 102 on page 487, and Figure 102A on page 488.) What is the magnetic variation at DFW Intl and IAH?

choices.text: 06 E at DFW and 05E at IAH.
06 W at DFW and 05W at IAH. Figure 101. Cha

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Magnetic variation은 DFW Intl.과 IAH 각각의 VORTAC information line 끝에서 확인할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: The magnetic variation is found at the end of the VORTAC information line for both DFW Intl. and IAH. Answer (B) is incorrect. Zero degrees magnetic variation is the Agonic line, the line where the variation between magnetic and true north is zero, which is well east of Texas. Answer (C) is incorrect. The magnetic variation is 06°E (not west). rt Supplement.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: At a cruising altitude of FL 220, the winds are forecast to be 280° at 46 kts with an outside temperature of ISA –3°. What IAS should be used to maintain a filed TAS of 233 kts at the proposed altitude?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. FL220의 ISA 온도는 15-(22×2)=-29°C이고 ISA-3이므로 OAT는 -32°C이다. E6B에서 pressure altitude 22,000 ft와 -32°C를 맞추면 TAS 233 kt에 대응하는 IAS는 약 167 KIAS이다.
questions.explanation_en: The temperature is indicated as ISA –3, which is International Standard Atmosphere temperature –3°C. The ISA temperature for FL 220 is calculated by subtracting the standard lapse rate (2°C/1,000 ft.) from standard sea-level temperature of 15°C. The OAT is –32°C [15 – (22 × 2) –3]. In the center of the computer side of the flight computer, on the right side, put the air temperature of –32°C over the pressure altitude of 22,000 ft. On the outer scale, find TAS of 233 kt., which is over indicated airspeed (IAS) on the inner scale of 167 KIAS. Answer (A) is incorrect. This will maintain the fixed TAS if the OAT is –3°C, not –32°C. Answer (C) is incorrect. This will maintain the fixed TAS if the OAT is –50°C, not –32°C.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 348 on page 500.) What effect on the takeoff run can be expected on RWY 11R at Tucson Intl?

choices.text: Takeoff length shortened to 6,986 feet by displaced threshold.
Takeoff run shortened by 0.7 percent runway slope to the SE.
Takeoff run will be lengthened by the 0.7 percent upslope of the runway.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Fig. 348 RWY 11R-29L 정보의 '0.7% up'은 0.7% uphill slope를 뜻하며, 이륙 활주거리를 증가시킨다.
questions.explanation_en: The first line of runway information provides information common to the entire runway. At the end of RWY 11R-29L on Fig. 348, the information states, “0.7% up.” That indicates there is a 0.7% upslope grade on the runway, which will increase the distance required for the takeoff run. Answer (A) is incorrect. A displaced threshold will shorten the usable runway for landing, not for takeoff. Answer (B) is incorrect. The takeoff run is lengthened, not shortened, due to the 0.7% upslope.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 348 on page 500.) How can the pilot receive the latest NOTAM’s for the TUS-LAX flight?

choices.text: Request ADCUS on any FSS or Tower frequency.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 최신 NOTAM은 FSS에 직접, 전화 또는 무전으로 문의할 수 있다. TUS-LAX 구간의 최신 정보를 위해 Fig. 348에 기재된 FSS 주파수 122.2 MHz를 사용할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Pilots can receive the latest NOTAMs for their flight by contacting the nearest FSS in person, telephoning, or contacting on radio. For the latest information from TUS-LAX, the pilot should contact FSS on 122.2 MHz, as listed in the Chart Supplement on Fig. 348. Answer (A) is incorrect. ATIS provides noncontrol airport traffic and weather information, not NOTAMs. Answer (C) is incorrect. ADCUS means to “advise customs” of an international flight and is handled by an FSS, not by a tower.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 348 on page 500.) What distance is available for takeoff on RWY 11R at Tucson Intl?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Fig. 348에서 RWY 11R-29L의 활주로 길이는 8,408 ft이며, 이는 RWY 11R 이륙에 이용 가능한 거리이다.
questions.explanation_en: Runway information is shown on two lines. Information common to the entire runway is shown on the first line while information concerning the runway ends is shown on the second or following line. On Fig. 348, the runway length of RWY 11R-29L is 8,408 ft., which is the distance available for takeoff on RWY 11R. Answer (A) is incorrect. This is the length of RWY 03-21. Answer (C) is incorrect. This is the length of RWY 11L, not RWY 11R.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 348 on page 500 and Figure 361 on page 501.) Determine the DEP CON frequency for the TUS7.TUS SID after takeoff from RWY 11R at Tucson Intl.
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. TUS7.TUS SID에서 TUS R-280 outbound를 비행한다. RWY 11R 이륙 후 heading 280°에서 사용할 Departure Control 주파수는 125.1 MHz이다.
questions.explanation_en: In the TUS7.TUS SID, the pilot would track outbound on the R-280 from TUS. The Communications section of the Chart Supplement indicates that DEP CON frequency after takeoff from RWY 11R and heading 280° is 125.1 MHz. Answer (B) is incorrect. This is for departures from RWY 11 with a departure heading between 286° to 089°. Answer (C) is incorrect. This is for departures from RWY 29 with a departure heading between 066° to 274°.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 361 on page 501.) If communications are lost soon after takeoff on RWY 11R at Tucson Intl, what altitude restrictions apply in IMC conditions?

choices.text: Fly assigned heading for vectors to intercept appropriate transition, maintain 17,000 feet to GBN, then climb to assigned altitude.
Fly direct to the Tuscon VORTAC; climb to 17,000 feet; 10 minutes after departure, climb to assigned altitude.
Fly assigned heading for vectors to intercept the Gila Bend transition; climb to 17,000 feet; 10 minutes after departure, climb to FL 220.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. IMC에서 TUS RWY 11R 이륙 직후 통신두절이면 Tucson Seven Departure의 통신두절 절차를 따른다. Tucson VORTAC 직행, 17,000 ft 유지, 출발 10분 후 배정고도로 상승한다.
questions.explanation_en: If communications are lost soon after takeoff on RWY 11R at TUS in IMC conditions, the Tucson Seven Departure as described in Fig. 361 must be flown. Fly direct to the Tuscon VORTAC. Climb to maintain 17,000 ft. Next, climb to assigned altitude 10 min. after departure. Answer (A) is incorrect. The pilot must maintain 17,000 ft. and can climb to assigned altitude 10 min. after departure, not only after reaching GBN VORTAC. Answer (C) is incorrect. The pilot must fly direct to the TUSCON VORTAC and must climb to maintain 17,000 ft.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 361 on page 501.) What are the takeoff minimums for RWY 11R at Tucson Intl that apply to N91JB with a planned climb rate of 1,000 feet per minute at 140 knots?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. GS 140 kt는 분당 2.33 NM이므로 1,000 fpm 상승은 약 429 ft/NM이다. 이는 요구 400 ft/NM보다 크므로 standard departure minimum을 사용할 수 있다. 2발 BE-1900의 standard takeoff visibility는 1 SM이다.
questions.explanation_en: At a climbing rate of 140 kt. groundspeed (GS), the aircraft would cover 2.33 NM per minute (140 kt. ÷ 60 = 2.33 NM per minute). Climbing 1,000 feet each minute would be 429 feet per NM (1,000 ÷ 2.33 = 429.2 feet per NM). In Fig. 361, two sets of takeoff minimums are listed. Both allow use of standard departure weather minimums if you have a high enough climb gradient. The aircraft would require 400 feet per NM to use the standard departure minimums. The other takeoff minimum listed is climbing at 429 feet per NM. The standard minimums can be used for all of the runways. The standard minimums for aircraft is 1 SM, other than helicopters, having two engines or less. The BE-1900 has two engines. Answer (B) is incorrect. The Federal Aviation Regulations indicate the standard minimums of 1 SM for aircraft, other than helicopters, having two engines or less. Answer (C) is incorrect. The Federal Aviation Regulations indicate the standard minimums of 1 SM for aircraft, other than helicopters, having two engines or less.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 302 on page 499.) Flight 61 is a 14 CFR Part 121 carrier passenger turbojet aircraft planning to depart Lewiston-Nez County airport on RWY 30 using the POTOR TWO departure. There are no abnormal company policies or procedures. With 180 knots groundspeed, what takeoff conditions are required to depart?

choices.text: 300 feet per minute climb with both engines operative.
750 feet per minute climb with 1 engine operative.
900 feet per minute climb with 1 engine operative.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. POTOR TWO에서 RWY 26/30의 요구 climb gradient는 4,700 ft까지 300 ft/NM이다. GS 180 kt는 분당 3 NM이므로 필요한 상승률은 3×300=900 fpm이다.
questions.explanation_en: Refer to the note in Fig. 302 for the POTOR TWO departure. For RWY 26 and 30, the required climb gradient is 300 feet per NM to 4,700 feet. In parentheses, the equivalent climb rates can be seen in feet per minute (fpm) for speeds of 150 kts. (750 fpm) and 200 kts. (1,000 fpm). The aircraft is climbing at 180 kts. groundspeed and the fpm climb for that ground speed is not given, but it can be calculated. (180 kts. ÷ 60) = 3 miles covered per minute (The aircraft must climb at least 300 feet for every NM); 3 NM per minute × 300 feet per NM = 900 feet per minute. Answer (A) is incorrect. The climb must be a minimum of 300 feet per NM, not 300 feet per minute. Answer (B) is incorrect. The takeoff condition of 750 fpm is at 150 kts., not 180 knots.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 271 on page 498 and Legend 72 on page 502.) For a takeoff from Runway 25L at LAX, what is the minimum climb gradient that ATC expects the aircraft to maintain?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Fig. 271 RWY 25L의 takeoff minimum은 standard이다. 별도 요구가 없으면 ATC는 minimum IFR altitude에 도달할 때까지 최소 200 ft/NM의 climb gradient를 기대한다.
questions.explanation_en: Note that the Take-Off Minimums for runway 25L at the top of Fig. 271 are listed as standard. For standard procedures, ATC expects a minimum climb gradient of 200 ft./NM, unless required to level off by a crossing restriction, until the minimum IFR altitude is reached. Answer (A) is incorrect. The standard departure procedure requires a minimum climb gradient of 200 ft./NM. Without knowing the speed of the climb, it cannot be determined whether 500 fpm would comply with the minimum requirements. Answer (C) is incorrect. A climb gradient of 400 ft./NM is required for standard takeoff minimums to be used on Runway 6R, not 25L.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 255A on page 494 and Figure 257A on page 496.) Which approach control frequency is indicated for the TNP.DOWNE4 Arrival with LAX as the destination?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. DOWNE4 Arrival Fig. 255A의 북서쪽에 표시된 approach control 주파수는 124.05 MHz이다.
questions.explanation_en: The DOWNE4 Arrival on Fig. 255A indicates in the northwest corner of the chart the approach control and ATIS frequencies for the arrival. The approach control frequency is 124.05 MHz. Answer (A) is incorrect. This frequency is used for arrivals from 045° to 089°, which are not on the DOWNE4 Arrival. Answer (B) is incorrect. This frequency is used for arrivals from 090° to 224°, which are not on the DOWNE4 Arrival.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 255A on page 494 and Figure 257A on page 496.) At what point does the flight enter the final approach phase of the ILS RWY 25L at LAX?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Precision approach의 final approach phase는 glide slope intercept에서 시작하며, 이 지점이 precision approach의 FAF이다.
questions.explanation_en: The final approach phase for a precision approach begins with the intercept of the glide slope, at which time a descent may begin on the glide slope to the decision height. Thus, for a precision approach, the final approach fix is the intercept of the glide slope. Answer (A) is incorrect. LUVYN INT is an initial approach fix (IAF) and does not mark the point at which the flight enters the final approach phase. Answer (B) is incorrect. LIMMA INT is a fix at which the pilot should intercept the glide slope, but the intersection itself does not mark the point at which the airplane enters the final approach phase.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 255A on page 494 and Figure 257B on page 497.) The radio altimeter indication at the DA on the ILS RWY 24R approach at LAX is
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. ILS RWY 24R 접근의 minima section에서 DA에 해당하는 radio altimeter 값은 RA 115 ft이다.
questions.explanation_en: The radio altimeter indication at the DA on the ILS RWY 24R approach is indicated by “RA” followed by the appropriate indication within parentheses in the minima section. In this approach, the RA is 115 ft. Answer (A) is incorrect. The touchdown zone elevation (TDZE) is 120 ft. Answer (C) is incorrect. The decision altitude, expressed in MSL, is 220 ft.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 255A on page 494 and Figure 257A on page 496.) If the glide slope indication is lost upon passing HUNDA INT on the ILS RWY 25L approach at LAX, what action should the pilot take?

choices.text: Continue the approach as an LOC, and add 242 feet to the DH.
Immediately start the missed approach direct to CATLY INT.
Continue the approach as a LOC approach and add 1/2 mile to the visibility requirements and 242 feet to the decision height.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. LOC approach minimum이 별도로 공표되어 있으므로 ILS 관련 구성요소 불능 시 LOC 접근으로 계속할 수 있고 minimum은 242 ft만큼 증가한다.
questions.explanation_en: Because minimums are shown for an LOC approach, the pilot can continue and increase minimums by 242 feet. Answer (B) is incorrect. The approach can continue as an LOC approach. Answer (C) is incorrect. An increase in visibility is only required for Category C or D aircraft. The BE-1900 is a Category B aircraft.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 255A on page 494 and Figure 257A on page 496.) How can GAATE INT be identified?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Fig. 257A의 GAATE intersection은 I-LAX에서 17.2 DME인 DME fix이다. ILS와 함께 설치된 DME로 localizer course상의 fix를 정의하며, 대안으로 controller가 RADAR fix를 제공할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Refer to Fig. 257A. GAATE intersection is a DME fix which is 17.2 DME from I-LAX. The DME is installed with the ILS and established fixes on the localizer course. ILS is identified by three letters preceded by the letter “I.” An alternative to the DME fix is a RADAR fix provided by controllers. Answer (B) is incorrect. LAX 17.2 DME defines a circle, not an intersection. Answer (C) is incorrect. LAX R-249 and SLI R-327 do not intersect. GAATE INT can be identified by LAX R-069 and SLI R-338.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 257A on page 496.) How should the IFR flight plan be closed upon landing at LAX?

choices.text: LAX tower will close it automatically.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 운영 중인 관제탑이 있는 공항에 IFR로 착륙하면 비행계획은 자동 종료된다. 따라서 LAX Tower가 IFR flight plan을 자동으로 close한다.
questions.explanation_en: When operating on an IFR flight plan to an airport with a functioning control tower, the flight plan is automatically closed upon landing. In this case, LAX tower will close the IFR flight plan automatically. Answer (A) is incorrect. An IFR flight plan is closed with a flight service station only if there is no operating tower. Answer (B) is incorrect. An IFR flight plan is closed with an FSS only if there is no operating tower.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 256 on page 495 and Figure 257A on page 496.) What approach lights are available for the ILS RWY 25L approach at LAX?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Chart Supplement의 RWY 07R-25L 정보에서 RWY 25L의 'ALSF2'는 sequenced flashing lights가 포함된 고강도 접근등화, Category II 구성임을 뜻한다.
questions.explanation_en: Refer to the Chart Supplement excerpt and locate the runway data for RWY 07R-25L. The first line has information common to the runway. The second line contains specific information about the runway ends. RWY 25L indicates “ALSF2,” which translates to high-intensity approach lighting system with sequenced flashing lights, Category II configuration. Answer (B) is incorrect. RWY 25R has an MALSR and a displaced threshold. Answer (C) is incorrect. High-intensity runway lights (HIRL), touchdown zone lights (TDZ), and centerline lights (CL) are runway, not approach, lighting systems.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 257B on page 497.) What is the DH for the ILS RWY 24R CAT II at LAX if the pilot has completed initial CAT II certification within the preceding 6 months, but has flown no CAT II approaches?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Cat II ILS 제한으로 DH 150 ft 이상이 요구된다. Fig. 257B의 공표 minimum은 RA 115/DH 100/DA 220이므로 DH에 50 ft를 더해 새 minimum은 RA 165, DA 270 ft가 된다.
questions.explanation_en: A pilot is restricted to a 150 foot decision height until the CAT II ILS limitation is removed. Refer to Fig. 257B. The published minimums are a Radar Altimeter height (RA) of 115 feet which corresponds to a decision height (DH) of 100 feet, and a decision altitude (DA) of 220 feet. A 100 feet DH is too low to meet the CAT II ILS limitation of 150 feet. Fifty additional feet must be added, requiring new minimums that would be RA 165 and a DA of 270 feet. Answer (A) is incorrect. RA 115 / 220 feet are the minimums for a pilot without a CAT II ILS limitation. Answer (C) is incorrect. This answer is higher than the limitations set forth in the regulations for this CAT II ILS approach.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 354 on page 508.) What action should be taken by the pilot if communications are lost after departure from RWY 16 at PWK if VMC?

choices.text: Continue the flight under VMC and land as soon as practicable.
Climb to 3,000 feet; after 3 minutes, turn direct to PMM and climb to FL 190.
Start right turn within 1 mile of the departure end of RWY, remain east of ORD VOR/DME R-345, and maintain 3,000 feet; 3 minutes after departure, turn direct to PMM, and climb to FL 190.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 양방향 무선통신 고장이 VMC에서 발생하면 VFR로 계속 비행하여 가능한 한 빨리 착륙해야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: If two-way radio communication failure occurs in VMC, the pilot should continue the flight under VFR and land as soon as practicable. Answer (B) is incorrect. If radio communication failure occurs while in, or when encountering, VMC, the pilot must continue the flight under VFR and land as soon as practicable. Answer (C) is incorrect. While the pilot should follow the SID instructions to ensure separation from approaches to RWY 14R at O’Hare, the pilot must continue the flight under VFR. The pilot should follow the routing and altitude restrictions if communications are lost in IMC, not VMC.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 354 on page 508.) The PIC of PTZ 70 will use 25° of bank during the turn after departing RWY 16 at PWK. What is the maximum TAS that the aircraft may maintain during the turn and remain east of the ORD VOR/DME R-345 under a no wind condition?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Pal-Waukee Two Departure의 표에서 25° bank에 허용되는 최대 TAS는 162 kt이다.
questions.explanation_en: The table at the top of the Pal-Waukee Two Departure (Fig. 354) provides the maximum TAS for a given bank angle required during the turn after takeoff to remain east of the ORD VOR/DME R-345 under a no wind condition. Under a bank angle of 25° is the maximum TAS of 162 kt. Answer (A) is incorrect. This would be the maximum TAS if you were to use a bank angle of slightly less than 25°, not 25°. Answer (C) is incorrect. This would be the maximum TAS if you were to use a bank angle slightly greater than 25°, not 25°.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 354 on page 508.) To remain east of the ORD VOR/DME R-345, while flying the PAL-WAUKEE TWO DEPARTURE, requires a turn radius of
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. RWY 16 이륙 후 ORD VOR/DME R-345 동쪽에 머물기 위해서는 turn radius가 5,000 ft 미만이어야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: To remain east of the ORD VOR/DME R-345 while flying the Pal-Waukee Two Departure after a takeoff on RWY 16 requires a turn radius of less than 5,000 ft. This information is found as a note on the left side of the chart, above the departure route description. Answer (A) is incorrect. A turn radius of less than 5,000 ft., not over 5,000 ft., is required by the SID. Answer (B) is incorrect. A turn radius of less than 5,000 ft., not 5,000 ft., is required by the SID.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 354 on page 508.) What action should be taken by the PIC of PTZ 70 if the communication radios fail after takeoff from RWY 16 at PWK while in IMC conditions?

choices.text: Climb to 3,000 feet on RWY heading; after 3 minutes, turn direct to PMM and climb to FL 190.

Start right turn within 1 mile of the departure end of RWY 16 and remain east of the 345 radial of the ORD VOR/DME while climbing to 3,000 feet; after 3 minutes, turn direct to PMM and climb to FL 190.
Set 7600 in Mode 3 of the transponder, turn direct to Northbrook (the IAF), climb to 2,700 feet, and fly the ILS RWY 16 to land at PWK.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. IMC에서 PWK RWY 16 이륙 후 Pal-Waukee Two Departure 중 통신두절이면 SID narrative를 따른다. RWY 16 departure end에서 1 NM 이내에 우선회를 시작해 ORD R-345 동쪽을 유지하며 3,000 ft 또는 배정고도로 상승한 뒤 filed route로 진행한다.
questions.explanation_en: If radio communication failure occurs after takeoff from RWY 16 at PWK while in IMC and the pilot has been cleared for the Pal-Waukee Two Departure, (s)he should fly the SID as described in the narrative. Thus, the pilot should start a right turn within 1 NM of the departure end of RWY 16 to remain east of the ORD VOR/DME R-345 while climbing to 3,000 ft. or assigned altitude. Then, proceed as filed. Answer (A) is incorrect. When departing RWY 16, the pilot must make a right turn within 1 NM of the departure end, not maintain runway heading. Answer (C) is incorrect. While the pilot would squawk 7600, the routing clearance is the Pal-Waukee Two Departure, not a direct turn to OBK VORTAC to execute the ILS RWY 16 approach to land at PWK.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 354 on page 508.) To remain east of the ORD VOR/DME R-345, while flying the PAL-WAUKEE TWO DEPARTURE, in an aircraft flying at 140 kts TAS in the climb in calm winds, requires a bank angle of

choices.text: about standard rate no matter what the winds are.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Fig. 354의 No Wind Bank Angle 표에서 TAS 140 kt는 122 kt/15°와 143 kt/20° 사이를 보간하면 약 19.3°이므로 가장 가까운 값은 20°이다.
questions.explanation_en: Referring to Fig. 354, in the upper right hand corner, there is a No Wind Bank Angle chart for 122 KTS and 143 KTS. Interpolating for 140 KTS TAS would be 19.286°. The closest answer would be 20°. It is just as easy to look at this chart and notice that 140 KTS TAS is closer to 143 KTS TAS at 20° than it is to 122 KTS TAS at 15°. Answer (B) is incorrect. This is obviously false since a strong enough wind from the east would blow the aircraft past the R-345 radial even at a 45° bank. Answer (C) is incorrect. The 25° section in the chart is for an airspeed of 162 KTS. This is well over the airspeed of 140 KTS TAS that is given in the question.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 301 on page 507.) The PIC (single pilot 135 with A/P) of PTZ 70 has less than 100 hours of PIC time in the BE 1900. Due to BUF weather being 100 feet, 1/4 mile in blowing snow, which is below landing minimums, the PIC requested and received clearance to SYR, the filed alternate. Under Part 135, what are the PIC’s minimums at SYR for the ILS RWY 10?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 14 CFR 135.225에 따라 해당 터빈항공기 형식에서 PIC 100시간 미만이면 MDA/DH에 100 ft, visibility에 1/2 SM 또는 RVR 2,400 ft를 추가한다. Autopilot 사용으로 visibility가 RVR 1800까지 완화되는 조건을 반영하면 SYR ILS RWY 10 PIC minimum은 719/42이다.
questions.explanation_en: 14 CFR 135.225 requires that, if the PIC has less than 100 hr. of PIC time in that type of turbine-powered airplane (i.e., BE 1900), the MDA or DH is increased by 100 ft., and the visibility is increased 1/2 SM (or 2,400 ft. RVR). The use of an autopilot reduces the approach visibility requirement to 1800 RVR, as noted in the pilot briefing information. Thus, the PIC’s minimums at SYR for the straight-in ILS RWY 10 approach are 719/42. Answer (A) is incorrect. This answer provides the straight-in DH as published on the approach chart, not the appropriate DH for a PIC with less than 100 hr. of PIC time. Answer (C) is incorrect. These are the standard alternate weather minimums for selecting an airport as an alternate with a nonprecision approach, not the actual minimums when conducting the approach at the alternate airport.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 301 on page 507 and Legend 72 on page 510.) During the approach (ILS RWY 10 at SYR) while maintaining an on glide slope indication with a groundspeed of 110 knots, what was the approximate rate of descent for PTZ 70?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. SYR ILS RWY 10의 glide slope는 3°. GS 110 kt에서 3° 경로를 유지하는 강하율은 표의 90 kt=478 fpm, 120 kt=637 fpm 사이를 보간해 약 585 fpm이다.
questions.explanation_en: Fig. 301 provides the IAP chart for the ILS RWY 10 approach at SYR. In the lower left corner of the profile view is GS 3.00°, or a 3° glide slope. Refer to the Rate of Climb/Descent Table in Legend 72 to determine the rate of descent to maintain a 3° glide slope with a groundspeed of 110 kt. Since a groundspeed of 110 kt. is not shown on the table, it must be interpolated. Find 3° in the Climb/Descent Angle column, and move right to a groundspeed of 90 kt. to determine a rate of descent of 478 fpm. For a groundspeed of 120 kt., the rate of descent is 637 fpm. Interpolate for 110 kt. to determine a rate of descent of approximately 585 fpm. Answer (A) is incorrect. This is the approximate rate of descent with a groundspeed of 110 kt. while maintaining a 2.5°, not 3°, glide slope. Answer (C) is incorrect. This is the approximate rate of descent with a groundspeed of 110 kt. while maintaining a 3.5°, not 3°, glide slope.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 279 on page 506 and Legend 72 on page 510.) To maintain glide slope on the ILS 32R approach at 120 knots, what is the approximate rate of descent required if the aircraft is experiencing a 15 knot direct headwind?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. ORD ILS/LOC RWY 32R에서 3° glide slope, TAS 120 kt와 15 kt headwind이면 GS는 105 kt이다. 3° 표를 보간하면 필요한 강하율은 약 558 fpm이다.
questions.explanation_en: Fig. 279 provides the IAP chart for the ILS/LOC RWY 32R approach at ORD. In the top right corner of the profile view is GS 3.00°, or a 3° glide slope. Refer to the Rate of Climb/Descent Table in Legend 72 to determine the rate of descent to maintain a 3° glide slope with a groundspeed of 105 kt. (120 kt. – 15 kt. headwind). Because a groundspeed of 105 kt. is not shown on the table, it must be interpolated. Find 3° in the Climb/Descent Angle Column, and move right to a groundspeed of 90 kt. to determine a rate of descent of 478 fpm. For a groundspeed of 120 kt., the rate of descent is 637 fpm. Interpolate for 105 kt. to determine a rate of descent of approximately 558 fpm. Answer (A) is incorrect. The profile view of the chart shows that the glide slope angle is 3°, and that angle should be used on the Rate of Climb/Descent Table. Answer (B) is incorrect. The amount of 637 fpm is the descent rate if the groundspeed is 120 kt. In this scenario, there is a 15 kt. headwind, which means the groundspeed is actually 105 kt.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 171 on page 460.) While proceeding on J547 from PMM to FNT with winds aloft of 020° at 61 kts, what TAS should PTZ 70 maintain to arrive at FNT 30 minutes after passing PMM?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. PMM에서 FNT까지 109 NM을 30분에 비행하려면 GS 218 kt가 필요하다. 바람 023°/61 kt와 MC 075°를 E6B에 적용하면 필요한 TAS는 약 260 kt이다.
questions.explanation_en: To determine the required TAS to arrive at FNT 30 min. after passing PMM, find the required groundspeed. The distance is 109 NM; thus, the groundspeed required is 218 kt. (109 NM ÷ 0.5 hr.). Next, compute the TAS on the wind side of the computer: 1. Set the magnetic wind direction of 023° under the true index, and place a pencil mark at 61 kt. (windspeed) up from the grommet. 2. Place the average MC of 075° (J547) under the true index. 3. Slide the grid so the groundspeed of 218 kt. is under the grommet. 4. Read the TAS of 260 kt. under the pencil mark. Answer (A) is incorrect. A TAS of 255 kt. would complete the trip from PMM to FNT in approximately 31 min., not 30 min. Answer (B) is incorrect. A TAS of 265 kt. would complete the trip from PMM to FNT in approximately 29 min., not 30 min.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 171 on page 460 and Legend 55 on page 509.) The facility (Kankakee) that is located 9 miles NE of Chicago Midway or 27 miles SSE of Northbrook (OBK) is a/an

choices.text: Automated Weather Observing System (AWOS/ASOS) with frequency.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. OBK VORTAC 남동쪽의 Kankakee 시설은 FSS Remote Communications Outlet(RCO)이다.
questions.explanation_en: The facility labeled Kankakee that is located southeast of OBK VORTAC is an FSS remote communications outlet (RCO). Answer (A) is incorrect. ARINC transmitter/frequencies are not shown on en route charts. Answer (B) is incorrect. AWOS/ ASOS frequencies are not shown on high-altitude en route charts.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 310 on page 514.) EAB 90 is a CAT B aircraft and received a clearance to fly the LOC RWY 09L approach, to circle to land RWY 27R. The LANDI fix was received. What are the minimums?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. PHL ILS RWY 9L의 LANDI fix circling minimum에서 Category B는 640-1이다.
questions.explanation_en: Fig. 310 is the ILS RWY 9L IAP at PHL. The LANDI fix minimums for circling are listed in the lower window of the profile section. For a Cat. B aircraft that received the LANDI fix, the circling minimums are 640-1. Answer (A) is incorrect. These are the circling minimums with the LANDI fix received for a Cat. A, not Cat. B, aircraft. Answer (C) is incorrect. These are the circling minimums without, not with, the LANDI fix identified.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 310 on page 514.) EAB 90 is a CAT B aircraft and received a clearance to fly the LOC RWY 09L, to land RWY 09L. The LANDI fix was received. What are the minimums?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. PHL LOC RWY 09L straight-in에서 LANDI fix를 받은 Category B 항공기의 S-LOC 9L minimum은 440/24이다.
questions.explanation_en: Fig. 310 is the ILS RWY 9L IAP at PHL. The LANDI fix minimums are located in the lower section of the profile view section. A clearance to fly the LOC RWY 09L, to land RWY 09L, means a straight-in approach. For a Cat. B aircraft that received the LANDI fix, the S-LOC 9L minimums are 440/24. Answer (B) is incorrect. The MDA for a S-LOC 9L approach with the LANDI fix received is 440 ft., not 500 ft. Answer (C) is incorrect. These are the minimums without, not with, the LANDI fix received for a S-LOC 9L approach.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 310 on page 514.) The PIC on EAB 90 has not flown 100 hours as PIC in the BE 1900 (CAT B aircraft). What are the minimums for the PIC when flying the ILS RWY 09L, at PHL with a flight director?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 14 CFR 135.225에 따라 BE-1900 형식 PIC 100시간 미만이면 MDA/DH +100 ft, visibility +1/2 SM 또는 RVR 2,400 ft를 적용한다. 따라서 PHL ILS RWY 09L PIC minimum은 313/42이다.
questions.explanation_en: 14 CFR 135.225 requires that, if the PIC of a turbine-powered airplane has less than 100 hr. as PIC in that type of airplane (i.e., BE 1900), the MDA or DH is increased by 100 ft., and the visibility by 1/2 SM (or 2,400 ft. RVR). Thus, the PIC’s minimums when flying the ILS RWY 09L approach at PHL are 313/42. Answer (B) is incorrect. These are the minimums if the PIC has at least, not less than, 100 hr. as PIC in the BE 1900. Answer (C) is incorrect. The visibility increases by 1/2 SM, or 2,400 ft. RVR, not 1,800 ft. RVR, if the PIC has less than 100 hr. as PIC in the BE 1900.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 310 on page 514.) The PIC of EAB 90 has 89 hours and 29 landings as PIC in the BE 1900, while operating under Part 135. The PIC has 1,234 hours and 579 landings as PIC in the DC-3 while operating under Part 135. What are the minimums for the ILS RWY 9L approach at PHL, for this PIC?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. BE-1900 형식 PIC 100시간 미만이면 14 CFR 135.225의 가산 minimum을 적용하며, 다른 형식인 DC-3 PIC 시간은 이 100시간 요건에 포함되지 않는다. 결과적으로 PHL ILS RWY 9L minimum은 313/42이다.
questions.explanation_en: 14 CFR 135.225 requires that, if the PIC of a turbine-powered airplane has less than 100 hr. as PIC in that type of airplane (i.e., BE 1900), the MDA or DH is increased by 100 ft., and the visibility is increased by 1/2 SM (or 2,400 ft. RVR). Thus, the PIC’s minimums when flying the ILS RWY 9L approach at PHL are 313/42. The DC-3 time does not count toward the 100-hr. requirement because it is a different type of airplane. Answer (A) is incorrect. These are the minimums if the PIC has at least, not less than, 100 hr. as PIC in the BE 1900. Answer (B) is incorrect. Visibility increases by 2,400 ft. RVR (1/2 SM), not 600 ft. RVR, if the PIC has less than 100 hr. as PIC in the BE 1900.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 183 on page 513 and Figure 311 on page 515.) When the weather at PHL goes below the PIC’s minimums, the flight diverts to ACY. Upon arrival at ACY, EAB 90 is cleared for the ILS RWY 13 approach. The PIC has 89 hours of PIC time in the BE 1900. What are the PIC’s minimums?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Part 135에서 해당 터빈 형식 PIC 100시간 미만이면 MDA/DH +100 ft, visibility +1/2 SM 또는 RVR 2,400 ft를 적용하되 alternate 사용 시의 ceiling/visibility를 넘겨 가산할 필요는 없다. ACY ILS RWY 13 PIC minimum은 375/42이다.
questions.explanation_en: 14 CFR 135.225 requires that, if the PIC of a turbine-powered airplane has less than 100 hr. as PIC in that type of airplane (i.e., BE 1900), the MDA or DH is increased by 100 ft. and the visibility is increased by 1/2 SM (or 2,400 ft. RVR), but not to exceed the ceiling and visibility minimums when used as an alternate airport. Thus, the PIC’s minimums for the ILS RWY 13 approach at ACY are 375/42. Answer (A) is incorrect. These are the alternate minimums for the ILS RWY 13 to list the airport as an alternate, not to fly the approach, for Cat. D, not Cat. B, aircraft. Answer (B) is incorrect. These are the minimums if the PIC has at least, not less than, 100 hr. as PIC in the BE 1900.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Legend 12 on page 516.) Newport News/Williamsburg Intl is a 14 CFR Part 139 airport. The Chart Supplement contains the following entry: ARFF Index A. What is the minimum number of aircraft rescue and fire fighting vehicles, and the type and amount of fire fighting agents that the airport should have?

choices.text: Two vehicles and 600 pounds dry chemical (DC) or Halon 1211 or 500 pounds of DC plus 100 gallons of water.
One vehicle and 500 pounds of dry chemical (DC) or Halon 1211 or 450 pounds DC plus 100 gallons of water.
One vehicle and 500 pounds of dry chemical (DC) or Halon 1211 or 350 pounds DC and 1,000 gallons of water.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Chart Supplement Legend의 ARFF Index A 기준은 최소 차량 1대와 500 lb DC 또는 HALON 1211, 또는 450 lb DC + 물 100 gal이다.
questions.explanation_en: Legend 12 is a Chart Supplement legend. Look at the table at the top of the legend and find the airport index A on the left margin. The minimum number of vehicles is one, and the type and amount of fire-fighting agents are 500 lb. of DC or HALON 1211 or 450 lb. DC plus 100 gal. of water (H2O). Answer (A) is incorrect. An airport having an ARFF Index C, not A, is required to have at least two vehicles. Answer (C) is incorrect. An airport having an ARFF Index A is required to have one vehicle and 500 lb. DC or HALON 1211 or 450 lb., not 350 lb., DC and 100 gal., not 1,000 gal., of water.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 292 on page 518.) To receive the DME information from the facility labeled “DME Chan 22” at La Guardia requires that

choices.text: N711JB be equipped with a UHF NAV radio, which is tuned to channel 22.
a military TACAN be tuned to channel 22.
the VHF NAV radio be tuned to the ILS (108.5) frequency.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. ILS/DME는 주파수 pairing으로 co-located 시설의 course와 distance 정보를 제공한다. DME를 받으려면 ILS 주파수 108.5 MHz에 tune한다.
questions.explanation_en: ILS/DME facilities provide course and distance information from collocated components under a frequency pairing program. Thus, to receive DME information requires that the DME receiver be tuned to the ILS frequency of 108.5. Answer (A) is incorrect. Channel 22 refers to a TACAN receiver, which is used by military, not civilian, aircraft. Answer (B) is incorrect. A military aircraft would select channel 22 on TACAN for DME information, but a civilian aircraft would use the ILS frequency of 108.5 to receive the DME.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 293 on page 519.) The La Guardia weather goes below minimums and New York Approach Control issues a clearance to N711JB, via radar vectors, to ASALT Intersection. As N711JB is approaching ASALT, Approach Control clears the aircraft to fly the VOR RWY 13L/13R approach. What is the distance from ASALT Intersection to RWY 13L?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. JFK VOR or GPS RWY 13L/13R에서 ASALT→CRI 6 NM, CRI→MAP 2.6 NM, MAP→RWY 13L 3.6 NM이므로 ASALT에서 RWY 13L까지 총 12.2 NM이다.
questions.explanation_en: Fig. 293 is the VOR or GPS RWY 13L/13R IAP at JFK. In the lower left-hand corner of the planview is ASALT Int. From ASALT to CRI is 6 NM. The distance from CRI to the MAP is 2.6 DME, and the arc distance from the MAP to RWY 13L is 3.6 NM. Thus, the distance from ASALT to RWY 13L is 12.2 NM (6 + 2.6 + 3.6). Answer (A) is incorrect. The distance from ASALT to RWY 13L is 12.2 NM, not 12.3 NM. Answer (C) is incorrect. The distance from ASALT to RWY 13L is 12.2 NM, not 13.2 NM.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 293 on page 519.) The La Guardia Weather goes below minimums and New York Approach Control issues a clearance to N711JB, via radar vectors, to ASALT Intersection. What is the lowest altitude that Approach Control may clear N711JB to cross ASALT Intersection?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Fig. 293에서 ASALT INT의 공표 mandatory altitude는 3,000 ft이다. 다만 footnote에 따라 ATC가 승인하면 minimum 2,000 ft를 사용할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Fig. 293 is the VOR or GPS RWY 13L/13R IAP at JFK. Look at the profile view and locate ASALT Int. at the top left corner. Next to ASALT is 3000 with a line above and below the number, which means a mandatory altitude. To the left is a cross to reference a footnote, which is just above and to the right. The note states that, at ASALT Int., 2,000 ft. is the minimum altitude when authorized by ATC. Answer (A) is incorrect. This is the mandatory altitude to cross ASALT, unless authorized by ATC, which may use 2,000 ft. as the lowest altitude. Answer (B) is incorrect. The lowest altitude at which ATC may clear an aircraft to cross ASALT is 2,000 ft., not 2,500 ft.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 293 on page 519.) The distance from Canarsie (CRI) to RWY 13R at JFK is
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. CRI에서 MAP DMYHL까지 2.6 NM, DMYHL에서 RWY 13R까지 2.6 NM이므로 CRI에서 RWY 13R까지 총 5.2 NM이다.
questions.explanation_en: Fig. 293 is the VOR or GPS RWY 13L/13R IAP at JFK. Look at the profile view and locate CRI. The distance from CRI to the MAP DMYHL is 2.6 NM. The distance from DMYHL to RWY 13R is 2.6 NM as shown on the planview. Thus, the distance from CRI to RWY 13R is 5.2 NM (2.6 + 2.6). Answer (B) is incorrect. This is the distance to RWY 13R if the arc distance of 3.6 NM is added to the distance from CRI to the MAP. Answer (C) is incorrect. This is the distance to RWY 13R if the arc distance of 2.6 NM is added to the distance from CRI to the first cluster of lead-in lights, not the MAP.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 192 on page 466.) On the airway J10 between OBH and LBF, the MAA is 41,000 feet. What is the MAA on J197 between FSD and OBH?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Jet route system은 18,000 ft MSL부터 45,000 ft MSL까지 설정되고 J+번호로 식별한다. J197 FSD-OBH 구간에 더 낮은 MAA가 별도로 없으므로 MAA는 jet route 상한인 FL450이다.
questions.explanation_en: The jet route system consists of routes established from 18,000 ft. MSL to 45,000 ft. MSL inclusive. Jet routes are identified by the letter “J” followed by the airway number. Since there is no lower MAA established for J197 between FSD and OBH, the MAA is the upper limit of the jet route. Answer (A) is incorrect. The upper limit of a jet route is 45,000 ft. MSL, not 43,000 ft. MSL. Answer (C) is incorrect. This is the upper limit of Class A airspace, not a jet route.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 374 on page 522.) While being radar vectored for the ILS or LOC RWY 8, Denver Approach Control tells PIL 10 to contact the tower, without giving the frequency. What frequency should PIL 10 use for tower?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. DEN ILS/LOC RWY 8 접근의 Denver Tower 주파수는 124.3 MHz이다.
questions.explanation_en: Fig. 374 is the IAP chart for the ILS or LOC RWY 8 approach at DEN. The communication frequencies are shown in the upper center portion of the IAP. Under Denver Tower is the frequency 124.3. Answer (A) is incorrect. This is the ground control, not tower, frequency for RWY 8. Answer (B) is incorrect. This is the tower frequency for RWY 25.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 374 on page 522.) The PIC of PIL 10 has 87.5 hours and 26 landings as PIC in the B-767, while operating under Part 121. The PIC has 1,876 hours and 298 landings, as PIC in the L-1011 while operating under Part 121. What are the minimums for the ILS RWY 8 approach at DEN for the PIC?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Part 121에서 해당 형식 PIC 100시간 미만이면 MDA/DH +100 ft, visibility +1/2 SM을 적용한다. 다른 Part 121 형식에서 PIC 100시간 이상이면 해당 형식 landing 1회당 1시간을 최대 50%까지 대체할 수 있다. 이 조건에서 B-767 26회 착륙을 반영하면 요구시간이 74시간으로 줄어 87.5시간으로 충족하므로 DEN ILS RWY 8 공표 minimum 5551/18을 사용할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: If the PIC has not served 100 hr. as PIC in the type of airplane (s)he is operating under Part 121, the MDA or DH must be increased by 100 ft., and the visibility by 1/2 SM (or 2,400 ft. RVR). However, the PIC time requirement may be reduced (not more than 50%) by substituting one landing in that type of airplane, while operating under Part 121, for one required hour of PIC time, if the PIC has at least 100 hr. as PIC in another type of airplane while operating under Part 121. Since the PIC has over 100 hr. as PIC in the L-1011 while operating under Part 121, (s)he can substitute each landing in the B-767 for one required hour of PIC time (100 hr. requirement – 26 landings = 74 new hr. requirement). Thus, the PIC meets the 100-hr. PIC requirement with 87.5 hr. and can use the published minimums of 5551/18 for the ILS RWY 8 approach at DEN. Answer (B) is incorrect. These would be the PIC minimums for the ILS RWY 8 approach at DEN if the PIC had less than, not more than, 100 hr. as PIC in the L-1011. Answer (C) is incorrect. These are not minimums for the ILS RWY 8 LOC approach at DEN for a PIC with or without 100 hr. as PIC in the B-767 under Part 121.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 375 on page 523 and Figure 376 on page 524.) When PIL 10 becomes visual, at 3.8 NM from the end of Runway 8, if the aircraft is on glide slope and on course what should the pilot see for a Visual Glideslope Indicator?

choices.text: Two white and two red lights on the right side of the runway, in a row.
One white and one red light on the left or right side of the runway, in a row.
Two red and two white lights, in a row, on the left side of the runway.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. DEN RWY 08의 PAPI(P4L)는 활주로 왼쪽에 설치된 4등식 PAPI이다. 정상 glide slope에서는 왼쪽 한 줄에서 적색 2개와 백색 2개가 보인다.
questions.explanation_en: Fig. 376 is the Chart Supplement excerpt for Denver Intl. The runway data begin on the line titled RWY 08-26. Go down one line to RWY 08, which has information concerning the approach end of the runway.
