The Visual Glideslope Indicator is given as PAPI (P4L), which means that the PAPI is a four-light system installed on the left side of the runway. Thus, when on the glide slope, the pilot will see two red and two white lights, in a row, on the left side of the runway. Answer (A) is incorrect. The PAPI on RWY 8 is on the left, not right, side of the runway. Answer (B) is incorrect. RWY 8 has a four-light, not a two-light, PAPI system.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 375 on page 523 and Figure 376 on page 524.) All of the runways at Denver Intl have what type of Visual Glideslope Indicators?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. DEN의 모든 활주로 끝에는 Visual Glideslope Indicator로 PAPI가 설치되어 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Fig. 376 is the Chart Supplement excerpt for DEN. Look at the second line of each runway data line for the runway end data, which list lighting systems for each runway end. Note that all runways at DEN have PAPI (precision approach path indicator) type of Visual Glideslope Indicators. Answer (A) is incorrect. All runways at DEN are equipped with PAPI, not PVASI (pulsating/steady burning visual approach slope indicator), type of Visual Glideslope Indicators. Answer (C) is incorrect. All runways at DEN are equipped with PAPI, not APAP (alignment of panels on approach path), type of Visual Glideslope Indicators.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 330 on page 527.) PTL 55 received the following clearance from Bay Approach Control. PTL 55 is cleared ILS RWY 19L at SFO, sidestep to RWY 19R. 1.3 times the VS0 speed, of PTL 55, is 165 knots. What is the lowest minimum descent altitude (MDA) and the lowest visibility that PTL 55 may accomplish the sidestep?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. SFO ILS RWY 19L에서 PTL55의 1.3 VS0가 165 kt이므로 Approach Category D이다. Category D의 SIDESTEP RWY 19R minimum은 340-2이다.
questions.explanation_en: Fig. 330 is the IAP chart for the ILS RWY 19L at SFO. Look at the minimums section at the lower right portion of the chart. On the left side of the table, locate the SIDESTEP RWY 19R row. Since PTL 55 has a speed of 1.3 VS0 of 165 kt., it is an approach category D airplane (i.e., 1.3 VS0 of 141 kt. or more, but less than 166 kt.). The minimums for a Cat. D airplane for the side step to RWY 19R approach are 340-2. Answer (A) is incorrect. These (note that 1 SM is equivalent to an RVR of 5,000 ft.) are the minimums for Cat. A and B, not Cat. D, aircraft for the side step to RWY 19R approach. Answer (B) is incorrect. These are the minimums for a Cat. C, not Cat. D, aircraft for the side step to RWY 19R approach.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 330 on page 527.) The PIC of PTL 55 has 75 hours and 30 landings as PIC in the B-747, while operating under Part 121. The PIC has 759 hours and 312 landings, as PIC, in the B-767 while operating under Part 121. What are the minimums for the ILS RWY 19L approach at SFO, for the PIC?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Part 121에서 해당 형식 PIC 100시간 미만이어도 다른 Part 121 형식 PIC 100시간 이상이면 해당 형식 landing으로 최대 50시간까지 대체할 수 있다. B-747 착륙 실적을 반영해 100시간 요건을 충족하므로 SFO ILS RWY 19L 공표 minimum 211/40을 사용할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: If the PIC has not served 100 hr. as PIC in the type of airplane (s)he is operating under Part 121, the MDA or DH must be increased by 100 ft. and the visibility by 1/2 SM (or 2,400 ft. RVR). However, the PIC time requirement may be reduced (not more than 50%) by substituting one landing in that type of airplane, while operating under Part 121, for one required hour of PIC time if the PIC has at least 100 hr. as PIC in another type of airplane while operating under Part 121. Since the PIC has over 100 hr. as PIC in the B-767 while operating under Part 121, (s)he can substitute each landing in the B-747 for one hour of required PIC time. Thus, the PIC meets the 100-hr. PIC requirement and can use the published minimums of 211/40 for the ILS RWY 19L approach at SFO. Answer (A) is incorrect. These would be the minimums for the PIC if (s)he had less than, not more than, 100 hr. as PIC in another type of airplane while operating under Part 121. Answer (C) is incorrect. These would be the minimums if SFO was used as the alternate, not destination, and the PIC had less than, not more than, 100 hr. as PIC in another type of airplane while operating under Part 121.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 380 on page 530 and Legend 12 on page 531.) San Francisco Intl (SFO) is a 14 CFR Part 139 airport. What is the minimum number of aircraft rescue and fire fighting vehicles, and the type and amount of fire fighting agents that the airport should have?

choices.text: Three vehicles and 500 pounds of dry chemical (DC) or Halon 1211 or 450 pounds DC and 4,000 gallons of water.
Three vehicles and 500 pounds of dry chemical (DC) or Halon 1211 or 500 pounds of DC plus 5,000 gallons of water.
Three vehicles and 500 pounds of dry chemical (DC) or Halon 1211 or 450 pounds DC plus 6,000 gallons of water.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. SFO의 ARFF Index는 E이다. Index E 기준 최소 차량은 3대이며 500 lb DC/HALON 1211 또는 450 lb DC와 6,000 gal 물 등 규정 소화제가 필요하다.
questions.explanation_en: Fig. 380 is the Chart Supplement excerpt for SFO. First, look for the aircraft rescue and fire-fighting (ARFF) index on the second line, which is ARFF Index E. Next, Legend 12 is a Chart Supplement legend. Look at the table at the top of the legend. Locate the Airport Index column on the left side and move down to Index E. The minimum number of vehicles is three, and the airport is required to have at least 500 lb. of dry chemical (DC) or HALON 1211 or 450 lb. DC plus 6,000 gal. of water (H2O). Answer (A) is incorrect. Three vehicles and 500 lb. DC or HALON 1211 or 450 lb. DC and 4,000 gal. of water are required at OAK (ARFF Index D), not SFO (ARFF Index E). Answer (B) is incorrect. An airport with an ARFF Index E is required to have three vehicles and 500 lb. DC or HALON 1211 or 450 lb., not 500 lb., DC plus 6,000 gal., not 5,000 gal., of water.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 335 on page 528 and Figure 380 on page 530.) At San Francisco Intl (SFO), the runway hold position signs are

choices.text: all on the left-hand side of the taxiways.
all on the right-hand side of the taxiways.
on either side of the taxiways.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. SFO airport diagram note에 따르면 일부 runway hold position sign은 유도로 왼쪽이 아니라 오른쪽에 설치되어 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Fig. 335 is the airport diagram for SFO. On the right side of the diagram is a note that states, “Several runway hold position signs are on the right rather than the left side of the taxiways.” Answer (A) is incorrect. While normally, runway hold position signs are on the left side of the taxiways, SFO has some on the right side as noted on the Airport Diagram. Answer (B) is incorrect. Several, not all, runway hold position signs are on the right, rather than the left, side of the taxiways.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 336 on page 529.) Due to weather, PTL 55 was unable to land at SFO. PTL 55 was given radar vectors to NAGVY Intersection and clearance to fly the ILS RWY 27R approach at Oakland Intl. What frequencies will PTL 55 use for Oakland Tower and Oakland Ground Control?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. OAK ILS RWY 27R 접근의 Tower frequency는 118.3 MHz, Ground Control은 121.9 MHz이다.
questions.explanation_en: Fig. 336 is the IAP chart for the ILS RWY 27R approach at OAK. The communication frequencies are listed in the upper right corner of the planview section. Look for RWY 9-27. The tower control frequency is 118.3, and the ground control frequency of 121.9 is provided in the next box to the right. Answer (A) is incorrect. The ground control frequency for RWY 9-27 and RWY 15-33 is 121.9. Answer (C) is incorrect. The tower frequency for RWY 9-27 and RWY 15-33 is 118.3.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 310 on page 536.) TNA 90 is a CAT C aircraft and has received clearance to fly the LOC RWY 09L and circle to land RWY 27R. LANDI fix is received. What are the minimums?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. PHL LOC RWY 9L을 비행해 RWY 27R로 circling하는 Category C 항공기의 LANDI fix circling minimum은 640/1 3/4이다.
questions.explanation_en: Fig. 310 is the IAP chart for the LOC RWY 9L approach at PHL. The LANDI fix minimums for a circling approach are listed in the bottom left corner of the chart. The Cat. C minimums for an aircraft cleared to fly the LOC RWY 09L and circle to land on RWY 27R are 640/1 3/4. Answer (A) is incorrect. These are the circling minimums with LANDI fix identified for a Cat. D, not Cat. C, airplane. Answer (C) is incorrect. These are the circling minimums if LANDI fix cannot be identified, not if LANDI fix is identified.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 310 on page 536.) TNA 90 is a CAT C aircraft and has received a clearance to fly the LOC RWY 09L; LANDI fix is received and TNA 90 is cleared to land 09L. What are the minimums?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. PHL S-LOC 9L에서 LANDI fix를 받은 Category C 항공기의 minimum은 440/40이다.
questions.explanation_en: Fig. 310 is the IAP chart for the ILS RWY 9L approach at PHL. The LANDI fix minimums for the S-LOC 9L approach are listed in the bottom left of the chart. For a Cat. C airplane, the LANDI fix minimums for an S-LOC 9L are 440/40. Answer (B) is incorrect. These are the minimums for a Cat. C airplane if LANDI fix cannot be identified, not if LANDI fix is identified. Answer (C) is incorrect. These are the LANDI fix minimums for a Cat. C airplane conducting a circling approach, not an S-LOC 9L approach.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 310 on page 536.) The PIC of TNA 90 has 49 hours and 102 landings as PIC in the MD-90 while operating under Part 121. The PIC also has 959 hours and 246 landings, as PIC, in the B-727 while operating under Part 121. What are the minimums with LANDI for the ILS RWY 9L approach at PHL, for this PIC with an operative Flight Director?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Part 121에서 해당 형식 PIC 100시간 미만일 때 다른 형식 경험으로 대체할 수 있는 최대치는 50%이다. MD-90 착륙 50회를 적용해도 총 인정시간이 99시간이라 요건을 충족하지 못하므로 PHL ILS RWY 9L 가산 minimum 313/42를 사용한다.
questions.explanation_en: If the PIC has not served 100 hr. as PIC in the type of airplane (s)he is operating under Part 121, the MDA or DH must be increased by 100 ft., and the visibility by 1/2 SM (or 2,400 ft. RVR). However, the PIC time requirement may be reduced (not more than 50%) by substituting one landing in that type of airplane, while operating under Part 121, for one required hour of PIC time if the PIC has at least 100 hr. as PIC in another type of airplane while operating under Part 121. Since the PIC has over 100 hr. as PIC in the B-727 while operating under Part 121, (s)he can substitute each of only 50 landings (i.e., 50% of required time) in the MD-90 for one hour of required PIC time. This will give the PIC only 99 hr., which means the PIC minimums are raised for the ILS RWY 9L approach at PHL. The PIC minimums are 313/42. Answer (A) is incorrect. These are the published minimums, which can be used only if the PIC has 100 hr. or more, not less than 100 hr., as PIC in the MD-90. Answer (C) is incorrect. RVR visibility is increased by 2,400 ft., not 600 ft.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 310 on page 536.) The PIC on TNA 90 (CAT C aircraft operated under 14 CFR Part 121) has not flown 100 hours as PIC in the MD-90. What are the minimums without LANDI while flying the ILS RWY 9L to land 09R at PHL?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Part 121에서 MD-90 형식 PIC 100시간 미만이면 circling minimum에도 MDA/DH +100 ft, visibility +1/2 SM을 적용한다. PHL ILS RWY 9L circling minimum은 860/2 3/4가 된다.
questions.explanation_en: Fig. 310 is the IAP chart for the ILS RWY 9L approach at PHL. If the PIC has not served 100 hr. as PIC in the type of airplane (s)he is operating under Part 121, the MDA or DH must be increased by 100 ft., and the visibility by 1/2 SM (or 2,400 ft. RVR). Thus, in a circling approach, if the PIC of TNA 90 has not flown 100 hr. as PIC in the MD-90, the minimums to conduct the ILS RWY 9L at PHL are 860/2 3/4. Answer (A) is incorrect. If the PIC has less than 100 hr. as PIC in the MD-90, the RVR visibility must be increased by 1/2 mi., not 1/4 mi. Answer (B) is incorrect. If the PIC has less than 100 hr. as PIC in the MD-90, the minimums must be increased by 100 ft. and 1/2 mi. visibility.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 386 on page 539 and Legend 12 on page 540.) Windsor Locks/Bradley Intl, is a 14 CFR Part 139 airport. What is the minimum number of aircraft rescue and fire-fighting vehicles, and what type and amount of fire-fighting agents is the airport required to have?

choices.text: Two vehicles and 600 pounds dry chemical (DC), or Halon 1211 or 500 pounds of DC plus 4,000 gallons of water.
Three vehicles and 500 pounds of dry chemical (DC), or Halon 1211 or 450 pounds DC plus 3,000 gallons of water.
Three vehicles and 500 pounds of dry chemical (DC), or Halon 1211 or 450 pounds DC and 4,000 gallons of water.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. BDL의 ARFF Index는 D이다. Index D 기준 최소 차량은 3대이며 500 lb DC/HALON 1211 또는 450 lb DC와 4,000 gal 물 등 규정 소화제가 필요하다.
questions.explanation_en: Fig. 386 is the Chart Supplement excerpt for BDL. First, look at the aircraft rescue and fire-fighting (ARFF) index on the third line, which is ARFF Index D. Next, Legend 12 is a Chart Supplement legend. Look at the table at the top of the legend. Locate the Airport Index column on the left side and move down to Index D. The minimum number of vehicles is three, and the airport is required to have at least 500 lb. of dry chemical (DC) or HALON 1211 or 450 lb. DC plus 4,000 gal. of water (H2O) Answer (A) is incorrect. BDL is required to have three, not two, vehicles. Answer (B) is incorrect. Three vehicles and 500 lb. DC or HALON 1211 or 450 lb. DC plus 3,000 gal. of water are required for an airport with an ARFF Index C, not ARFF Index D.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 343 on page 538.) The airport diagram of Bradley Intl Airport has a symbol (appears to be a triangle balanced on top of another triangle) located close to the approach end of RWY 24. What does this symbol indicate?

choices.text: Practice hover area for the Army National Guard helicopters.
Two course lights, back to back, which flash beams of light along the course of an airway.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. BDL airport diagram에서 RWY 24 접근단 밖의 겹친 삼각형 모양 기호는 runway radar reflector 위치를 나타낸다.
questions.explanation_en: Fig. 343 is the airport diagram for BDL. The symbol that appears to be one triangle on top of another triangle located off the approach end of RWY 24 indicates that runway radar reflectors are at that position. Answer (B) is incorrect. Symbols are not used to indicate a practice hover area for helicopters. Answer (C) is incorrect. Two course lights, back to back, which flash beams of light along the course of an airway are used to mark airway segments in a few remote mountainous areas, not at an airport.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 183 on page 535 and Figure 311 on page 537.) The PIC, of TNA 90, has 75 hours as PIC of this type airplane. The MD-90 is a Category C aircraft. What is the lowest ceiling/visibility that may be forecast to use ACY as an alternate on the flight plan, and what is the lowest visibility that may exist at ACY prior to the final approach segment to continue the ILS RWY 13 approach?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. ACY ILS RWY 13은 비표준 alternate 표시가 있지만 그 비표준 값은 Cat E에만 적용되므로 Cat C는 standard precision alternate minimum 600-2를 사용할 수 있다. 다만 해당 형식 PIC 100시간 미만이면 alternate에서 landing visibility는 최소 1 SM 또는 RVR 5,000 ft 이상이어야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: Fig. 311 is the IAP chart for the ILS RWY 13 approach at ACY. In the top left corner of the chart, there is a black triangle with a white “A” inside, which indicates nonstandard alternate minimums. Fig. 183 lists the nonstandard alternate minimums for ACY. Since the nonstandard alternate minimums for the ILS RWY 13 apply to Cat. E aircraft only, a Cat. C aircraft can use the standard alternate minimums for a precision approach of 600-2. If the PIC has not served 100 hours as PIC in that type of airplane, the minimum landing visibility at an alternate airport cannot be less than 1 SM (or 5,000 ft. RVR). Answer (A) is incorrect. The lowest visibility that may exist at ACY prior to the final approach segment to continue to ILS RWY 13 approach is 1 SM, not 2 SM. Answer (C) is incorrect. The minimum RVR visibility must be 5,000 ft., not 2,400 ft.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: (Refer to Figure 183 on page 535 and Figure 311 on page 537.) The weather at PHL goes below the PIC’s minimums and TNA 90 (a CAT C aircraft operating under 14 CFR Part 121) diverts to the alternate ACY. Upon arrival at ACY, TNA 90 is cleared for an ILS RWY 13 approach. The PIC has less than 100 hours of PIC time in the MD-90. What are the landing minimums?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Part 121에서 해당 형식 PIC 100시간 미만이면 가산 minimum은 alternate 사용 시 적용값을 넘을 필요가 없지만 landing minimum은 어떤 경우에도 300 ft 및 1 SM(RVR 5,000 ft)보다 낮을 수 없다. ACY RWY 13 TDZE 75 ft를 반영하면 PIC minimum은 375/50이다.
questions.explanation_en: If the PIC has not served 100 hours as PIC in the type of airplane (s)he is operating under Part 121, the MDA or DH and visibility need not be increased above those applicable to the airport when used as an alternate, but in no event may the landing minimums be less than 300 ft. and 1 SM (or 5,000 ft. RVR). Fig. 311 is the IAP chart for the ILS RWY 13 approach at ACY. The TDZE for RWY 13 is found in the airport diagram at the lower left of the chart. The TDZE for RWY 13 is 75 ft. Thus, the landing minimums for the PIC of TNA 90 for the ILS RWY 13 approach are 375/50. Answer (A) is incorrect. The RVR visibility must be at least 5,000 ft., not remain the same. Answer (C) is incorrect. An RVR visibility of 4,200 ft. would be required if ACY were the destination, not the alternate, airport.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is the primary cause of all changes in the Earth’s weather?

choices.text: Variations of solar energy at the Earth’s surface.
Changes in air pressure over the Earth’s surface.
Movement of air masses from moist areas to dry areas.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 모든 기상현상은 열교환을 동반하거나 그 결과로 발생한다. 지표의 불균등한 태양가열이 기압차를 만들고 이것이 지구의 기상변화를 일으키는 근본 원인이다.
questions.explanation_en: Every physical process of weather is accompanied by or is the result of a heat exchange. Unequal solar heating of the Earth’s surface causes differences in air pressure that result in all changes in the Earth’s weather. Answer (B) is incorrect. Changes in air pressure are a result of the unequal solar heating of the Earth’s surface. Answer (C) is incorrect. Movement of air masses is a result of unequal solar heating of the Earth’s surface.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What term describes an elongated area of low pressure?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Trough는 길게 늘어진 저압부로, 가장 낮은 기압이 최대 저기압성 곡률을 이루는 선을 따라 위치한다.
questions.explanation_en: A trough is defined as an elongated area of low pressure with the lowest pressure along a line marking maximum cyclonic curvature. Answer (B) is incorrect. A ridge is an elongated area of high, not low, pressure. Answer (C) is incorrect. A hurricane or typhoon is a tropical cyclone (low) with highest sustained winds of 64 kt. or greater.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which weather condition is defined as an anticyclone?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Anticyclone은 고기압 영역이다. 북반구에서는 시계방향, 남반구에서는 반시계방향으로 순환하며 적도에서는 방향이 뚜렷하지 않다.
questions.explanation_en: An anticyclone is an area of high atmospheric pressure. The circulation is clockwise in the Northern Hemisphere, counterclockwise in the Southern Hemisphere, and undefined at the Equator. Answer (A) is incorrect. Calm is defined as the absence of wind or of apparent motion of the air. Answer (C) is incorrect. COL is the neutral area between two highs or two lows. It is also the intersection of a trough and a ridge.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is a feature of air movement in a high pressure area?

choices.text: Ascending from the surface high to lower pressure at higher altitudes.
Descending to the surface and then outward.
Moving outward from the high at high altitudes and into the high at the surface.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 고기압에서는 상대적으로 무거운 공기가 하강한 뒤 지표에서 바깥쪽으로 퍼져나간다. 따라서 고기압은 하강기류와 발산이 특징이다.
questions.explanation_en: The air movement out of a high-pressure area depletes the quantity of air because the air is heavier than the low-pressure air surrounding it. Therefore, high-pressure areas are areas of descending air toward the surface, then outward from the high. Answer (A) is incorrect. Air descends, not ascends, from a high-pressure area, at all altitudes. Answer (C) is incorrect. The air always moves outward, not inward, from a high, regardless of altitude.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Where is the usual location of a thermal low?

choices.text: Over the eye of a hurricane.
Over the surface of a dry, sunny region.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 건조하고 맑은 지역이 강한 지표가열로 매우 뜨거워지면 thermal low가 형성된다. Thermal low는 비교적 얕고 기압경도가 약하며 뚜렷한 cyclonic circulation이 없는 경우가 많다.
questions.explanation_en: A dry, sunny region becomes quite warm from intense surface heating, thus generating a surface low-pressure area known as a thermal low. Thermal lows are relatively shallow with weak pressure gradients and without well-defined cyclonic circulation. Answer (A) is incorrect. Thermal lows develop over dry, sunny regions, not in the Arctic. Answer (B) is incorrect. An eye of a hurricane marks the center of a well-developed tropical cyclone, not a thermal low.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: A low-pressure area is an area of
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 저기압에서는 상승하는 공기를 보충하기 위해 주변 공기가 안쪽으로 유입된다.
questions.explanation_en: Air flows into low pressure areas to replace rising air. Answer (A) is incorrect. Stagnant air is air that is not moving or does not move. Answer (B) is incorrect. Descending air is found in a high-pressure area, not a low-pressure area.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which event usually occurs after an aircraft passes through a front into the colder air?

choices.text: Wind direction shifts to the left.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Front는 pressure trough 안에 위치하고 일반적으로 찬 공기 쪽의 기압이 더 높다. 따라서 전선을 가로질러 더 찬 공기로 들어가면 기압은 보통 상승한다.
questions.explanation_en: A front lies in a pressure trough, and pressure generally is higher in cold air. Thus, when you cross a front directly into colder air, barometric pressure usually increases. Answer (A) is incorrect. The temperature/dew point spread usually differs across a front, but it may not decrease if you fly into a cold, dry air mass. Answer (B) is incorrect. In the Northern Hemisphere, the wind always shifts to the right, not left, due to the Coriolis force.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is a feature of a stationary front?

choices.text: The warm front surface moves about half the speed of the cold front surface.
Weather conditions are a combination of strong cold front and strong warm front weather.
Surface winds tend to flow parallel to the frontal zone.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 서로 다른 밀도의 기단이 맞서 전선면이 거의 움직이지 않으면 stationary front가 된다. 지상풍은 이 전선대를 따라 거의 평행하게 분다.
questions.explanation_en: The opposing forces exerted by adjacent air masses of different densities are such that the frontal surface between them shows little or no movement and a stationary front results. The surface winds tend to flow parallel to this frontal zone. Answer (A) is incorrect. The movement of a warm front surface at about half the speed of the cold front surface is a feature of the movement of a warm, not stationary, front when the general wind flow is the same in each case. Answer (B) is incorrect. Weather conditions that are a combination of strong cold front and strong warm front weather are a feature of an occluded, not stationary, front.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which atmospheric factor causes rapid movement of surface fronts?

choices.text: Upper winds blowing across the front.
Upper low located directly over the surface low.
The cold front overtaking and lifting the warm front.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 전선의 이동은 상층풍의 영향을 크게 받는다. 상층풍이 전선을 가로질러 불면 전선은 대체로 그 바람 방향으로 이동한다.
questions.explanation_en: The upper wind flow dictates to a great extent the movement of the front. Systems tend to move with the upper winds. When winds aloft blow across a front, it tends to move with the wind. Answer (B) is incorrect. An upper low located directly over a surface low is a factor in how extensive the weather will be, not in how fast it will move. Answer (C) is incorrect. A cold front overtaking and lifting the warm front is a characteristic of an advancing cold front.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: In which meteorological conditions can frontal waves and low pressure areas form?

choices.text: Slow-moving cold fronts or stationary fronts.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Frontal wave와 저기압은 보통 이동이 느린 cold front 또는 stationary front에서 잘 형성된다.
questions.explanation_en: Frontal waves and areas of low pressure usually form on slow-moving cold fronts or on stationary fronts. Answer (A) is incorrect. Occluded fronts are formed by frontal waves and areas of low pressure that cause a cold front to close together with a warm front. Frontal waves and low-pressure areas normally form on slow-moving cold, not warm, fronts. Answer (C) is incorrect. A cold front occlusion occurs when the air behind the cold front is colder than the air in advance of the warm front, lifting the warm front aloft.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What type weather change is to be expected in an area where frontolysis is reported?

choices.text: The frontal weather is becoming stronger.
The front is moving at a faster speed.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Frontolysis는 인접 기단이 변질되어 전선을 사이에 둔 온도·기압 차가 줄어들면서 전선이 약화·소멸하는 과정이다.
questions.explanation_en: Frontolysis is the process in which the adjacent air masses modify, and as temperature and pressure equalize across a front, the front dissipates. Answer (A) is incorrect. Frontal weather becoming stronger is a weather change that is to be expected in an area where frontogenesis, not frontolysis, is reported. Answer (C) is incorrect. A front moving at a fast speed is a weather change expected in an area of frontogenesis, not frontolysis.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which weather condition is an example of a nonfrontal instability band?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Instability line은 전선이 아닌 좁은 대류활동 띠이다. 이 활동이 완전히 발달한 뇌우로 구성되면 squall line이라 한다.
questions.explanation_en: An instability line is a narrow, nonfrontal line or band of convective activity. If this activity is fully developed thunderstorms, it is called a squall line. Answer (B) is incorrect. Advective fog occurs when warm, moist air moves over a cool surface. It forms in stable, not unstable, air. Answer (C) is incorrect. Frontogenesis is the generation of a frontal, not nonfrontal, zone.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Dew point fronts are also called
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 미국 서부 Texas·New Mexico에서 Plains 북쪽까지는 dew point front인 dry line이 흔하다. Gulf of Mexico에서 북상하는 습한 공기와 남서쪽의 더 건조하고 약간 밀도 높은 공기가 만난다. 습윤측에는 야간·이른 아침 안개와 하층운이, 건조측에는 대체로 맑은 하늘이 나타나며 봄·초여름에는 squall line과 tornado가 잘 발생한다.
questions.explanation_en: During a considerable part of the year, dew point fronts are common in western Texas and New Mexico northward over the plains states. Moist air flowing north from the Gulf of Mexico abuts the dryer and, therefore, slightly denser air flowing from the southwest. Except for moisture differences, there is seldom any significant air mass contrast across this “front;” and therefore, it is commonly called a “dry line.” Nighttime and early morning fog and low-level clouds often prevail on the moist side of the line, while generally clear skies mark the dry side. In spring and early summer over Texas, Oklahoma, and Kansas, and for some distance eastward, the dry line is a favored spawning area for squall lines and tornadoes. Answer (A) is incorrect. Dew point fronts are also called dry lines, not wet lines. Answer (B) is incorrect. Dew point fronts are also called dry lines, not point fronts.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Frozen dew is
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 이슬이 먼저 생긴 뒤 얼면 frozen dew가 된다. Frozen dew는 단단하고 투명한 반면 frost는 흰색이고 불투명해 구별할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Sometimes dew forms and later freezes. Frozen dew is easily distinguished from frost. Frozen dew is hard and transparent, while frost is white and opaque. Answer (A) is incorrect. Frozen dew is hard and transparent, not opaque. Answer (C) is incorrect. Frost, not frozen dew, is white and opaque.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What weather difference is found on each side of a “dry line”?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Dry line은 서부 Texas와 New Mexico에서 Plains 북쪽까지 흔하며 Gulf의 습한 공기와 남서쪽의 건조하고 약간 더 밀도 높은 공기가 만나는 경계이다. 주된 차이는 수분·dew point이다.
questions.explanation_en: A “dry line” is common in Western Texas and New Mexico northward over the Plains. Moist air flowing north from the Gulf of Mexico meets the drier and slightly denser air flowing from the southwest. Except for moisture (dew point) differences, there is seldom any significant weather difference found on each side. Answer (A) is incorrect. Except for a moisture difference, not an extreme temperature difference, there is seldom any significant air mass contrast across the “dry line.” Answer (C) is incorrect. The side with moisture may have clouds, while generally clear skies mark the dry side.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Dew point fronts result from

choices.text: air density differences due to humidity levels.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Dry line의 밀도 차이는 주로 수분(습도) 차이에서 생긴다. Gulf에서 북상하는 습한 공기와 남서쪽의 건조한 공기가 맞닿는다.
questions.explanation_en: During a considerable part of the year, dew point fronts are common in western Texas and New Mexico northward over the plains states. Moist air flows north from the Gulf of Mexico and abuts the dryer and, therefore, slightly denser air flowing from the southwest. It is the moisture (humidity) difference that causes the air density differences. Answer (A) is incorrect. It is not the temperature, but the moisture difference, from which dew point fronts result. Answer (C) is incorrect. It is not the temperature aloft, but the moisture difference, from which dew point fronts result.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: If the winds aloft are blowing across the front,

choices.text: visibility around the front will be poor due to precipitation.
the winds aloft can be expected to turn at the frontal boundary.
the front can be expected to move with the upper winds.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 기상계는 대체로 상층풍과 함께 이동한다. 상층풍이 전선을 가로지르면 전선도 이동하고, 전선과 평행하게 불면 전선 이동은 거의 없다.
questions.explanation_en: Systems tend to move with the upper winds. When winds aloft blow across a front, the front tends to move with the wind. When winds blow parallel to the front, little or no movement will occur. Answer (A) is incorrect. Visibility within the front may be poor due to precipitation, but this is not directly related to the winds aloft. Answer (B) is incorrect. The upper wind flow dictates to a great extent the movement of the front. Frontal boundary systems tend to move with the upper winds, not change their direction.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Shallow frontal surfaces tend to give

choices.text: extensive cloudiness and large areas of precipitation.
areas of cloudiness and scattered precipitation.
heavy precipitation developing along the leading edge of the front.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 경사가 완만한 frontal surface는 넓은 범위의 운량과 광범위한 강수구역을 만들기 쉽다.
questions.explanation_en: Shallow frontal surfaces tend to give extensive cloudiness with large precipitation areas. Answer (B) is incorrect. Shallow frontal surfaces tend to have widespread precipitation, which often causes low stratus and fog. Answer (C) is incorrect. Shallow frontal surfaces tend to give extensive cloudiness with large precipitation areas. Heavy frontal precipitation is usually associated with sharp frontal surfaces.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Steep frontal surfaces are usually associated with
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 빠르게 이동하는 경사가 급한 cold front는 선단에서 따뜻한 공기를 강제로 상승시킨다. 찬 공기가 따뜻한 공기를 빠르게 대체하므로 선단 부근 전선경사가 가파르다.
questions.explanation_en: A fast moving, steep cold front forces upward motion of the warm air along its leading edge. The frontal slope is steep near the leading edge as cold air replaces warm air. Answer (A) is incorrect. A warm front is usually about half as fast as a cold front. Answer (C) is incorrect. A dry line is a boundary separating moist and dry air masses and an important factor in severe weather frequency in the Great Plains. It is not associated with a steep frontal surface.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: At lower levels of the atmosphere, friction causes the wind to flow across isobars into a low because the friction

choices.text: creates air turbulence and raises atmospheric pressure.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 지표마찰은 풍속과 Coriolis force를 줄이지만 pressure-gradient force에는 직접 영향을 주지 않는다. 따라서 바람은 등압선을 가로질러 저기압 쪽으로 향하게 된다.
questions.explanation_en: Surface friction decreases the wind speed and Coriolis force but does not affect pressure gradient force. The stronger pressure gradient turns the wind across the isobars toward lower pressure. Answer (B) is incorrect. Friction does not affect the pressure gradient force. Answer (C) is incorrect. Surface obstructions, not surface friction, cause air turbulence.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: At which location does Coriolis force have the least effect on wind direction?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Coriolis force는 적도 바로 위를 제외한 모든 곳에서 바람의 방향에 영향을 준다.
questions.explanation_en: The Coriolis force affects the wind direction everywhere except immediately at the Equator. Answer (A) is incorrect. The Coriolis force has the most (not least) effect on wind direction at the poles. Answer (B) is incorrect. The effects of the Coriolis force are quite pronounced in middle latitudes.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: How does Coriolis force affect wind direction in the Southern Hemisphere?

choices.text: Causes clockwise rotation around a low.
Causes wind to flow out of a low toward a high.
Has exactly the same effect as in the Northern Hemisphere.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 남반구에서 Coriolis force는 공기를 왼쪽으로 편향시킨다. 따라서 남반구의 저기압 주위 바람은 시계방향으로 회전한다.
questions.explanation_en: Coriolis force deflects air to the left in the Southern Hemisphere, which is the opposite from the Northern Hemisphere. In the Southern Hemisphere, the wind blows clockwise around a low. Answer (B) is incorrect. The wind flows from a high to a low, not a low to a high, in both the Northern and Southern Hemispheres. Answer (C) is incorrect. The Coriolis force deflects air to the left in the Southern Hemisphere, which is the opposite, not the same, effect as in the Northern Hemisphere.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What minimum thickness of cloud layer is indicated if precipitation is reported as light or greater intensity?

choices.text: A thickness which allows the cloud tops to be higher than the freezing level.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 공항에서 light 이상 강도의 강수가 보고되면 구름 두께가 최소 약 4,000 ft일 가능성을 예상할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: When arriving at or departing from an airport reporting precipitation of light or greater intensity, expect clouds to be at least 4,000 ft. thick. Answer (B) is incorrect. To produce significant precipitation (light or greater intensity), clouds are normally at least 4,000 ft., not 2,000 ft., thick. Answer (C) is incorrect. A cloud thickness resulting in cloud tops above the freezing level means ice droplets and supercooled water will develop.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is the lowest cloud in the stationary group associated with a mountain wave?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 산악파의 lee side에 구름을 만들 수 있을 만큼 수분이 있으면 가장 낮은 산악파 관련 구름은 rotor cloud이며 standing wave의 각 crest 아래에 형성된다.
questions.explanation_en: When moisture is sufficient to produce clouds on the lee side of a mountain, the lowest clouds associated with mountain wave are rotor clouds. These are found under each crest of the standing wave. Answer (B) is incorrect. The standing lenticular clouds mark the crest, i.e., the top, of each standing wave. Answer (C) is incorrect. Low stratus clouds are not associated with a mountain wave.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which condition produces weather on the lee side of a large lake?

choices.text: Warm air flowing over a colder lake may produce fog.
Cold air flowing over a warmer lake may produce advection fog.
Warm air flowing over a cool lake may produce rain showers.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 따뜻하고 습한 공기가 더 차가운 호수 위를 지나면 증발로 수분을 얻으면서 하층이 냉각되어 포화될 수 있다. 안개는 호수의 lee side, 즉 바람이 불어가는 쪽에서 넓고 짙게 발달할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Warm air flowing over a colder lake may become saturated by evaporation from the water while also becoming cooler in the low levels by contact with the cooler water. Fog often becomes extensive and dense to the lee side of the lake. The lee side is the side to which the wind is going. Answer (B) is incorrect. Cold air flowing over a warmer lake may produce rain showers, not advection fog, on the lee side of the lake. Answer (C) is incorrect. Warm air flowing over a cool lake may produce fog, not rain showers, on the lee side of the lake.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Clouds with extensive vertical development over mountainous terrain are a sign of
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 산을 가로지르는 바람은 mountain wave를 만들며 severe turbulence, 강한 수직기류, icing을 동반할 수 있다. 충분한 수분이 있으면 각 파의 crest 부근에 lenticular cloud가 형성된다.
questions.explanation_en: Winds across mountains cause mountain waves that are associated with severe turbulence, strong vertical currents, and icing. The extent of the turbulence is relative to the height of the ground, speed of the wind, and instability of the atmosphere. With adequate moisture, lenticular clouds will form at the top of each wave. Answer (A) is incorrect. The dry adiabatic lapse rate is a measurement of air with no moisture available to form clouds. Answer (B) is incorrect. The vertical development of the clouds indicate the presence of multiple waves with adequate upward motion and moisture to cause cloud formation.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which type clouds are indicative of very strong turbulence?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Standing lenticular cloud는 mountain wave의 crest에 형성되며 매우 강한 바람과 난류를 시사하는 중요한 징후이다.
questions.explanation_en: Standing lenticular clouds are formed on the crests of mountain waves. Wind can be quite strong blowing through these clouds, and their presence is a good indication of very strong turbulence. Answer (A) is incorrect. Nimbostratus is a gray or dark massive cloud layer, diffused by continuous rain, snow, or ice pellets. The stratus feature indicates very little turbulence. Answer (C) is incorrect. Cirrocumulus describes thin clouds appearing as small white flakes or patches of cotton. Their presence indicates some turbulence and possible icing.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: When advection fog has developed, what may tend to dissipate or lift the fog into low stratus clouds?
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Advection fog는 습한 공기가 더 차가운 지면이나 수면 위로 이동할 때 형성된다. 풍속이 약 15 kt까지 증가하면 깊어지지만 그보다 강하면 안개가 들어 올려져 low stratus 또는 stratocumulus가 될 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Advection fog forms when moist air moves over colder ground or water. It deepens as wind speed increases up to about 15 kt. Wind stronger than 15 kt. lifts the fog into a layer of low stratus or stratocumulus. Answer (A) is incorrect. Winds stronger than 15 kt., not a temperature inversion, tend to dissipate or lift advection fog. Answer (C) is incorrect. Surface temperature radiation is a factor in radiation fog, not advection fog.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: How are haze layers cleared or dispersed?

choices.text: By convective mixing in cool night air.
By wind or the movement of air.
By evaporation similar to the clearing of fog.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Haze는 바람으로 제거·분산될 수 있고, 주간 가열로 대류가 생기면 더 높은 고도까지 퍼질 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Haze layers may be cleared or dispersed by the wind, or heating during the day may cause convective movement of the air, spreading the haze to a higher altitude. Answer (A) is incorrect. Convective mixing is caused by heating during the day, not by the cool night air. Answer (C) is incorrect. Haze must be dispersed by movement of air. It cannot evaporate in a manner similar to the clearing of fog.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which conditions are necessary for the formation of upslope fog?

choices.text: Moist, stable air being moved over gradually rising ground by a wind.
A clear sky, little or no wind, and 100 percent relative humidity.
Rain falling through stratus clouds and a 10- to 25-knot wind moving the precipitation up the slope.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Upslope fog는 습하고 안정한 공기가 바람에 의해 경사면을 따라 서서히 상승하면서 냉각되어 형성된다. Upslope wind가 멈추면 안개도 소산한다.
questions.explanation_en: Upslope fog is formed by moist, stable air being cooled as it is gradually moved up sloping terrain by a wind. Once the upslope wind ceases, the fog dissipates. Answer (B) is incorrect. Clear skies, calm wind, and high humidity are conditions necessary for the formation of radiation fog, not upslope fog. Answer (C) is incorrect. Upslope fog is formed by moist air being moved gradually over rising ground, not by rain falling through stratus clouds and not by a wind blowing the precipitation up the slope.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Cumulus clouds often indicate
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Cumulus cloud는 convective updraft에서 형성되어 위로 발달하며 난류와 연관된다.
questions.explanation_en: Cumulus clouds are formed in a convective updraft, build upward, and are associated with turbulence. Answer (B) is incorrect. A temperature inversion prevents updrafts from forming which is needed for the formation of cumulus clouds. Answer (C) is incorrect. The dry adiabatic lapse rate is a measurement of air with no moisture available to form clouds.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Cumuliform clouds signify
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 불안정한 공기는 대류를 촉진한다. 불안정층에서 형성되는 구름은 cumuliform이고 수직 발달 정도는 불안정층의 깊이에 좌우된다.
questions.explanation_en: Unstable air favors convection. Cumulus (meaning heap) clouds form in a convective updraft and build upward. Within an unstable layer, clouds are cumuliform. The vertical extent of the cloud depends on the depth of the unstable layer. Answer (A) is incorrect. Lenticular clouds form over mountainous terrain. Answer (B) is incorrect. Cumuliform clouds can form in low or high temperatures depending on the ambient temperature.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Cloud formation is a process of
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 공기를 포화까지 냉각시키는 기본 과정 가운데 구름 형성의 가장 중요한 원인은 상승·팽창에 의한 expansional cooling이다.
questions.explanation_en: Of the three basic processes that cool air to saturation, expansional cooling is the major cause of cloud formation. Answer (A) is incorrect. Although stagnant air overlying a cooling surface is one of the basic processes that may cool air to saturation, it is not the major cause or process of cloud formation. Answer (C) is incorrect. Advective cooling is the process in which warm air blows over cool surfaces thereby cooling the air. This is not a process of cloud formation, this most often results in the formation of fog.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Cloud bases can usually be estimated by dividing the surface Fahrenheit temperature and dew point difference by
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 상승하는 공기에서 기온과 dew point는 1,000 ft당 약 4°F(2.2°C)의 속도로 가까워진다. 지상 기온-이슬점 차를 4°F 또는 2.2°C로 나누면 구름 밑면 고도를 천 ft 단위로 대략 추정할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Temperature and dew point in upward moving air converge at a rate of about 4°F (2.20°C) per 1,000 feet. Find the difference between the surface temperature and surface dew point, and then divide by 4°F or 2.20°C as appropriate. The resulting number provides an estimate of the cloud bases in thousands of feet. Answer (B) is incorrect. The rate of convergence of the surface temperature and dew point is 4°F per 1,000 feet. Answer (C) is incorrect. The rate of convergence of the surface temperature and dew point is 4°F per 1,000 feet.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Middle clouds are considered to be the clouds between
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 중층운에는 altostratus, altocumulus, nimbostratus가 포함된다. 주로 물방울로 이루어지며 상당 부분이 supercooled일 수 있고, 중위도에서 운저는 대략 6,500~20,000 ft 범위이다.
questions.explanation_en: The middle cloud family consists of the altostratus, altocumulus, and nimbostratus clouds. These clouds are primarily water, much of which may be supercooled. The height of the bases of these clouds ranges from about 6,500 to 20,000 feet in middle latitudes. Answer (A) is incorrect. The height of 1,000 to 6,500 feet AGL more closely describes the low cloud family, which exist near the Earth’s surface to 6,500 feet AGL. Answer (B) is incorrect. The high, not the middle, cloud family is from about 20,000 feet AGL and above.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Except for temperature, ice fog forms in conditions favorable to
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Radiation fog는 맑고 바람이 약한 밤에 지표가 복사냉각되면서 형성된다. 지면 가까이에 충분히 깊은 습윤층이 있으면 상대습도가 100%에 도달해 안개가 생긴다. 지표에 붙어 있고 보통 정체하며 깊이는 수 ft에서 약 1,000 ft까지 가능해 이착륙 시 매우 위험할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Conditions favorable for this type of fog are the same as for Arctic fog except for the temperature. Radiation fog forms at night under clear skies with calm winds when heat absorbed by the Earth’s surface during the day is radiated into space. Provided a deep enough layer of moist air is present near the ground, as the Earth’s surface continues to cool, the humidity will reach 100% and fog will form. Radiation fog varies in depth from 3 feet to about 1,000 feet, is always found at ground level, and usually remains stationary. This type of fog can reduce visibility to near zero at times and makes flying very hazardous during takeoffs and landings. Answer (A) is incorrect. Advection fog often looks like radiation fog and is also the result of condensation. However, the condensation in this case is caused not by a reduction in surface temperature, but rather by the horizontal movement of warm moist air over a cold surface. Answer (C) is incorrect. Arctic fog appears in very cold air from the Arctic ice or frozen-land regions moving over the warmer water of open parts of the Arctic Ocean. Rapid heating induces convection currents that rise in the air. These carry moisture upwards from the water surface, and this becomes visible as the moisture quickly condenses again in the very cold surrounding air. From this, a fog of rising columns of condensing water vapor is formed. The fog is usually fairly shallow, wispy, and smoke-like. Arctic fog may be seen in winter over the open water of rivers when the air is colder than water by 10°C or more.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Radiation fog forms
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Radiation fog는 야간 복사냉각이 큰 육지에서 주로 발생하며, 수면은 밤에 잘 냉각되지 않으므로 일반적으로 수면에서는 형성되기 어렵다.
questions.explanation_en: Radiation fog is restricted to land because water surfaces cool little from nighttime radiation. Answer (B) is incorrect. Water surfaces cool little from nighttime radiation, therefore, radiation fog would not be close to water or over water. Answer (C) is incorrect. When rain soaks the ground, followed by clearing skies, radiation fog is not uncommon the following morning. Ground fog usually burns off rather rapidly after sunrise. Other radiation fog generally clears before noon unless clouds move in over the fog. Radiation fog does not form under cloudy skies. It always forms over land.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Precipitation-induced fog

choices.text: results from relatively cooler rain or drizzle falling through warmer air.
results from relatively warmer rain or drizzle falling through cooler air.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Precipitation-induced fog는 비교적 따뜻한 비나 drizzle이 더 차가운 공기층을 통과할 때 형성되며 넓은 지역을 덮어 항공운항을 중단시킬 정도로 발달할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Precipitation-induced fog results from relatively warmer rain or drizzle falling through cooler air. This fog may extend over large areas, completely suspending air operations. Answer (A) is incorrect. Precipitation-induced fog can become quite dense and continue for an extended period of time. Answer (B) is incorrect. Precipitation-induced fog is the result of warmer, not cooler, rain or drizzle falling through cooler air.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Visibility above a haze layer is poor when looking
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Haze는 안정한 공기에서 잘 나타나며 보통 두께가 수천 ft이지만 때로 15,000 ft까지 이를 수 있다. Haze layer 위에서 아래를 내려다보는 시정은 좋지 않다.
questions.explanation_en: Haze occurs in stable air and is usually only a few thousand feet thick, but sometimes may extend as high as 15,000 feet. Downward visibility above a haze layer is poor. Answer (A) is incorrect. Forward visibility above a haze layer is normally good. Visibility in haze varies greatly depending upon whether the pilot is facing the sun. Answer (C) is incorrect. Downward visibility above a haze layer is poor. Visibility looking upward above a haze layer would be dependent on cloud conditions and be independent of the haze layer condition.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Stratus clouds are known for

choices.text: some turbulence and small amounts of icing.
little or no turbulence with hazardous icing at temperatures near or below freezing.
some turbulence and not significant icing.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Stratus는 난류가 매우 적은 편이지만 온도가 빙점 부근 또는 그 이하이면 심각한 icing 위험이 될 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Stratus clouds are known for very little turbulence but can pose a serious icing problem if temperatures are near or below freezing. Answer (A) is incorrect. Altocumulus clouds are known for some turbulence and small amounts of icing. Answer (C) is incorrect. Cumulus clouds are known for some turbulence and not significant icing.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Flight in haze

choices.text: is often hazardous when landing into the sun.
does not restrict visibility forward or below the aircraft.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Haze가 있을 때 태양을 정면으로 향해 착륙하면 시정이 크게 나빠져 위험할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Landing an aircraft into the sun is often hazardous if haze is present. Answer (A) is incorrect. Visibility overhead is normally not affected by haze. Answer (C) is incorrect. Haze definitely causes visibility restriction, especially when looking into or facing the sun.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Advection fog usually deepens in winds up to about
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Advection fog는 해안지역에서 가장 흔하지만 내륙 깊숙한 곳에서도 생길 수 있다. 풍속이 약 15 kt까지 증가할수록 깊어지는 경향이 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Advection fog is most common along coastal areas but can also develop deep in continental areas. Advection fog deepens as wind speed increases up to about 15 knots. Answer (B) is incorrect. Advection fog deepens as wind speed increases up to about 15 knots, not 10 knots. Answer (C) is incorrect. A wind speed of 5 knots would not cause advection fog to deepen, but 15 knots would.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Significant precipitation usually requires clouds to be
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 의미 있는 강수를 만들려면 구름 두께가 일반적으로 약 4,000 ft 이상이어야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: To produce significant precipitation, clouds usually are 4,000 feet thick or more. Answer (A) is incorrect. To produce significant precipitation, clouds would have to be 4,000 feet, not 2,000 feet, thick. Answer (B) is incorrect. To produce significant precipitation, clouds would have to be 4,000 feet, not 3,000 feet, thick.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: When does minimum temperature normally occur during a 24-hour period?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Diurnal variation은 24시간 동안의 기온변화이다. 최저기온은 보통 일출 직후, 경우에 따라 약 1시간 뒤에 나타난다.
questions.explanation_en: Diurnal variation is the change in temperature within a 24-hr. period. The minimum temperature normally occurs after sunrise, sometimes as much as 1 hr. after. Answer (B) is incorrect. The minimum temperature normally occurs after, not before, sunrise. Answer (C) is incorrect. The minimum temperature normally occurs after sunrise, not at midnight.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Temperature and radiation variations over land with a clear sky typically lead to

choices.text: outgoing terrestrial radiation peaking at noon.
temperature reaching a maximum closer to noon than to sunset.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 밤에는 태양가열이 없지만 지표의 terrestrial radiation은 계속되어 일출 직후까지 냉각된다. 들어오는 태양복사가 지표의 복사손실을 다시 넘어서기 시작하기 전까지 냉각되므로 최저기온은 보통 일출 직후에 나타난다.
questions.explanation_en: At night, heating is absent, but terrestrial radiation continues cooling the earth’s surface. Cooling continues until shortly after sunrise, when incoming solar radiation once again exceeds outgoing terrestrial radiation. Minimum surface air temperature usually occurs shortly after sunrise. Answer (B) is incorrect. Outgoing radiation peaks during the nighttime when no isolation occurs. Answer (C) is incorrect. Peak isolation occurs around noon, but maximum surface air temperature occurs during mid-afternoon.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which term applies when the temperature of the air changes by compression or expansion with no heat added or removed?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 공기가 팽창하면 냉각되고 압축되면 가열된다. 외부와 열의 출입 없이 일어나는 이런 변화를 adiabatic change라 한다.
questions.explanation_en: When air expands, it cools; when compressed, it warms. These changes are adiabatic, meaning that no heat is removed from or added to the air. Answer (A) is incorrect. Katabatic is a wind blowing down an incline caused by cold, heavier air spilling down the incline displacing warmer, less dense air. Answer (B) is incorrect. Advection is the horizontal flow in a convective current, i.e., wind.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is the approximate rate unsaturated air will cool flowing upslope?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 불포화 공기는 상승 시 약 3°C(5.4°F)/1,000 ft의 dry adiabatic rate로 냉각되고 하강 시 같은 비율로 가열된다.
questions.explanation_en: Unsaturated air moving upward and downward cools and warms at about 3°C (5.4°F) per 1,000 ft. This is the dry adiabatic rate of temperature change. Answer (B) is incorrect. Unsaturated air will cool flowing upslope at 3°C, not 2°C, per 1,000 ft. Answer (C) is incorrect. Unsaturated air will cool flowing upslope at 3°C, not 4°C, per 1,000 ft.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which process causes adiabatic cooling?

choices.text: Expansion of air as it rises.
Movement of air over a colder surface.
Release of latent heat during the vaporization process.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 상승하는 공기는 주위 기압이 낮아지면서 팽창하고, 그 팽창 때문에 adiabatic cooling이 발생한다.
questions.explanation_en: Adiabatic cooling is caused by the expansion of air as it rises. Any time air is moved upward, it expands because of decreasing atmospheric pressure. When air expands, it cools. Answer (B) is incorrect. Adiabatic cooling means that no heat is removed from the air, as would be the case if the air were moved over a colder surface. Answer (C) is incorrect. Adiabatic is the process in which no heat is removed from or added to the air.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What weather condition occurs at the altitude where the dewpoint lapse rate and the dry adiabatic lapse rate converge?

choices.text: Stable air changes to unstable air.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 대류 중 불포화 공기는 약 3°C/1,000 ft로 냉각되고 dew point는 약 0.56°C/1,000 ft로 감소한다. 두 값이 만나는 고도가 convective cloud base가 된다.
questions.explanation_en: The altitude where the dew point lapse rate and the dry adiabatic lapse rate converge is where convective cloud bases form. Unsaturated air in a convective current cools at about 3.0°C (5.4°F) per 1,000 ft.; dew point decreases at about 5/9°C (1°F) per 1,000 ft. When they converge, cloud bases form. Answer (B) is incorrect. Precipitation starts when precipitation particles have grown to a size and weight that the atmosphere can no longer suspend and the particles fall as precipitation. Answer (C) is incorrect. Air stability depends on the ambient or existing temperature lapse rate, not the convergence of the dew point lapse rate and the dry adiabatic lapse rate.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which type wind flows downslope becoming warmer and dryer?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Katabatic wind는 차갑고 무거운 공기가 경사면을 따라 내려가며 앞의 따뜻하고 가벼운 공기를 밀어내면서 형성된다. 하강하면서 압축되어 adiabatic warming과 drying이 일어난다.
questions.explanation_en: Katabatic wind forms because cold, heavy air spills down sloping terrain displacing warmer, less dense air ahead of it. The cold, heavy air is adiabatically heated and dried as it flows downslope because of heating due to the downward air being compressed by increasing pressure. Answer (A) is incorrect. A land breeze is a wind that flows from the cooler land toward warmer water. Answer (B) is incorrect. A valley wind is wind flowing up out of a valley because colder, denser air settles downward and forces the warmer air near the ground up a mountain slope.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is indicated about an air mass if the temperature remains unchanged or decreases slightly as altitude is increased?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 고도가 올라가도 기온이 거의 변하지 않거나 아주 조금만 감소하면 그 기단은 안정한 경향이 있다.
questions.explanation_en: If the air temperature remains unchanged or decreases only slightly as altitude is increased, the air mass tends to be stable. Answer (A) is incorrect. Unstable air would have a uniform decrease (approaching 3°C/1,000 ft.) in temperature with an increase in altitude. Answer (B) is incorrect. In a temperature inversion, the temperature increases with increases in altitude.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which condition is present when a local parcel of air is stable?

choices.text: The parcel of air resists convection.
The parcel of air cannot be forced uphill.
As the parcel of air moves upward, its temperature becomes warmer than the surrounding air.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 안정한 공기는 대류를 억제한다. 공기덩어리가 강제로 상승해도 주변보다 차가워져 상승력이 사라지면 원래 위치로 돌아가려 하므로 자발적 대류가 어렵다.
questions.explanation_en: Stable air resists convection. If a parcel of air is lifted, it is cooler than the surrounding air and will return to its original position when the lifting force is removed. Spontaneous convection is impossible in stable air. Answer (B) is incorrect. Stable air can be forced uphill to form a mountain wave. Answer (C) is incorrect. Rising air warmer than the surrounding air describes unstable, not stable, air.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: The stability of an air mass can usually be determined by

choices.text: measuring the dry adiabatic lapse rate.
cloud types and the type of precipitation.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 대기 안정도는 수직운동을 좌우한다. 안정한 공기는 수직운동을 억제해 얕고 층상인 stratus형 구름과 넓고 지속적인 강수를 만들고, 불안정한 공기는 수직발달이 큰 cumulus/cumulonimbus와 짧지만 강한 강수를 만들기 쉽다.
questions.explanation_en: Atmospheric stability influences weather by affecting the vertical motion of air. Stable air suppresses vertical motion while unstable air enhances it. Clouds formed in stable air will be shallow and layered, like stratus clouds. Clouds formed in unstable air will have more height and be of the cumulus or cumulonimbus type. Precipitation from stratus clouds tends to be over large areas and lasts for long periods. Precipitation from cumulus clouds tends to be more intense and over short periods. Answer (A) is incorrect. The tropopause is a thin boundary area between the troposphere and the stratosphere. The height of the tropopause varies widely due to the location above the earth and the time of the year and is not necessarily indicative of air mass stability. Answer (B) is incorrect. Stability is determined by the change in the ambient lapse rate not the dry lapse rate.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: When saturated air moves downhill, its temperature increases

choices.text: at a faster rate than dry air because of the release of latent heat.
at a slower rate than dry air because vaporization uses heat.
at a slower rate than dry air because condensation releases heat.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 포화공기가 산 아래로 내려오며 온도가 올라갈 때는 수분의 증발에 latent heat가 사용되므로 건조공기보다 가열률이 작다.
questions.explanation_en: When saturated air moves downhill, its temperature increases at a slower rate than dry air because vaporization uses heat known as the “latent heat of vaporization.” The water removal cools the air from which the water is removed. Answer (A) is incorrect. When saturated air moves downhill, its temperature increases at a slower, not faster, rate than dry air because of the absorption, not release, of latent heat. Answer (C) is incorrect. As air moves downhill, its temperature increases at a slower rate than dry air because vaporization uses heat, not because of the release of heat through condensation.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Adiabatic warming is also described as
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Adiabatic warming은 건조공기가 하강하면서 압축되어 외부 열공급 없이 온도가 상승하는 과정이다.
questions.explanation_en: Adiabatic warming (heating) is a process of heating dry air through compression. For example, as air moves down a slope it is compressed, which results in an increase in temperature. Answer (B) is incorrect. Solar warming is due to the sun transferring heat through radiation. Answer (C) is incorrect. Expansional heating would be a process of a liquid, such as water expanding from heat. It has nothing to do with adiabatic warming.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: How can the stability of the atmosphere be determined?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 기단의 안정도는 실제 환경감률과 상승공기의 adiabatic cooling rate 차이로 결정된다. 지표가열이나 상층냉각은 불안정을 강화하고, 지표냉각이나 상층가열은 안정을 강화한다.
questions.explanation_en: The difference between the ambient temperature lapse rate of a given mass of air and the adiabatic rates of cooling in upward-moving air determines the stability of the air. For example, surface heating or cooling aloft tends to make the air unstable, while surface cooling or warming aloft tends to make the air more stable. Answer (B) is incorrect. The difference between ambient temperature and adiabatic lapse rate, not atmospheric pressure at various levels, determines stability. Answer (C) is incorrect. The surface temperature/dew point spread is used to indicate probability of fog, not atmospheric stability.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Large areas of land
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 육지는 수면보다 일교차가 훨씬 크다. 수면에서는 하루 최대·최저 기온 차가 약 10°C일 수 있지만 육지에서는 최대 약 50°C까지도 가능하다.
questions.explanation_en: Large areas of land increase temperature variations. While a daily maximum and minimum temperature change may be only 10°C over water, a change of up to 50°C can occur over land. Answer (B) is incorrect. The troposphere is dramatically affected by the terrestrial surface. Solar radiation warms the land by heating the surface. The warm surface increases the temperature of the air above by terrestrial radiation. Answer (C) is incorrect. Large areas of land do not minimize temperature variations in the troposphere. Large land masses tend to increase the temperature variations in the troposphere.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: The air is 100% saturated with vapor at
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 상대습도는 실제 수증기량을 그 온도에서 최대로 포함할 수 있는 수증기량과 비교한 백분율이다. 100%이면 포화 상태이며 기온과 dew point가 같다.
questions.explanation_en: Relative humidity is expressed as a percent. It relates the actual water vapor present to that which could be present. Air with 100% humidity is saturated and is the dew-point temperature. Answer (A) is incorrect. The wet-bulb temperature is the temperature a parcel of air would have if it were cooled to saturation (100% relative humidity) by the evaporation of water into it with the latent heat being supplied by the parcel. In other words, this is the coolest temperature a parcel of air can achieve when evaporation is the only method of cooling applied. Answer (B) is incorrect. Humidity index is an index of the effect on human comfort of temperature and humidity levels.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Any wind blowing down an incline where the incline is influential in causing the wind is a
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Katabatic wind는 경사면이 원인이 되어 아래쪽으로 부는 바람을 말하며 mountain wind가 그 예이다.
questions.explanation_en: A katabatic wind is any wind blowing down an incline when the incline is influential in causing the wind. Mountain wind is a katabatic wind. Answer (A) is incorrect. A land breeze flows from land to water and is much smaller and weaker than a katabatic wind. Answer (B) is incorrect. Katabatic wind flows down an incline of a mountain, where the valley wind may not reach the crest of the mountain and is basically within the valley area.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Land surface heating on the coast results in
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 낮에는 차가운 바다에서 더 따뜻한 육지 쪽으로 부는 바람이 sea breeze이다.
questions.explanation_en: During the day, the wind that blows from the cool water to warm the land is a sea breeze. Answer (A) is incorrect. A chinook wind is a warm, dry wind that blows down the east side of the Rocky Mountains at the end of winter. Answer (B) is incorrect. At night the wind blows from cool land to warmer water and creates a land breeze.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Land surface cooling on the coast results in
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 밤에는 더 차가운 육지에서 상대적으로 따뜻한 수면 쪽으로 바람이 불며 이를 land breeze라 한다.
questions.explanation_en: At night, the wind blows from cool land to warmer water and creates a land breeze. Answer (A) is incorrect. A chinook wind is a warm, dry wind that blows down the east side of the Rocky Mountains at the end of winter. Answer (C) is incorrect. During the day, the wind that blows from the cool water to warm the land is a sea breeze.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Where is a common location for an inversion?

choices.text: At the base of cumulus clouds.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Temperature inversion은 고도가 증가할수록 기온이 상승하는 현상으로 어느 고도에서나 발생할 수 있고 stratosphere에서도 흔하다.
questions.explanation_en: Inversions may occur at any altitude and are common in the stratosphere. An inversion is an increase in temperature with an increase in altitude. Answer (A) is incorrect. A common location for an inversion is in the stratosphere, not at the tropopause. Answer (C) is incorrect. The base of cumulus clouds is where the dew point lapse rate and the dry adiabatic lapse rate converge. It is not a common location for an inversion.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What feature is associated with a temperature inversion?
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 기온역전에서는 정상적인 lapse rate가 뒤집혀 고도와 함께 기온이 상승한다. 이때 공기는 매우 안정해져 수직 혼합이 억제된다.
questions.explanation_en: A temperature inversion is defined as an increase in temperature with height; i.e., the normal lapse rate is inverted. Thus, any warm air rises to its own temperature and forms a stable layer of air. Answer (B) is incorrect. Instability occurs when the temperature decreases, not increases as in a temperature inversion, with an increase in altitude and the rising air continues to rise. Answer (C) is incorrect. Air mass thunderstorms result from instability. They do not occur when there is a temperature inversion.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What condition produces the most frequent type of ground-or surface-based temperature inversion?

choices.text: The movement of colder air under warm air or the movement of warm air over cold air.
Widespread sinking of air within a thick layer aloft resulting in heating by compression.
Terrestrial radiation on a clear, relatively calm night.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 맑고 서늘하며 바람이 약한 밤에는 지표가 상층 공기보다 빠르게 복사냉각되어 지면 부근에 inversion이 잘 형성된다.
questions.explanation_en: An inversion often develops near the ground on clear, cool nights when the wind is relatively calm. The ground radiates heat and cools much faster than the overlying air. Air in contact with the ground becomes cold, while the temperature a few hundred feet above changes very little. Answer (A) is incorrect. The movement of colder air under warm air is what happens when a cold front is advancing, and the movement of warm air over cold air is the process of an advancing warm front. Answer (B) is incorrect. Widespread sinking of air describes compressional or adiabatic heating.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What characterizes a ground-based inversion?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Ground-based inversion은 안개·연기·오염물질을 하층에 가두므로 시정이 나빠지는 특징이 있다.
questions.explanation_en: A ground-based inversion is characterized by poor visibility as a result of trapping fog, smoke, and other restrictions into low levels of the atmosphere. Answer (A) is incorrect. Convective currents at the surface do not occur when there is a ground-based inversion. Answer (B) is incorrect. When the temperature is cold, it is difficult for the earth to radiate enough heat to become colder than the overlying air.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which is a necessary condition for the occurrence of a low-level temperature inversion wind shear?

choices.text: The temperature differential between the cold and warm layers must be at least 10°C.
A calm or light wind near the surface and a relatively strong wind just above the inversion.
A wind direction difference of at least 30° between the wind near the surface and the wind just above the inversion.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 맑은 밤에 지상풍이 calm 또는 light이고 inversion 바로 위에 상대적으로 강한 바람이 있으면 low-level temperature inversion wind shear가 발생하기 쉽다.
questions.explanation_en: A temperature inversion forms near the surface on a clear night with calm or light surface wind, and a relatively strong wind just above the inversion is necessary to form a low-level temperature inversion wind shear. Answer (A) is incorrect. Magnitude of temperature differential in the inversion is not important; the wind shear is caused by the variation in wind speed. Answer (C) is incorrect. Surface wind and a relatively strong wind just above the inversion, not a wind direction difference of at least 30°, are needed to form a low-level temperature inversion wind shear. The wind shear is caused by wind speed variation, not variation in wind direction.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: An inversion aloft with temperatures below freezing can

choices.text: result in the possibility of freezing rain.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 전선면 아래에서 freezing rain이 내리면 clear ice가 빠르게 축적될 수 있다. 전선 위 따뜻한 층에서 생긴 비가 영하층을 통과하며 supercooled된 뒤 항공기 표면에 충돌해 즉시 언다.
questions.explanation_en: A condition favorable for rapid accumulation of clear icing is freezing rain below a frontal surface. Rain forms above the frontal surface at temperatures warmer than freezing. It falls through air at temperatures below freezing and becomes supercooled. The supercooled drops freeze on impact with an aircraft surface. Answer (B) is incorrect. Supercooled drops resulting from an inversion aloft with temperatures below freezing freeze on impact with an aircraft surface producing ice, not frost. Answer (C) is incorrect. Supercooled drops resulting from an inversion aloft with temperatures below freezing are raindrops, not hailstones.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: An increase in temperature with an altitude increase

choices.text: denotes the beginning of the stratosphere.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 일반적으로 상승하는 공기는 팽창해 냉각되지만, 고도가 올라갈수록 기온이 상승한다면 temperature inversion이 존재하는 것이다.
questions.explanation_en: Normally, as air rises and expands in the atmosphere, the temperature decreases. However, when the temperature of the air rises with altitude, this indicates that a temperature inversion exists. Answer (B) is incorrect. Although the temperature does begin to increase in the stratosphere, only specialized aircraft are likely to be able to operate high enough to see this change. Answer (C) is incorrect. A cold front passage does not always cause the temperature to increase with altitude. If it did, this would be an indication of an inversion.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: En route at FL 270, the altimeter is set correctly. On descent, a pilot fails to set the local altimeter setting of 30.57. If the field elevation is 650 feet, and the altimeter is functioning properly, what will it indicate upon landing?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. FL270에서 29.92를 설정한 채 실제 altimeter setting 30.57로 바꾸지 않고 강하하면 0.65 inHg 차이로 약 650 ft 낮게 지시한다. 표고 650 ft 공항에 착륙하면 고도계는 약 0 ft를 가리키게 된다.
questions.explanation_en: If an altimeter is set to 29.92 for flight at FL 270 and is not adjusted to the correct altimeter setting of 30.57 during descent, the altimeter will indicate an altitude lower than actual by 650 ft. (1,000 ft. × the difference between the two altimeter settings, which is .65). Thus, if the airplane lands at an airport with a field elevation of 650 ft., the altimeter will indicate sea level (650 ft. airport elevation – 650 ft. altimeter setting error). Answer (A) is incorrect. The figure of 585 ft. is obtained by subtracting 65 ft. rather than subtracting 650 ft. Answer (B) is incorrect. The figure of 1,300 ft. is obtained by adding 650 ft. rather than subtracting 650 ft.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: If the ambient temperature is colder than standard at FL 310, what is the relationship between true altitude and pressure altitude?

choices.text: They are both the same, 31,000 feet.
True altitude is lower than 31,000 feet.
Pressure altitude is lower than true altitude.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. FL310에서 표준보다 찬 공기에서는 압력면이 압축되어 실제고도(true altitude)가 pressure altitude보다 낮다. 즉 'high to low, look out below' 상황이다.
questions.explanation_en: At FL 310, the altimeter is set to pressure altitude (29.92). If the outside air temperature (ambient) is colder than standard, the air is compressed and heavier in weight per unit volume than on a warm day. Thus, in colder-than-standard air, the true altitude is lower than the pressure altitude. Answer (A) is incorrect. Both true and pressure altitudes are the same at FL 310 if the ambient air temperature is standard, not colder than standard. Answer (C) is incorrect. Pressure altitude is lower than true altitude in warmer-, not colder-, than-standard air temperature.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: If the ambient temperature is warmer than standard at FL 350, what is the density altitude compared to pressure altitude?

choices.text: Impossible to determine without information on possible inversion layers at lower altitudes.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Density altitude는 pressure altitude를 비표준 온도로 보정한 값이다. 표준보다 따뜻하면 공기가 팽창해 같은 pressure level이 더 높은 실제고도에 위치한다.
questions.explanation_en: Density altitude, by definition, is pressure altitude adjusted for nonstandard temperature. When the ambient air temperature is warmer than standard, the expanded air is lighter in weight per unit volume than on a cold day, and the pressure levels are raised. Thus, the pressure level where the altimeter indicates FL 350 is higher on a warm day than under standard conditions. Answer (A) is incorrect. Density altitude is higher, not lower, when air temperature is warmer than standard. Answer (C) is incorrect. Density altitude is pressure altitude corrected for nonstandard temperatures. Pressure altitude is based on a standard pressure atmosphere at a particular altitude, and inversion layers at lower levels have no effect on pressure altitude.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: What is corrected altitude (approximate true altitude)?

choices.text: Pressure altitude corrected for instrument error.
Indicated altitude corrected for temperature variation from standard.
Density altitude corrected for temperature variation from standard.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Corrected altitude는 indicated altitude를 표준대기와의 온도차로 보정한 값으로 true altitude의 근사값이다.
questions.explanation_en: Corrected altitude is the indicated altitude of an airplane’s altimeter corrected for temperature variation from standard atmospheric temperature. This is an approximation of true altitude. Answer (A) is incorrect. Pressure altitude corrected for instrument error is a nonsense concept. Answer (C) is incorrect. Density altitude is pressure altitude corrected for temperature variation from standard. Density altitude is a final figure and not subject to additional adjustments.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: Which pressure is defined as station pressure?

choices.text: Station barometric pressure reduced to sea level.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Station pressure는 측정지점, 즉 공항 field elevation에서 실제로 측정한 기압이다.
questions.explanation_en: Pressure can be measured only at the point of measurement. The pressure measured at a station or airport is “station pressure,” or the actual pressure at field elevation. Answer (A) is incorrect. Altimeter setting is the value to which the scale of a pressure altimeter is adjusted to read field elevation. Answer (C) is incorrect. Station barometric pressure reduced to sea level is a method to readily compare station pressures between stations at different altitudes.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.question: At an indicated altitude of 9,000 feet with a temperature of 85°F, density altitude is
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 85°F는 약 29.4°C이다. Pressure altitude 9,000 ft와 약 29°C를 E6B에 적용하면 density altitude는 약 12,750 ft, 가장 가까운 값은 12,800 ft이다.
questions.explanation_en: Using your E6B on the flight computer side, find the conversion for Celsius to Fahrenheit at the bottom of the flight computer. The temperature of 85°F is about 29.4°C. Now go to the pressure altitude scale and line up just past the mark for 29°C to 9,000 ft. pressure altitude. Note the density altitude arrow points to about 12,750 feet. The closest answer is 12,800 feet. Answer (A) is incorrect. A density altitude of 13,900 feet would require a temperature of about 44°C. Answer (C) is incorrect. A density altitude of 11,400 feet would require a temperature of about 15°C.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
