questions.explanation_en: A narrower-than-usual runway can create an illusion that the aircraft is at a higher altitude than it actually is, which could result in striking objects along the flight path or landing short. Answer (B) is incorrect. Runway width has no effect on the perceived speed in an approach to landing. Answer (C) is incorrect. A wider-, not narrower-, than-usual runway can create the illusion that the aircraft is lower than actual altitude, creating the risk of the pilot leveling out the aircraft high and landing hard or overshooting the runway.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: What illusion, if any, can rain on the windscreen create?
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Windshield의 rain은 실제보다 runway 위에서 더 높게 있는 것처럼 보이게 해 조종사가 낮은 접근을 하도록 만들 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Rain on the windscreen can create the illusion of greater height above the runway. The pilot who does not recognize this illusion will fly a lower approach. Answer (A) is incorrect. Rain on the windscreen can create the illusion of being higher than actual. Answer (B) is incorrect. Rain on the windscreen can create the illusion of being higher, not lower, than actual.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: You have just touched down hard on a narrower than usual runway at night. You realize you just experienced
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Hard landing은 늦은 flare와 연관될 수 있으며, 좁은 활주로가 실제보다 높게 느끼게 하는 runway-width illusion이 원인이 될 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: A hard landing implies a late flare, which can be caused by runway width illusion. A narrower-than-usual runway can create the illusion that the airplane is at a higher-than-actual altitude. Answer (B) is incorrect. There is no defined runway elevation illusion; however, the runway width illusion can give a pilot the impression (s)he is at a higher altitude than (s)he really is, leading to a hard landing due to a late flare for landing. Answer (C) is incorrect. The featureless terrain illusion assumes the runway is not in proximity to any visible ground features. This illusion can result from overwater landings, snow covered landscapes, or dark ground. A hard landing on a narrow runway implies the pilot suffered from the runway width illusion, not a featureless terrain illusion.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: Staring at static light in the darkness can create the illusion of

choices.text: autokinesis which could lead to loss of control.
halo vision and night vision loss.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Autokinesis는 어두운 곳의 정지된 불빛을 몇 초 이상 응시하면 움직이는 것처럼 보이는 현상이다.
questions.explanation_en: Autokinesis occurs when a static, or stationary, light in the dark appears to move about when stared at for many seconds. The disoriented pilot will lose control of the aircraft in attempting to align it with the light. Answer (A) is incorrect. Autonomic involuntary muscle response can happen day or night. It is controlled by the nervous system. Answer (C) is incorrect. Halos are bright circles that appear to surround a source of light, such as oncoming car headlights. Night vision loss is from white lights shining in the eyes. Autokinesis happens with even dim lights and does not cause night vision loss.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: You just touched down faster than planned in haze on a runway at night. You realize you have just experienced
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Haze는 runway가 더 멀리 있는 것처럼 느끼게 해 낮은 접근을 만들고, 정상보다 빠른 속도로 갑자기 touchdown할 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Atmospheric haze can create the illusion of being at a greater distance from the runway. The pilot who does not recognize this illusion will fly a lower approach, abruptly touching down at a faster than normal landing speed. Answer (B) is incorrect. Runway width illusion is created by a narrower-than-usual runway. The pilot who does not recognize this illusion will fly a lower approach and risk striking objects along the approach path or landing short. Answer (C) is incorrect. An absence of ground features can create the illusion that the aircraft is at a higher altitude than it actually is. The pilot who does not recognize this illusion will fly a lower approach and a hard, short landing.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.question: You just touched down hard in the rain on a narrower than usual runway at night. You have just experienced
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Windshield rain과 narrow-runway illusion은 모두 실제보다 높게 느끼게 하므로 조종사가 낮은 접근을 해 hard landing으로 이어질 수 있다.
questions.explanation_en: Rain in the windscreen can create the illusion of greater height. Runway width illusion (narrower-than-usual runway) can create the illusion that the aircraft is at a higher altitude than it actually is. The pilot who does not recognize these two together will fly a lower approach that results in a hard landing. Answer (A) is incorrect. Ground lighting illusion is caused by lights along a straight path such as a road, and even lights on moving trains can be mistaken for runway and approach lights. The pilot who does not recognize this illusion will fly a higher than normal approach, landing long. Answer (B) is incorrect. Runway length illusion with a runway that is short will cause the pilot who does not recognize this illusion to fly a higher than normal approach. A runway that is longer will cause just the opposite. The pilot who does not recognize this illusion will fly a lower approach.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: Human behavior

choices.text: rarely results in accidents unless deliberate actions are performed.
causes three out of four accidents.
is well understood, so behavioral induced accidents are exceedingly rare occurrences.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Human behavior 연구는 사람이 왜 특정 방식으로 행동하는지 이해해 항공 human error의 결과를 줄이는 데 사용된다. 오류 자체를 완전히 제거할 수는 없으므로 예측 가능한 오류를 훈련과 시스템으로 관리하는 것이 핵심이다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: The study of human behavior is an attempt to explain how and why humans function the way they do. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) utilizes studies of human behavior in an attempt to reduce human error in aviation. Three out of four accidents result from human error. Eliminating human error is an unrealistic goal since errors are a normal part of human behavior. On the other hand, realizing that many aviation accidents are preventable means designing ways to reduce the consequences of human error. The study of human behavior coupled with pilot training that offsets predictable human error helps achieve that goal. Answer (A) is incorrect. Many aviation accidents are preventable and are based on human error. In fact, three out of four accidents are a result of human error, which is a normal part of human behavior. Answer (C) is incorrect. Three out of four accidents are a result of human error. Many aviation accidents are preventable, and continued study of human behavior is a necessary step in the goal of reducing the consequences of human error.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: Risk management, as part of the aeronautical decision making (ADM) process, relies on which features to reduce the risks associated with each flight?

choices.text: Application of stress management and risk element procedures.
The mental process of analyzing all information in a particular situation and making a timely decision on what action to take.
Situational awareness, problem recognition, and good judgment.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Risk management는 ADM의 일부로 situational awareness, problem recognition, good judgment를 이용해 각 비행의 위험을 줄이는 과정이다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: Risk management is that part of the ADM process which relies on situational awareness, problem recognition, and good judgment to reduce risks associated with each flight. Answer (A) is incorrect. Risk management relies on situational awareness, problem recognition, and good judgment, not the application of stress management and risk-element procedures, to reduce the risks associated with each flight. Answer (B) is incorrect. Judgment, not risk management, is the mental process of analyzing all information in a particular situation and making a timely decision on what action to take.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: Risk is increased when flightcrew members

choices.text: fail to monitor automated navigation systems.
allocate time to verify expected performance of automated systems.
question the performance of each other’s duties.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 시스템을 감시하지 않고 결과를 확인하지 않으면 조종사는 운항에서 분리되어 'passenger in command'처럼 complacency에 빠질 수 있다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: By failing to monitor systems and failing to check the results of the processes, the pilot becomes detached from the aircraft operations and slides into the complacent role of passenger in command. Answer (B) is incorrect. Monitoring and verifying the performance of automated systems enhances the crew’s situational awareness of the progress of the flight and aircraft performance. Answer (C) is incorrect. Consciously or subconsciously cross-checking the performance of each other’s duties reduces the risk of an error and enhances safety.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: The most important key to risk management is

choices.text: the sense of security provided by experience.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. External pressure 관리는 risk management에서 특히 중요하다. 시간·일정 압박은 조종사가 다른 모든 위험요인을 무시하게 만들 수 있고 많은 사고에 관여한다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: Management of external pressures is the single most important key to risk management because it is the one risk factor category that can cause a pilot to ignore all the other risk factors. External pressures put time-related pressure on the pilot and figure into a majority of accidents. Answer (A) is incorrect. Predisposition is an attitude or tendency to act in a certain way. Although understanding this can alleviate risk, it is not the most important factor in good risk management. Answer (C) is incorrect. A sense of security does not necessarily mean that risks have been properly managed, and it may lead to complacency, thereby compounding the existing risks.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: Aeronautical decision making (ADM) can be defined as a

choices.text: mental process of analyzing all available information in a particular situation, making a timely decision on what action to take, and when to take the action.
decision making process which relies on good judgment to reduce risks associated with each flight.
systematic approach to the mental process used by pilots to consistently determine the best course of action in response to a given set of circumstances.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. ADM은 주어진 상황에서 최선의 행동을 일관되게 선택하기 위한 체계적인 mental decision-making process이다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: ADM is a systematic approach to the mental process used by pilots to consistently determine the best course of action in response to a given set of circumstances. Answer (A) is incorrect. Judgment, not ADM, can be defined as a mental process of analyzing all available information in a particular situation and making a timely decision on what action to take and when to take the action. Answer (B) is incorrect. ADM relies not only on good judgment but also on the importance of attitudes in the decision-making process to reduce risks associated with each flight.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: The aeronautical decision making (ADM) process identifies several steps involved in good decision making. One of these steps is

choices.text: making a rational evaluation of the required actions.
identifying personal attitudes hazardous to safe flight.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. ADM에는 여러 좋은 의사결정 단계가 포함되며 그중 하나가 안전비행에 위험한 개인의 hazardous attitude를 식별하는 것이다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: The ADM process addresses all aspects of decision making on the flight deck and identifies several steps involved in good decision making. One of these steps is to identify personal attitudes hazardous to safe flight. Answer (A) is incorrect. Making a rational evaluation of the required actions is a step in good judgment, not a step in good decision making. Answer (C) is incorrect. The “can do,” or macho, attitude is one of the personal hazardous attitudes to identify in the steps involved in good decision making.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: Examples of classic behavioral traps that experienced pilots may fall into are to

choices.text: promote situational awareness and then necessary changes in behavior.
complete a flight as planned, please passengers, meet schedules, and “get the job done.”
assume additional responsibilities and assert PIC authority.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 경험 많은 조종사도 계획대로 비행을 끝내려는 강박, 승객을 만족시키려는 욕구, 일정 준수 압박, '일을 끝내야 한다'는 집착 같은 classic behavioral trap에 빠질 수 있다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: Pilots have been known to fall into a number of classic behavioral traps. Pilots, particularly those with considerable experience, as a rule always try to complete a flight as planned, please passengers, meet schedules, and do what it takes to “get the job done.” Answer (A) is incorrect. To promote situational awareness and then to make necessary changes in behavior are part of learning good decision making, not classic behavioral traps. Answer (C) is incorrect. Assuming additional responsibilities and asserting PIC authority are not examples of classic behavioral traps.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: All experienced pilots have fallen prey to, or have been tempted by, one or more of these dangerous tendencies or behavior problems at some time in their career. Select the answer that best describes these tendencies.

choices.text: Deficiencies in instrument skills and knowledge of aircraft systems or limitations.
Peer pressure, loss of situational awareness, and operating with inadequate fuel reserves.
Performance deficiencies due to stress from human factors, such as fatigue, illness, or emotional problems.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 경험 많은 조종사도 peer pressure, situational awareness 상실, 불충분한 fuel reserve 운항 같은 위험한 행동경향에 빠질 수 있으므로 이를 인식하고 제거해야 한다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: All experienced pilots have fallen prey to, or have been tempted by, dangerous tendencies or behavior patterns. Some dangerous tendencies or behavior patterns, which must be identified and eliminated, include peer pressure, loss of situational awareness, and operating with inadequate fuel reserves. Answer (A) is incorrect. Deficiencies in instrument skills and knowledge of aircraft systems or limitations are factors that increase flight deck stress, not dangerous tendencies and behavior patterns that must be eliminated in experienced pilots. Answer (C) is incorrect. Performance deficiencies due to stress from human factors, such as fatigue, illness, or emotional problems, are factors that increase stress, not dangerous tendencies or behavior patterns that must be eliminated in experienced pilots.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: An experienced pilot trying to meet a schedule

choices.text: can expect the flight crew to alert them to problems or areas of concern.
will always err on the side of caution.
can fail to perceive operational pitfalls.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 일정을 맞추려는 distraction은 조종사와 승무원이 중요한 식별요소를 놓치게 해 흔한 operational pitfall로 이어질 수 있다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: The distraction of trying to meet the requirements of a schedule can cause a pilot, and even a flight crew, to miss key identifying factors and fall into common operational pitfalls. Answer (A) is incorrect. The pilot in command is solely responsible for the successful and safe outcome of the flight. (S)he should not rely on or expect crew members to ensure safety, but rather (s)he should prevent the preoccupation and distraction of trying to adhere to a schedule. Answer (B) is incorrect. A pilot focused on meeting a schedule is more likely to stray from the side of caution because (s)he is distracted with meeting a demand rather than the overall safety of the flight.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: In order to gain a realistic perspective on one’s attitude toward flying, a pilot should

choices.text: understand the need to complete the flight.
obtain both realistic and thorough flight instruction during training.
take a Self-Assessment Hazardous Attitude Inventory Test.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 자신의 비행 태도를 현실적으로 평가하려면 Self-Assessment Hazardous Attitude Inventory Test를 활용할 수 있다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: In order to gain a realistic perspective on one’s attitudes toward flying, a pilot should take a Self-Assessment Hazardous Attitude Inventory Test. Answer (A) is incorrect. The need to complete a flight is a behavioral trap that must be eliminated, not a way to gain a perspective on one’s attitudes toward flying. Answer (B) is incorrect. While realistic and thorough flight instruction during training improves skills, it does not enable a pilot to gain perspective on his or her attitude toward flying.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: Hazardous attitudes occur to every pilot to some degree at some time. What are some of these hazardous attitudes?

choices.text: Antiauthority, impulsivity, macho, resignation, and invulnerability.
Poor situational awareness, snap judgments, and lack of a decision making process.
Poor risk management and lack of stress management.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. ADM의 5가지 hazardous attitude는 antiauthority, impulsivity, invulnerability, macho, resignation이다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: The five hazardous attitudes addressed in the ADM process are antiauthority, impulsivity, invulnerability, macho, and resignation. Answer (B) is incorrect. Poor situational awareness and snap judgments are indications of the lack of a decision-making process, not hazardous attitudes. Answer (C) is incorrect. Poor risk management and lack of stress management lead to poor ADM and are not considered hazardous attitudes.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: Name some hazardous attitudes that can affect your judgment during the aeronautical decision making (ADM) process.
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 의사결정을 해치는 대표 5가지 hazardous attitude는 반권위적 태도, 충동성, 불사신적 사고, macho, resignation이다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: The five hazardous attitudes that can affect your judgment during the ADM process are antiauthority, impulsivity, invulnerability, macho, and resignation. Answer (A) is incorrect. Reevaluation is not a hazardous attitude in the ADM process. Answer (C) is incorrect. While peer pressure and stress levels may be factors contributing toward hazardous attitudes in the ADM process, they are not attitudes themselves.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: What should a pilot do when recognizing a thought as hazardous?

choices.text: Correct this hazardous thought by making a thorough risk assessment.
Label the thought as hazardous and then correct that thought by stating the corresponding antidote.
Avoid allowing this hazardous thought to develop.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Hazardous thought를 인식하면 먼저 위험한 생각이라고 label하고 해당 attitude의 antidote를 말해 교정해야 한다. 각 antidote를 미리 암기해 즉시 떠올릴 수 있어야 한다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: When you recognize a hazardous thought, you should label it as hazardous; then correct the attitude by stating the corresponding antidote. Antidotes should be memorized for each of the hazardous attitudes so that they automatically come to mind when needed. Answer (A) is incorrect. When you recognize a hazardous thought, you should label it as hazardous and then correct the attitude by stating the corresponding antidote, not by making a thorough risk assessment. Answer (C) is incorrect. While you do not want the hazardous thought to develop, the way to avoid this is to recognize and label the thought as hazardous and then correct it by stating the corresponding antidote.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: In the aeronautical decision making (ADM) process, what is the first step in neutralizing a hazardous attitude?

choices.text: Recognizing the invulnerability of the situation.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Hazardous attitude는 먼저 위험한 생각임을 인식한 뒤 안전한 행동으로 redirect함으로써 효과적으로 상쇄할 수 있다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: Hazardous attitudes, which contribute to poor pilot judgment, can be effectively counteracted by redirecting that hazardous attitude so that appropriate action can be taken. Recognition of hazardous thoughts is the first step in neutralizing them in the ADM process. Answer (B) is incorrect. Invulnerability is a hazardous attitude. The first step in neutralizing a hazardous attitude is to recognize it. Answer (C) is incorrect. Before a rational judgment can be made, the hazardous attitude must be recognized and then redirected so that appropriate action can be taken.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: Hazardous attitudes which contribute to poor pilot judgment can be effectively counteracted by

choices.text: taking meaningful steps to be more assertive with attitudes.
early recognition of these hazardous attitudes.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 위험한 생각을 발견하면 hazardous라고 명확히 인식·label하고 그에 맞는 antidote를 적용해 태도를 바꿔야 한다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: Hazardous attitudes, which contribute to poor pilot judgment, can be effectively counteracted by redirecting them so that appropriate action can be taken. When you recognize a hazardous thought, you should label it as hazardous; then correct the attitude by stating the corresponding antidote. Answer (B) is incorrect. You should respond to a hazardous attitude with an antidote, not with steps to be more assertive with attitudes. Answer (C) is incorrect. While the first step in neutralizing a hazardous attitude is recognition, to counteract the attitude you must state the appropriate antidote.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: What is the antidote for a pilot with a “macho” attitude?

choices.text: I’m not helpless. I can make a difference.
Follow the rules. They are usually right.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Macho attitude는 다른 사람에게 자신을 증명하려고 불필요한 위험을 감수하는 태도이다. Antidote는 'Taking chances is foolish.'이다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: Pilots exhibiting a macho attitude will try to prove themselves by taking risks in order to impress others. When this hazardous attitude is recognized, the pilot should state the antidote, “Taking chances is foolish.” Answer (A) is incorrect. The antidote for a resignation, not a macho, attitude is, “I’m not helpless. I can make a difference.” Answer (B) is incorrect. The antidote for an antiauthority, not a macho, attitude is, “Follow the rules. They are usually right.”

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: Success in reducing stress associated with a crisis on the flight deck begins with

choices.text: eliminating the more serious life and flight deck stress issues.
knowing the exact cause of the stress.
assessing stress areas in one’s personal life.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Cockpit crisis management의 stress를 줄이려면 먼저 자신의 삶 전반에 존재하는 stress를 개인적으로 평가하는 것이 중요하다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: If you hope to succeed in reducing stress associated with crisis management on the flight deck, it is essential to begin by making a personal assessment of stress in all areas of your life. Answer (A) is incorrect. In order to eliminate the more serious life and flight deck stress issues, you must first make an assessment of stress in all areas of your life to identify those stressors. Answer (B) is incorrect. In order to know the exact cause of the stress, you must first make an assessment of stress in all areas of your life to identify stressors and the causes of them.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: An air carrier aircraft flown into the ground while the crew is troubleshooting a landing gear fault is an example of
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Eastern Airlines Flight 401 사고는 landing gear 문제에 집중하다 crew가 situational awareness를 잃어 발생한 대표 사례로, 숙련된 승무원도 경계를 놓치면 SA를 상실할 수 있음을 보여준다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: This question describes Eastern Airlines Flight 401, which crashed into the Everglades causing 101 fatalities. The crew was working a landing gear problem and apparently lost situational awareness. That crash, while tragic, proves that even experienced crews can fall prey to a loss of situational awareness if they are not vigilant and do not take precautions to prevent that possibility. Answer (A) is incorrect. Neglect and reliance on memory would not cause a pilot or crew troubleshooting a landing gear fault to fly into the ground. Loss of situational awareness could and has resulted in that particular scenario, however. Answer (C) is incorrect. Lack of experience does not in and of itself cause pilots or crew members to fly into the ground while troubleshooting a landing gear or other system fault. Loss of situational awareness could and has resulted in that particular scenario, however, even when the pilots involved were experienced.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: To help manage flight deck stress, a pilot should

choices.text: think of life stress situations that are similar to those in flying.
try to relax and think rationally at the first sign of stress.
avoid situations that will degrade the ability to handle flight deck responsibilities.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Flight deck stress를 관리하려면 stress의 첫 징후에서 스스로 긴장을 풀고 합리적으로 생각하도록 훈련해야 한다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: To help manage flight deck stress, you must condition (teach) yourself to relax and think rationally at the first sign of stress. Answer (A) is incorrect. Many of the stress coping techniques practiced for life stress management are not practical in flight. Answer (C) is incorrect. Avoiding situations that will degrade a pilot’s ability to handle flight deck responsibilities is considered a part of risk management, not flight deck stress management.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: The DECIDE process consists of six elements to help provide a pilot a logical way of approaching aeronautical decision making. These elements are to

choices.text: estimate, determine, choose, identify, detect, and evaluate.
determine, evaluate, choose, identify, do, and eliminate.
detect, estimate, choose, identify, do, and evaluate.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. DECIDE model은 Detect, Estimate, Choose, Identify, Do, Evaluate의 6단계로 의사결정을 논리적으로 진행하게 한다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: The DECIDE model, comprised of six elements, is intended to provide a pilot with a logical way of approaching decision making. These six elements, using the acronym DECIDE, are detect, estimate, choose, identify, do, and evaluate. Answer (A) is incorrect. One of the elements of the DECIDE process is “do,” not “determine.” Answer (B) is incorrect. Two of the elements of the DECIDE process are “detect,” not “determine,” and “estimate,” not “eliminate.”

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: When a recently certificated pilot decides to not wait any longer for the fog and low ceilings to lift, this pilot may be exhibiting the hazardous
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 기상이 좋아질 근거가 없는데 'I can do it'이라고 판단해 계속 시도하는 것은 macho attitude의 예이며 성별과 관계없이 나타날 수 있다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: A pilot waiting for weather to improve, who then decides, “I can do it,” without any sign of improving conditions, is exhibiting the macho attitude. Although this is commonly thought of as a male trait, women pilots can also fall prey to the macho attitude. Answer (A) is incorrect. Resignation is characterized by a pilot who gives up and displays an attitude that suggests (s)he has bad luck, or that someone is plotting against them. Answer (C) is incorrect. An impulsive pilot tends to do the first thing that comes to mind. While impulsivity could be an answer, it is not as accurate as the “I can do it” attitude of the macho pilot.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: An air carrier crew fixated on completing the last flight of a four day trip often may exhibit
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. 정해진 시간에 집에 도착하는 등 특정 목표에 집착해 대안 행동을 무시하는 현상을 get-there-itis라 하며 조종사의 판단을 손상시킨다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: The desire to satisfy a specific personal goal, like getting home on time after a four-day trip, is known as get-there-itis. This fixation with meeting a specific goal impairs pilot judgment, sometimes causing them to disregard any alternative course of action. Answer (B) is incorrect. The described scenario suggests get-there-itis, the desire to achieve a specific goal regardless of outside influences and conditions. It does not describe a staged decision-making process. Answer (C) is incorrect. The naturalistic decision-making process is a methodical approach to decision-making that includes analysis of the pilot, aircraft, environment, and external factors.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: Automatic Decision-Making is
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Automatic decision-making은 훈련과 경험에 기반한 반사적 의사결정으로, 분석적 판단을 할 시간이 없는 비상상황에서 주로 사용된다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: Automatic decision-making is a reflexive process that is anchored in training and experience. It is most often used in emergencies when there is no time to practice more analytical decision-making alternatives. Answer (B) is incorrect. Automatic decision-making is not impulsive or rash. While the process works quickly, it requires the pilot to correlate the current situation to similar situations experienced previously in order to choose an appropriate course of action. Answer (C) is incorrect. Automatic decision-making is reflexive in nature, not internalized. The automatic decision-making process requires the pilot to correlate the current situation to similar situations experienced previously in order to choose an appropriate course of action.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: When a pilot believes advanced avionics enable operations closer to personal or environmental limits,

choices.text: greater utilization of the aircraft is achieved.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 첨단 avionics가 있다고 해서 안전을 과신해서는 안 된다. Judgment와 ADM은 기술을 안전으로 연결하는 역할을 하며, 조종사·항공기·환경·외부압력 조건에 따라 personal minimum의 safety buffer를 조정해야 한다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: Pilots should not be lulled into a false sense of security simply because they have advanced avionics. Judgment and aeronautical decision making serve as the bridge between technology and safety. Any flight you make involves almost infinite combinations of pilot skill, experience, condition, and proficiency; aircraft equipment and performance; environmental conditions; and external influences. Both individually and in combination, these factors can compress the safety buffer provided by your baseline personal minimums. Consequently, you need a practical way to adjust your baseline personal minimums to accommodate specific conditions. Answer (A) is incorrect. While one may be able to use an aircraft in more challenging environments, the risks involved with such flights also increase. Therefore, the best answer choice is that risk is increased when a pilot believes advanced avionics enable operations closer to personal or environmental limits. Answer (C) is incorrect. Risk is increased, not decreased, when a pilot believes advanced avionics enable operations closer to personal or environmental limits.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: Automation in aircraft has proven

choices.text: to present new hazards in its limitations.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Automation은 안전성을 높이지만 동시에 오류를 숨기거나 complacency를 만들 수 있다. 사람은 신뢰도가 높은 자동시스템을 수동적으로 감시하는 데 취약하므로 automation이 situational awareness를 높이기도 하고 낮추기도 한다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: Most of the aviation community believes automation has made flying safer, but there is a fear that pilots fail to see that automation is a double-edged sword. Pilots need to understand the advantages of automation while being aware of its limitations. Experience has shown that automated systems can make some errors more evident while sometimes hiding other errors or making them less obvious. When passively monitoring an automated system for faults, abnormalities, or other infrequent events, humans perform poorly. The more reliable the system is, the worse the human performance becomes. It is a paradox of automation that technically advanced avionics can both increase and decrease pilot awareness. Answer (B) is incorrect. Automation is not necessarily flawless. Proper use of checklists and systematic training should be used to control common error-prone tasks and notice errors from automation before they become a threat to safety of flight. Answer (C) is incorrect. While automation has prevented accidents, it can also cause accidents from complacency. Therefore, it is not the best answer choice. When passively monitoring an automated system for faults, abnormalities, or other infrequent events, humans perform poorly. The more reliable the system is, the worse the human performance becomes. It is a paradox of automation that technically advanced avionics can both increase and decrease pilot awareness.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: A pilot’s attitude

choices.text: has no effect on aviation decisions.
has no effect on pilot perceptions.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Hazardous attitude를 인식하면 그것을 위험하다고 label한 뒤 대응 antidote를 적용해 올바른 행동으로 redirect해야 한다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: Hazardous attitudes contribute to poor pilot judgment but can be effectively counteracted by redirecting the hazardous attitude so that correct action can be taken. After recognition as hazardous, the pilot should label it as hazardous, then state the corresponding antidote. Answer (A) is incorrect. Attitude has an effect on every aviation decision, whether hazardous or not. Answer (C) is incorrect. After recognition as hazardous, the pilot should label it as hazardous, then state the corresponding antidote. If this does not happen, the results could be catastrophic. If a pilot does not perceive a hazardous attitude as hazardous and takes corrective action, the effects of that pilot’s aviation decisions will always be unsafe.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: When a pilot fixates on the original goal or destination is
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Get-there-itis는 원래 목표나 목적지에 집착해 다른 대안을 무시함으로써 조종사의 판단을 손상시키는 성향이다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: The definition of “get-there-itis” is the disposition that impairs pilot judgment through a fixation on the original goal or destination combined with a disregard for any alternative course of action. Answer (B) is incorrect. With get-there-itis, there is no thinking at all, analytical or other. It is “I have to get there, at this time, no matter what.” Answer (C) is incorrect. There is basically no decision-making process within “get-there-itis.”

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: The lighter workloads associated with glass (digital) flight instrumentation

choices.text: are instrumental in decreasing flightcrew fatigue.
have proven to increase safety in operations.
may lead to complacency by the flightcrew.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Glass cockpit의 automation과 높은 SA 기능은 안전성을 크게 높일 수 있지만 workload 감소가 complacency를 만들 수 있다. 사람은 자동시스템의 드문 오류를 감시하는 데 약하므로 고신뢰 automation일수록 적극적 monitoring이 중요하다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: The enhanced situational awareness and automation capabilities offered by a glass cockpit vastly expand its safety and utility, especially for personal transportation use. At the same time, there is some risk that lighter workloads could lead to complacency. Humans are characteristically poor monitors of automated systems. When passively monitoring an automated system for faults, abnormalities, or other infrequent events, humans perform poorly. The more reliable the system is, the worse the human performance becomes. It is a paradox of automation that technically advanced avionics can both increase and decrease pilot awareness. Answer (A) is incorrect. The introduction of automation is often intended to reduce workload and augment performance; however, this is not always the result. Automation can lead to distraction from the primary task, increased workload, boredom, or complacency. Answer (B) is incorrect. It is helpful to note that all human activity involving technical devices entails some element of risk. Knowledge, experience, and flight requirements tilt the odds in favor of safe and successful flights. The advanced avionics aircraft offers many new capabilities and simplifies the basic flying tasks, but only if the pilot is properly trained and all the equipment is working properly.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: Attitude is a motivational predisposition to

choices.text: respond to people, situations, or events in a given manner.
frame all circumstances in various predetermined scenarios.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Attitude는 특정 사람·상황·사건에 일정한 방식으로 반응하려는 동기적 성향이며 의사결정의 질에 직접 영향을 준다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: Attitude will affect the quality of decisions. Attitude is a motivational predisposition to respond to people, situations, or events in a given manner. Answer (B) is incorrect. In the real world, no scenarios are predetermined. The pilot must be able to recognize a hazardous attitude and apply the appropriate antidote no matter what the situation is. Answer (C) is incorrect. Whenever the need calls, the pilot must think through the situation and evaluate a decision to be made before making that decision. This is not always a quick process. Making a quick decision may lead to the wrong outcome.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: Not cross-checking the heading indicator with the runway for correct runway heading and alignment agreement is an example of
questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 목표·일정 압박은 안전에 악영향을 줄 수 있다. 예를 들어 시간을 아끼려고 runway heading과 실제 alignment를 확인하지 않으면 wrong-runway takeoff로 이어질 수 있다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: The pressure to meet goals can adversely affect safety. A pilot may rely on short-term memory rather than spend the additional time needed to confirm that runway heading and alignment are in agreement. Skipping this step may lead to taking off on the wrong runway. Answer (A) is incorrect. Even an experienced pilot that has trained to perform a task can become prey to operational pitfalls. Answer (B) is incorrect. If the departure runway heading is not close to what is indicated in the heading indicator, either it is the incorrect runway or a malfunction has occurred. This is not an example of an instrument interpretation problem.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: Experienced pilots, as compared to inexperienced pilots, are more likely to make automatic decisions which culminate in

choices.text: not being tempted by falling prey to one or more operational pitfalls.
the exercise of proper judgment and making correct decisions.
classic behavioral traps which lead to accidents and incidents.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 숙련된 조종사도 계획대로 비행을 끝내려는 강박, 승객 만족 욕구, 일정 압박, 'get the job done' 집착 같은 classic behavioral trap에 빠질 수 있다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: Classic behavioral traps that lead to accidents and incidents that experienced pilots may fall into are (1) the compulsion to complete a flight as planned, (2) the desire to please passengers, (3) the pressure to meet schedules, and (4) the determination to “get the job done.” Note that while this answer may not be perfect, it is the best of the three choices given. Answer (A) is incorrect. The classic behavioral traps are operational pitfalls that come with the development of pilot experience. Answer (B) is incorrect. Experienced pilots are more likely to make automatic decisions which culminate from classic behavioral traps to get the job done.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: Working 6 days in a row with 14 hours a day waiting, flying, waiting, flying, and waiting will leave you

choices.text: with a minor case of acute fatigue.
with a case of chronic fatigue.
well rested after an 8-hour rest period.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Acute fatigue는 단기간의 피로로, 과도한 활동·흥분·수면부족 뒤 흔히 느끼는 정상적인 일시적 피로이다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: Acute fatigue is short term and is a normal occurrence in everyday living. It is the kind of tiredness people feel after a period of strenuous effort, excitement, or lack of sleep. Answer (B) is incorrect. Chronic fatigue comes about over a long period of time and usually has psychological roots, although an underlying disease is sometimes responsible. Continuous high stress levels produce chronic fatigue. Answer (C) is incorrect. To assist in battling fatigue, 8 hours rest is needed daily.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: Flightcrew members must receive fatigue education and awareness training

choices.text: with all required air carrier dispatcher and every flightcrew member training activity.
annually for flightcrew member schedulers, operational control individuals and flightcrew members and dispatchers.
annually for flight crewmembers and every 24 months for dispatchers, flightcrew member schedulers, and operational control individuals.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Certificate holder는 flightcrew, dispatcher, scheduler, operational control 및 관련 관리자 등을 대상으로 Administrator 승인 fatigue education/awareness training을 매년 제공해야 한다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: Each certificate holder must develop and implement an education and awareness training program approved by the Administrator. This program must provide annual education and awareness training to all employees of the certificate holder responsible for administering the provisions of this rule, including flightcrew members, dispatchers, individuals directly involved in the scheduling of flightcrew members, individuals directly involved in operational control, and any employee providing direct management oversight of those areas. Answer (A) is incorrect. The training for specified personnel is required annually, not at every training event. Answer (C) is incorrect. This training is annual, not every 24 months.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: One of the most dangerous hazards in aviation is
questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. Acute fatigue가 있다면 비행하지 않는 것이 최선이다. Flight deck에서 피로가 발생하면 훈련이나 경험만으로 그 부정적 영향을 극복할 수 없다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: If suffering from acute fatigue, stay on the ground. If fatigue occurs on the flight deck, no amount of training or experience can overcome the detrimental effects. Answer (A) is incorrect. Hypoxic hypoxia can be resolved almost immediately by obtaining oxygen. Answer (C) is incorrect. Drugs are not the most dangerous hazard in aviation. Some drugs can safely be taken while piloting an aircraft.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: Checking your aircraft heading with runway alignment will help prevent

choices.text: taking off on the wrong runway.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 활주로에 진입한 뒤 aircraft heading과 runway alignment를 cross-check하면 wrong-runway takeoff를 예방하는 데 도움이 된다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: Once reaching and taking the runway, checking the aircraft heading against runway alignment will help prevent the pilot from taking off on the wrong runway. Answer (A) is incorrect. The only way to determine what taxiway a pilot is turning onto is by checking the taxiway identifier sign on the side of the runway just before the taxiway, then checking again once on the taxiway (using the taxiway identifier sign on the side of the taxiway after departing the runway). The heading indicator is irrelevant on a taxiway. Answer (B) is incorrect. The only way to determine what taxiway a pilot is on is by checking the taxiway identifier sign on the side of the taxiway. The heading indicator is irrelevant on a taxiway.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: Evidence proves

choices.text: more aviation accidents occur during landing and tend to be more deadly.
more aviation accidents occur during landing, but more fatal accidents occurring during takeoff.
takeoffs result in more aviation accidents, but fewer fatalities.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 사고의 약 40.3%가 landing 중 발생하지만 사망자의 약 3.7%를 차지한다. 반면 takeoff/climb 사고는 약 16.4%이지만 사망자의 약 14.4%를 차지한다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: Evidence shows that 40.3% of aviation accidents occur during landing, but they only account for 3.7% of fatalities. By comparison, takeoff/climb only accounts for 16.4% of aviation accidents but accounts for 14.4% of fatalities. Answer (A) is incorrect. Evidence shows that more aviation accidents occur during landing than during takeoff (40.3% compared to 16.4%, respectively) but takeoffs are more fatal, accounting for 14.4% of fatal aviation accidents compared to only 3.7% during landing. Answer (C) is incorrect. Evidence shows that takeoffs result in fewer aviation accidents than landing (16.4% compared to 40.3%, respectively) but takeoffs are more deadly, accounting for 14.4% of aviation accident fatalities compared to only 3.7% during landing.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: Chronic fatigue is
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Chronic fatigue는 장기간 지속되는 피로로 지속적 높은 stress와 심리적 원인이 흔하며 질병이 원인일 수도 있다. 의사의 치료가 필요하다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: Chronic fatigue is long-term fatigue. It usually has psychological roots, although an underlying disease is sometimes responsible. Continuous high stress levels produce chronic fatigue. This type of fatigue requires treatment by a physician. Answer (B) is incorrect. Short-term fatigue is known as acute fatigue and can be treated with 8 hours of sleep. Answer (C) is incorrect. Weekly fatigue is acute fatigue and requires 8 hours of sleep to cure.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: Risk is increased when the pilot becomes detached from the operation and

choices.text: does not use all of the automation features to the fullest extent.
fails to monitor the systems and check the results of processes.
depends on the other pilot to use automation only partially enabled or rarely.

questions.explanation: 정답은 B입니다. 시스템 monitoring과 결과 확인을 하지 않으면 조종사는 aircraft operation에서 분리되고 complacency에 빠져 risk가 증가한다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: Risk is increased when a pilot fails to monitor systems. By failing to monitor systems and failing to check the results of the processes, the pilot becomes detached from the aircraft operations and slides into the complacent role of passenger in command. Answer (A) is incorrect. It is not a risk to not use all the automation features to the fullest extent, but risk is increased when a pilot fails to monitor systems. Answer (C) is incorrect. Risk is not increased when the pilot depends on the other pilot to use automation only partially or rarely.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: An air carrier pilot takes off as ordered in the afternoon when embedded thunderstorms are indicated on radar and NOAA is broadcasting weather watches. This might be described as an example of
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Resignation attitude는 'What's the use?'처럼 자신이 결과에 영향을 줄 수 없다고 생각해 포기하는 태도이며, 불합리한 요구에도 순응할 수 있다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: Having a resigned attitude is saying or thinking, “What’s the use?” The pilot does not see himself or herself as being able to make a great deal of difference in what happens to himself or herself. (S)he “gives in.” Sometimes, such pilots will even go along with unreasonable requests just to be a “nice person.” Answer (B) is incorrect. A pilot exhibiting the anti-authority attitude is one who does not like to be told what to do or follow rules and who thinks (s)he is usually right. Answer (C) is incorrect. An impulsive attitude is shown by a pilot who does things on impulse. (S)he acts first and thinks last.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: The FAA believes safety is
questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. FAA는 항공안전 교육과 seminar를 제공하며, flight instructor는 학생과의 모든 비행에서 기본 안전관행과 절차를 일관되게 보여주어 올바른 습관을 형성해야 한다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: The FAA offers many courses and seminars to enhance air safety. The FAA puts the burden of instilling safe flying habits on the flight instructor, who should follow basic flight safety practices and procedures in every flight operation (s)he undertakes with a student pilot. Answer (B) is incorrect. Safety should be the core component of operations. Answer (C) is incorrect. Never automatically assume a crewmember is safe. Always be certain they are safe. Always check and cross-check what is being done during operations.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: Situational awareness is the

choices.text: perception and classification of any three of the fundamental risk elements.
visualization and characterization of the factors and conditions affecting the flight at that particular moment.
accurate perception and understanding of all factors and conditions within the five fundamental risk elements.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. Situational awareness는 비행 전·중·후 안전에 영향을 주는 기본 risk element의 모든 요인과 조건을 정확히 인지하고 이해하는 것이다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: Situational awareness is the accurate perception and understanding of all the factors and conditions within the five fundamental risk elements that affect safety before, during, and after the flight. Answer (A) is incorrect. There are five fundamental risk elements, not three. They are flight, pilot, aircraft, environment, and mission (type of operation). Answer (B) is incorrect. The pilot should visualize and characterize the factors and conditions affecting the flight before the moment, not at that particular moment.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: Fatigue is

choices.text: a physiological state of reduced mental or physical performance capability resulting from lack of sleep or increased physical activity that can reduce a flight crew member’s alertness and ability to safely operate an aircraft or perform safety-related duties.

a physiological state of reduced mental, physical, or emotional capability that results from lack of exercise, rest, or required nutrients that can reduce a crew member’s alertness to safely perform the required duties.

a physiological state of reduced mental or physical performance capability resulting from lack of REM sleep or decreased physical activity along with illness that impairs the crew member’s alertness and ability to safely operate an aircraft or perform safety-related duties.

questions.explanation: 정답은 A입니다. Fatigue는 수면부족이나 신체활동 증가 등으로 정신적·신체적 수행능력이 떨어져 승무원의 alertness와 안전운항 능력을 저하시키는 생리적 상태이다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: Fatigue is a physiological state of reduced mental or physical performance capability resulting from lack of sleep or increased physical activity that can reduce a flight crew member’s alertness and ability to safely operate an aircraft or perform safety-related duties. Answer (B) is incorrect. The definition of fatigue does not address nutrition; however, it is quite important for any crew member to live a healthy lifestyle. Answer (C) is incorrect. The definition of fatigue addresses all sleep, not specifically REM sleep, generic illnesses, or a reduction of physical activity.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

subunit.title: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)

questions.question: The first step in good decision-making is

choices.text: learning how to recognize and cope with stress.
identifying personal attitudes hazardous to safe flight.

questions.explanation: 정답은 C입니다. 좋은 의사결정의 첫 단계는 안전비행에 위험한 자신의 hazardous attitude를 인식·식별하는 것이다.
tags: Human Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
questions.explanation_en: The first step in good decision-making is to recognize or identify personal attitudes hazardous to safe flight. Answer (A) is incorrect. Learning behavior modification techniques is the second step in good decision-making. Answer (B) is incorrect. Learning how to recognize and cope with stress is the third step in good decision-making.

questions.subject: ATP Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Aeromedical Factors and Aeronautical Decision Making (ADM)
